articles.title: Two Italian technicians killed in drone attack in Kuwait; Iran denies involvement
articles.summary:
Two Italian technicians working for Rheinmetall Italia were killed in a drone attack on a facility in Kuwait on Thursday, according to Kuwait's defence ministry and Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani. Tajani said the drones were Iranian and struck an air-defence surveillance station, injuring two others, a Pakistani national and a Kuwaiti army officer.

Iran's armed forces spokesman denied any Iranian attack and suggested it may have been a false-flag operation, AAP reported. Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi also denied involvement and offered Kuwait a joint investigation. Tajani said Italy would lodge a complaint with the Iranian embassy in Rome.
keyFacts: Kuwait's defence ministry blamed Iran for the attack on a 'vital facility'
Italy says two others were injured, a Pakistani and a Kuwaiti officer
Iran denies responsibility and has offered a joint investigation

articles.title: Trump calls on Putin to pull back military aggression in Europe and make a quick deal
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that he wanted Russian President Vladimir Putin to pull back all military aggression against territories in Europe and to reach a deal quickly, the ABC reported. A day earlier, Trump and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte issued a joint statement after talks at Mar-a-Lago urging Russia to avoid actions that expand the war, according to AFP.

US mediator Jared Kushner said talks had reached a partial deadlock over Ukrainian territory, and said Putin had agreed not to use nuclear weapons, the ABC reported. Ukraine's air force said Russia launched ballistic missiles and 113 drones overnight on Wednesday.
keyFacts: Trump made the call in a Truth Social post
Trump and Rutte jointly urged Russia not to widen the war
Kushner said territory remains the main sticking point in talks

articles.title: Eurozone nominates Pablo Hernández de Cos to succeed Lagarde as ECB president
articles.summary:
Eurozone governments agreed to recommend Spanish economist Pablo Hernández de Cos as the next president of the European Central Bank, European Council President António Costa said on Thursday, according to Al Jazeera. Hernández de Cos, 55, currently heads the Bank for International Settlements and is a former governor of the Bank of Spain.

He is due to take over in February from Christine Lagarde, who is leaving before her term ends in October next year. Costa said Laurence Boone and Markus Brunnermeier were also recommended for the ECB executive board. The ECB governing council and the European Parliament must still give their formal backing.
keyFacts: Hernández de Cos currently heads the Bank for International Settlements
He is due to replace Christine Lagarde in February
The nomination still needs ECB and European Parliament backing

articles.title: Australia enacts Antarctic logistics agreement with China as Beijing plans ice runway
articles.summary:
The Australian Antarctic Division has a logistics agreement with China's polar research institute for the 2026-27 season, the ABC reported, citing a Senate estimates brief released under freedom of information. The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade told the ABC the agreement had been enacted, but gave no details of its terms.

China is seeking approval to build a blue-ice runway in the Grove Mountains, inside the Australian Antarctic Territory, according to an environmental evaluation lodged with the Antarctic Treaty system. It proposes up to eight flights a year from about 2029-30. A DFAT spokesperson said all parties must comply with the Antarctic Treaty.
keyFacts: The agreement covers the 2026-27 Antarctic season
China's proposed runway would allow up to eight flights a year
Defence and DFAT refused FOI requests on Chinese icebreaker port visits

articles.title: Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv shopping centre and two other buildings, mayor says
articles.summary:
Russian ballistic missiles struck a shopping centre and two other buildings on the eastern side of Kyiv late on Wednesday, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said, according to Reuters. Klitschko told residents to stay in shelters while the attack continued, and said one building was badly damaged.

Klitschko initially reported three people wounded and later said four were hurt, two seriously, Reuters reported. Russia's defence ministry said on Thursday its forces had hit military-industrial facilities in Kyiv, according to Interfax as cited by Al Jazeera. Ukraine and Russia both deny targeting civilians.
keyFacts: The strikes hit Kyiv's east bank late on Wednesday
Four people were wounded, two seriously, Klitschko said
Russia said it targeted military-industrial sites

articles.title: Ukraine says strike on Russia's Savasleyka airbase damaged five military aircraft
articles.summary:
Ukraine's General Staff said on Wednesday it had struck the Savasleyka airbase in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region, east of Moscow, damaging five aircraft, Al Jazeera reported. It said three MiG-31 jets, used to launch hypersonic missiles, and two Su-34 fighter-bombers were hit.

Russia did not immediately comment on the claim. Ukrainian Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara said this week that Ukraine had struck 16 ballistic missile launchers over several months, according to Al Jazeera. The claimed strike follows Ukrainian attacks on Russian ships off Libya.
keyFacts: The airbase is in the Nizhny Novgorod region
Ukraine says three MiG-31s and two Su-34s were damaged
Russia had not commented on the claim

articles.title: Putin says Russian response to Ukrainian refinery attacks is inevitable
articles.summary:
Russian President Vladimir Putin said Russia would inevitably respond to continuing Ukrainian drone attacks on its oil refineries, speaking at a Kremlin meeting with officials and oil executives, AAP reported. Putin said Kyiv was continuing the attacks despite an appeal from the US president.

Ukraine has said it will stop striking Russian energy sites only when Russia does the same. Two industry sources estimated the attacks have cut combined Russian refinery processing by 45 per cent since late October, according to AAP. Several Russian regions have limited retail fuel sales, and Putin said petrol prices had stabilised after peaking in October.
keyFacts: Putin said 'retaliatory measures' were inevitable
Industry sources say refinery processing has fallen about 45%
Some Russian regions have restricted retail fuel sales

articles.title: Russian-installed governor says Ukrainian drone killed five in occupied Zaporizhzhia
articles.summary:
A drone attack on a car park in the village of Vesioloye in the Russian-occupied part of Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region killed five people and wounded three, the Moscow-installed governor Yevgeny Balitsky said on Telegram on Thursday, according to Al Jazeera. He blamed Ukraine for the attack.

Ukraine did not comment on the claim in Al Jazeera's report, and the casualty figures have not been independently verified. The report came hours after Russian missiles struck Kyiv and as Ukraine's energy capacity was reported to be below 40 per cent of pre-war levels.
keyFacts: Five people were killed and three wounded, the governor said
The attack hit a car park in Vesioloye
The claim has not been independently verified

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says it downed missiles over Riyadh; projectile lands at Jazan port
articles.summary:
The Saudi-led coalition said its air defences destroyed two ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh and two drones over the Eastern Province, The National reported. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said a cruise missile aimed at the western region and a drone near Jeddah port were also intercepted, while a projectile fell at Jazan port, causing minor damage and no civilian casualties.

The Houthis said they targeted Jeddah and Jazan ports in retaliation for coalition strikes on Hodeidah. There was no immediate confirmation that Jeddah was hit. The coalition later said the Houthis attacked the Jazan refinery and warned of a firm military response, the ABC reported.
keyFacts: Two ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh were destroyed, the coalition said
A projectile caused minor damage at Jazan port
The Houthis described the attacks as retaliation for Hodeidah strikes

articles.title: Bank of Korea raises cash rate to 3.25% and lifts growth forecasts
articles.summary:
South Korea's central bank raised its key interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to 3.25 per cent on Thursday, citing strong domestic growth and inflation above its target, Al Jazeera reported. Annual inflation was 2.8 per cent in October, compared with the bank's 2 per cent target.

The Bank of Korea raised its growth forecast to 3.9 per cent for 2026 and 4.1 per cent for 2027, up from 3.3 and 2.9 per cent in August. Third-quarter GDP rose 3.4 per cent year on year, while October exports rose 94 per cent, with semiconductors making up nearly half, according to Al Jazeera.
keyFacts: The key rate rose 0.25 points to 3.25%
October inflation was 2.8%, above the 2% target
The 2026 growth forecast was raised to 3.9%

articles.title: Trump calls pre-election GDP figures fake after upward revision to 4.3% growth
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump said on Truth Social that economic figures released before the November midterm elections were fake and called for an immediate investigation, Al Jazeera reported. He did not provide evidence.

On Wednesday, the Bureau of Economic Analysis revised third-quarter annualised growth up to 4.3 per cent from its advance estimate of 3.4 per cent, released on October 29. The BEA did not respond to Al Jazeera's request for comment; it has previously said advance estimates change because they are based on incomplete source data. Republicans lost ground in the November 3 midterms.
keyFacts: Q3 growth was revised to 4.3% from 3.4%
Trump called for an investigation without providing evidence
The BEA says advance estimates rely on incomplete data

articles.title: US Federal Reserve survey reports slight to moderate growth and sticky inflation
articles.summary:
The US Federal Reserve's Beige Book survey, released on Wednesday, found economic activity grew at a slight to moderate pace across most of the country, with employment rising and prices increasing moderately, Reuters reported. Business contacts cited cost pressures from energy, transport, healthcare, insurance and tariffs.

Contacts said input costs were rising faster than the prices they could charge because customers were sensitive to price increases. Commerce Department data showed the PCE price index rose 3.8 per cent in the year to October, with the core measure up 3.3 per cent. Reuters said the Fed is broadly expected to raise rates at its December 8-9 meeting.
keyFacts: Most of the Fed's 12 districts reported growth
Annual PCE inflation was 3.8% in October
The Fed's next decision is due on December 8-9

articles.title: US judge blocks FCC hearing on licences of eight Disney-owned ABC stations
articles.summary:
US District Judge Loren AliKhan granted Disney a preliminary injunction on Wednesday stopping the Federal Communications Commission from holding a hearing on the licences of eight ABC-owned television stations, Al Jazeera reported. In her ruling, she wrote that FCC Chair Brendan Carr had followed President Trump's rhetoric.

Carr ordered early licence reviews in April, a day after Trump urged ABC to fire host Jimmy Kimmel; the licences were not due for renewal until at least 2028. An FCC spokesperson said the ruling was wrong on the facts and the law. ABC News called it a victory for the First Amendment.
keyFacts: The injunction covers eight ABC-owned stations
The FCC ordered early licence reviews in April
The FCC says the ruling is wrong on facts and law

articles.title: US judge strikes down Trump's August birthright citizenship restrictions
articles.summary:
US District Judge Christopher Cooper ruled on Wednesday that children affected by President Donald Trump's August executive orders on birthright citizenship are under US jurisdiction and entitled to citizenship under the Constitution, Al Jazeera reported. A Maryland court had already blocked the same policy with a preliminary injunction in September.

The case was brought by rights groups on behalf of affected children. ACLU lawyer Cody Wofsy said the president needed to accept the law. White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis described it as a ruling from an activist judge. The Supreme Court struck down Trump's original order in June.
keyFacts: The ruling concerns executive orders issued in August
A Maryland court blocked the policy in September
The White House criticised the decision

articles.title: Guinea-Bissau's military-led government delays elections by two years to 2028
articles.summary:
Guinea-Bissau's transitional president, Major General Horta Inta-a, issued a decree on Thursday moving presidential and legislative elections planned for December 6 to November 2028, Al Jazeera reported. The decree cited insufficient technical, material and financial conditions for holding the vote.

The army seized power last November, removing President Umaro Sissoco Embaló, who was seeking another term. The transitional charter bars Inta-a from standing. West African bloc ECOWAS has called for a short and transparent transition back to civilian rule, according to Al Jazeera.
keyFacts: Elections were due on December 6
The new date is November 2028
The military took power in November last year

articles.title: Jordan's parliament sends tougher anti-terrorism amendments to committee
articles.summary:
Jordan's House of Representatives voted on Wednesday to refer draft amendments to the 2006 Anti-Terrorism Law to its legal committee, Al Jazeera reported. According to the state-run Jordan News Agency, the changes would raise minimum prison terms to 10 years, and up to 15 in some cases, while keeping the death penalty for the most serious offences.

The bill follows an October 23 attack on a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate. First Deputy Speaker Ayatollah Freihat urged the government to withdraw the draft, criticising vague terms. Speaker Ibrahim Tarawneh said the chamber would review the legislation.
keyFacts: Minimum sentences would rise to 10 years
The bill goes to committee, then the Senate
It follows the October 23 church attack

articles.title: French forces seize more than three tonnes of methamphetamine near French Polynesia
articles.summary:
French armed forces boarded an unflagged oil tanker outside French Polynesia's maritime zone and found 150 bales of methamphetamine weighing 3.328 tonnes, according to a statement from French Pacific command reported by the ABC. A US Coast Guard patrol aircraft assisted in tracking the vessel.

The drugs were taken to Tahiti to be destroyed, and the crew and vessel were released, the ABC reported. French seizures in the region this year now exceed 15 tonnes. University of Canterbury academic José Sousa-Santos told the ABC the seizure suggested traffickers were shifting towards methamphetamine for Australian and New Zealand markets.
keyFacts: The seizure weighed 3.328 tonnes
French seizures in the region exceed 15 tonnes this year
The US Coast Guard assisted the operation

articles.title: Global shares rise as tech stocks recover; Wall Street shut for Thanksgiving
articles.summary:
Share markets in Asia and Europe rose on Thursday as technology stocks recovered, while US markets were closed for Thanksgiving, AP reported. Japan's Nikkei 225 closed 0.9 per cent higher and Australia's S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.8 per cent to 8,763.80. Germany's DAX was up 1.9 per cent in early trading.

Brent crude rose to about $US91 a barrel, according to AP. On Wednesday, Nvidia shares fell 3.9 per cent after S&P Global Ratings warned of a possible downgrade over governance. US markets reopen on Friday for a shortened session.
keyFacts: The ASX 200 rose 0.8% to 8,763.80
Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 0.9%
US markets reopen Friday for a shortened session

articles.title: Florida attorney-general seeks to revoke doctor's licence over alleged illegal abortions
articles.summary:
Florida Attorney-General James Uthmeier asked the state Board of Medicine to revoke the licence of Dr Sylvester Braithwaite, saying state health officials found he performed at least 149 illegal abortions in North Miami Beach between June 2024 and September 2026, WKMG reported. Surgeon General Joseph Ladapo issued an emergency order restricting his licence so he cannot perform elective abortions.

The order alleges more than 50 elective abortions after six weeks between June and September 2026. Florida generally bars abortions after six weeks, with limited exceptions. The allegations have not been tested before the board, and WKMG's report did not include a response from Dr Braithwaite.
keyFacts: The attorney-general alleges at least 149 illegal abortions
An emergency order restricts the doctor's licence
The Board of Medicine has yet to consider the case

articles.title: Carney says Trump has not raised Pentagon criticism of Canada's defence spending
articles.summary:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Wednesday that US President Donald Trump had not raised the Pentagon's concerns about Canada's military in their talks, according to CBC News and The Globe and Mail. The comments followed public criticism from the Pentagon of Canada's defence spending and military readiness.

Carney pointed to Canada's NATO deployment in Latvia, Arctic cooperation and recent defence investment, Canadian media reported. Canadian ministers responded that Canada is a sovereign nation, while acknowledging readiness shortfalls and promising faster recruitment.
keyFacts: Carney said the issue had not come up with Trump
The Pentagon criticised Canada's defence spending this week
Carney cited Canada's NATO deployment in Latvia

articles.title: Victorian Electoral Commission says it cannot stop filming outside voting centres
articles.summary:
The Victorian Electoral Commission said it has no power to stop filming in public areas outside voting centres, after Nationals MP Emma Kealy raised concerns about a One Nation volunteer wearing smart glasses outside the Horsham early voting centre, the ABC reported. Recording devices are banned for scrutineers inside voting centres and during counting.

One Nation candidate Andrew Partridge confirmed the volunteer wore the glasses and said they were used to take photos for social media, without recording audio. The VEC separately said ballot papers were not accessed after a security breach closed the Horsham centre for an hour on Tuesday.
keyFacts: The VEC says filming in public outside centres is not prohibited
One Nation says the glasses were used only for photos
Victoria votes on Saturday

articles.title: Annual climate statement shows emissions fell 1.3%, short of pace for 2035 target
articles.summary:
Australia's greenhouse gas emissions fell by 6.2 million tonnes, or 1.3 per cent, in the year to June 2026, according to the federal government's annual climate change statement released on Thursday. The ABC reported the fall was smaller than in the previous two reporting periods.

Xinhua reported the statement projects emissions on current trends at 42 per cent below 2005 levels in 2030 and 48 per cent in 2035, against targets of 43 per cent and 62 to 70 per cent. Climate Change Authority chair Matt Kean said annual cuts of 25 to 30 million tonnes are needed. Climate Minister Chris Bowen wrote that the recent rate of reduction was faster than the decade average.
keyFacts: Emissions fell 6.2 million tonnes in the year to June 2026
The 2035 target is a 62–70% cut on 2005 levels
Renewables supplied a record 45.9% of the main power grid, the ABC said

articles.title: Victorian Coalition costings include leasing sewage plants and axing crossing removals
articles.summary:
Victoria's Coalition released its election costings on Thursday, two days before Saturday's state election, the ABC reported. The Parliamentary Budget Office said the policies would reduce net debt by $20 billion over four years, to $176 billion.

The plan includes leasing Melbourne Water's Eastern and Western treatment plants, which the costings say would raise $13.63 billion by 2030-31 including land sales. Level crossing removals at Yarraville, Spotswood and on the Upfield line would be cancelled, and free kindergarten would stay at 15 hours a week. Opposition Leader Jess Wilson set a surplus target for 2032-33. Labor Treasurer Colin Brooks and Greens leader Ellen Sandell both criticised the plans.
keyFacts: PBO says the policies cut net debt by $20 billion over four years
Sewage plant leases would raise $13.63 billion by 2030-31
More than 1.6 million Victorians had already voted, the ABC said

articles.title: Queensland Ambulance Service commissioner to leave after deaths linked to delays
articles.summary:
Queensland Ambulance Service Commissioner Craig Emery will retire, Health Minister Tim Nicholls announced on Thursday, the ABC reported. Emery's five-year contract was due to end in February, and he will finish on 31 December after a period of leave. Deputy commissioner David Hartley will act in the role.

The ABC reported seven patients have died while waiting for ambulances in Queensland since late June. Nicholls said it was Emery's decision and denied he had been pushed out. United Workers Union Queensland's Fiona Scalon described Emery as a "scapegoat". Opposition Leader Steven Miles said the underlying cause was bed block in hospitals.
keyFacts: Emery finishes on 31 December
Seven patients have died waiting for ambulances since late June, the ABC said
David Hartley will be acting commissioner

articles.title: NT Police investigate emailed threat against ministers over child protection laws
articles.summary:
Northern Territory Police are investigating an encrypted email sent early on Thursday that threatened violence, including at public places in Darwin, unless the territory's new child protection laws are scrapped, according to AAP and the ABC. Chief Minister Lia Finocchiaro said it was sent at 4.16am to ministerial and electorate offices, government media units, the clerk and the ombudsman.

Assistant Commissioner Sonia Kennon said police were treating the threat as credible until assessed, while noting many such threats are hoaxes, AAP reported. Police were also checking reports of similar emails in other jurisdictions. Finocchiaro called the email disturbing, and Opposition Leader Selena Uibo condemned threats of violence.
keyFacts: The email was sent at 4.16am on Thursday
Anti-terrorism units are assessing its credibility, police said
The sender has not been identified

articles.title: Bureau of Meteorology forecasts above-average summer temperatures for nearly all Australia
articles.summary:
The Bureau of Meteorology expects above-average temperatures across almost all of Australia this summer as an El Niño strengthens, the ABC reported on Thursday. Bureau climatologist Qian Zhou said there is a higher chance of unusually high maximum temperatures nationwide, except a small area near Exmouth in WA.

The outlook shows below-average rainfall likely in Tasmania and coastal parts of the Kimberley and Pilbara, and possible extreme rainfall in southern Queensland and north-eastern NSW, particularly in December. The bureau said October was the warmest October on record for global sea surface temperatures. Royal Australian College of GPs president Ramya Raman said extreme heat can cause significant public health problems.
keyFacts: Above-average temperatures are forecast for almost all of Australia
An El Niño is strengthening, the bureau says
October set a record for global sea surface temperatures

articles.title: Federal regulator clears $32 billion Queensland data centre from further assessment
articles.summary:
The National Environmental Protection Agency has decided the $32 billion Western Downs Digital Park near Dalby in Queensland does not need further federal environmental assessment, the ABC reported on Thursday. The agency found the project unlikely to have a significant impact on matters of national environmental significance.

Anthropic signed an agreement in September to use the site and hoped to begin operations in 2027. Developer Zerra DC welcomed the decision, which the ABC said took about two months. The project still needs council and state approvals. A Climate Council report has said the site could become a major emissions source without renewable power, and local group Western Downs Says Pause said the project was being fast-tracked.
keyFacts: The project is valued at $32 billion
Council and state approvals are still required
Anthropic aims to begin using the site in 2027

articles.title: Flinders Island bushfire burns about 10% of island; up to six homes damaged or destroyed
articles.summary:
A bushfire on Tasmania's Flinders Island had burned about 13,000 hectares by Thursday after a wind change pushed it south-west, according to the Tasmania Fire Service. This updates earlier reports of emergency warnings on the island.

TFS deputy regional chief Steve Richardson told ABC radio that up to six homes had been damaged or destroyed, though crews had not been able to safely assess them, AAP reported via SBS. Residents near Killiecrankie were told around 10am it was too late to leave. Power lines are down on several roads and some communication towers are running on backup generators, the ABC said. The fire is suspected to have been started by lightning.
keyFacts: About 13,000 hectares have burned
Up to six homes damaged or destroyed, not yet assessed
An evacuation centre is operating at Whitemark

articles.title: Court gives David Jones administrators three more months to find a buyer
articles.summary:
The NSW Supreme Court has extended the administration of department store chain David Jones, giving administrator McGrathNicol more time to complete a sale, AAP reported on Thursday. A second creditors' meeting has been set for 3 March. McGrathNicol's lawyer had described the extension as modest.

AAP reported David Jones owes $155 million to Hilco and about $81 million to owner Anchorage Capital, and that more than 140 parties have contacted the administrators. Eighteen Australian stores and one in New Zealand are due to close by the end of the year, and almost 1,700 of about 6,000 staff have been made redundant. Chief executive Erica Berchtold told 2GB she expected the business to survive.
keyFacts: Second creditors' meeting set for 3 March
19 stores are closing by year end
Almost 1,700 staff have been made redundant, AAP says

articles.title: Harvey Norman says pre-tax profit fell 47% in first four months as sales drop
articles.summary:
Harvey Norman's pre-tax profit fell 47 per cent in the first four months of the financial year, and same-store sales at its 195 Australian franchises fell 3.7 per cent to the end of October, AAP reported after the retailer's annual meeting on Wednesday.

Same-store sales were down 1.6 per cent in the first 20 days of November. Executive chairman Gerry Harvey told AAP he expected 2027 to be very difficult, named inflation as his biggest concern and said he believed a recession was unavoidable. He said the half-year profit fall would be smaller than 47 per cent. Shares fell 2.8 per cent to $4.13, AAP said.
keyFacts: Pre-tax profit down 47% in the four months to October
Australian same-store sales down 3.7%
Shares fell 2.8% to $4.13

articles.title: Chalmers says Suncorp whistleblower claims are serious and expects regulator scrutiny
articles.summary:
Treasurer Jim Chalmers said allegations about insurer Suncorp's handling of home insurance claims were serious and that he expected the regulator to examine them closely, the ABC reported on Thursday. The allegations were aired by a former employee on the ABC's 7.30 program on Tuesday.

The whistleblower alleged Suncorp rewarded staff for denying or reducing claims and that its culture put profit ahead of customers. APRA said it took the concerns seriously, and the Australian Consumers Insurance Lobby called for ASIC to intervene. The Insurance Council declined to comment. The ABC's reports did not include a response from Suncorp.
keyFacts: The allegations were broadcast on 7.30 on Tuesday
APRA says it takes the concerns seriously
A consumer group has called for ASIC intervention

articles.title: Virgin Australia airport workers strike at four major airports over pay and shifts
articles.summary:
Virgin Australia airport workers held short strikes on Thursday at Adelaide, Brisbane, Melbourne and Sydney airports, the Australian Services Union said, according to the ABC. Stoppages ran for two to three hours in the morning and afternoon at the different airports.

The union said the dispute concerns pay and being required to work nine-hour shifts at single rates, and warned of delays and cancellations. ASU assistant national secretary Scott Cowen said Virgin could end the action with a fair offer. Virgin said it had contingency plans and did not expect passengers to be affected, and that it remained committed to working with unions.
keyFacts: Strikes affect Adelaide, Brisbane, Melbourne and Sydney
The ASU says nine-hour shifts at single rates are in dispute
Virgin says it has contingency plans in place

articles.title: Tasmania's upper house rejects greyhound racing ban; government says phase-out continues
articles.summary:
Tasmania's Legislative Council voted six to eight on Wednesday against a bill to formally ban greyhound racing, the ABC reported. The bill, which had passed the lower house, would have ended the industry by June 2029 and immediately banned breeding for racing and non-medical euthanasia of racing dogs. Labor and six independents voted against it.

Racing Minister Roger Jaensch said the phase-out would proceed without legislative protections, and Premier Jeremy Rockliff said taxpayer funding would end from 2029. The Welfare Alliance for Greyhounds described the outcome as "perverse", while RSPCA Tasmania said the industry should not treat it as a reprieve.
keyFacts: The bill was defeated six votes to eight
It would have ended racing by June 2029
The government says public funding ends from 2029

articles.title: Fire after crash on Cairo ring road kills at least 30, Egypt's health ministry says
articles.summary:
At least 30 people were killed on Wednesday when a fire broke out on Cairo's Ring Road in the Warraq area, Egypt's health ministry said, according to AP. The ABC's version of the AP report said the fire followed a fuel tanker crash and that more than two dozen cars and motorcycles were burned.

Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said the toll was preliminary. Reports of the number injured differed between versions of the AP story, at 15 and 25. The public prosecutor's office said DNA testing was under way to identify victims. President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi offered condolences.
keyFacts: At least 30 people were killed
The death toll is preliminary, the health minister said
DNA testing is being used to identify victims

articles.title: UK maritime agency reports projectile explosion near tanker 50 nautical miles off Dubai
articles.summary:
The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said a tanker's captain reported an explosion caused by an unidentified projectile about 50 nautical miles west of Dubai early on Thursday local time, according to Anadolu Agency and Middle East Eye.

UKMTO said all crew were safe and accounted for, and there was no damage to the vessel or environmental impact. The agency classed the incident as suspicious activity and advised ships to proceed with caution. No group had claimed responsibility in the reports. The incident follows a series of attacks on Gulf shipping and Saudi infrastructure linked to the Iran conflict.
keyFacts: The explosion was about 50 nautical miles west of Dubai
No damage or injuries were reported
UKMTO advised vessels to proceed with caution

articles.title: Palestinian media say Israeli strike killed Hamas deputy education minister and his wife
articles.summary:
Palestinian media reported that an overnight Israeli strike on an apartment building in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza killed Khaled Abu Nada, deputy education minister in the Hamas-run government, and his wife, The Times of Israel reported on Thursday.

The Israeli military said it had struck a senior Hamas operative and would release more details later. The reports said two people were killed. The strike follows Israeli strikes earlier this week that Israeli and Palestinian officials said killed senior Hamas internal security figures.
keyFacts: The strike hit an apartment building in Deir al-Balah
Palestinian media named the official as Khaled Abu Nada
The IDF said it targeted a senior Hamas operative

articles.title: Poland plans no-fly zone along its border with Ukraine from around January
articles.summary:
Poland's deputy defence minister Cezary Tomczyk said a decree would create a no-fly zone in eastern Poland extending between a dozen and several dozen kilometres from the Ukrainian border, Ukrainska Pravda reported on Wednesday, citing Polish outlet Interia.

The aim is for the decree to take effect at the end of December or start of January. The report linked the plan to debris from Russian Kh-101 missiles found in three places in Poland after a 20 November attack on Ukraine, and a drone that entered Polish airspace overnight on 23–24 November. The Kyiv Independent reported Poland has also asked NATO to intercept Russian missiles over Ukraine.
keyFacts: The zone would extend up to several dozen kilometres from the border
Target start is late December or early January
Russian missile debris was found in three Polish locations

articles.title: Karachi building collapse kills three; police arrest four as families report 17 missing
articles.summary:
A six-storey building under construction collapsed in Karachi's KECHS area near Baloch Colony on Wednesday, killing at least three people and injuring 14, Dawn reported, citing rescue officials. Karachi mayor Murtaza Wahab said building authorities had planned to demolish the structure but a court stay order had prevented it.

Police arrested four suspects on Thursday and registered a case naming more than 10 people, including the landowner, builder and engineers, Aaj News reported. Families have reported 17 people missing. Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah ordered a review of possible negligence, and President Asif Ali Zardari called for a full investigation.
keyFacts: At least three dead and 14 injured
Four suspects arrested; 17 people reported missing
A court stay had blocked a planned demolition, the mayor said

articles.title: Death toll in flooded West Java gold mine rises to 13, with 13 still missing
articles.summary:
Thirteen workers have died and 13 remain missing after a river overflowed and flooded an unlicensed gold mine in West Java, Indonesia, AFP reported on Thursday, citing search and rescue chief Desiana Kartika Bahari. Earlier reports said 26 workers were trapped.

West Java police spokesman Hendra Rochmawan said 11 miners escaped before the shafts flooded after heavy rain on Monday, and that authorities were not alerted until Tuesday. The shaft is about 100 metres deep, according to AFP. The search for the missing workers resumed on Thursday.
keyFacts: 13 confirmed dead and 13 missing
11 miners escaped before flooding, police said
Authorities were alerted a day after the flood

articles.title: Vance says Nvidia's Huang is not under investigation and does not need a pardon
articles.summary:
US Vice President JD Vance said on Wednesday that the Justice Department and national security officials told him Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang was not under investigation, CBS News reported. Vance said Huang did not need a pardon and that reinstating him was ultimately the board's decision.

Nvidia's board reinstated Huang on Monday after he resigned earlier this month, the ABC reported. President Donald Trump told the New York Post a pardon was "always an option" but probably unnecessary. Attorney-General Todd Blanche said there was no evidence Huang broke any law. Huang is due to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on 1 December.
keyFacts: Vance said he was told Huang is not under investigation
Huang was reinstated as CEO on Monday
Huang is due before a Senate committee on 1 December

articles.title: ESA's Hera images show large crater left on asteroid Dimorphos by NASA's DART impact
articles.summary:
New images from the European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft show a stadium-sized crater on the asteroid Dimorphos, left by NASA's deliberate DART collision in 2022, the ABC reported, citing Reuters and ESA.

Hera mission scientist Michael Küppers said the side hit by DART is now completely covered by a crater, while the opposite side showed no major change. He said Dimorphos is now tumbling chaotically and that there are hundreds of boulders in the system. Dimorphos is about 151 metres wide and orbits the larger asteroid Didymos; neither poses a threat to Earth. Hera is due to move within 13 kilometres next month.
keyFacts: DART struck Dimorphos in 2022 to test asteroid deflection
Dimorphos is about 151 metres wide
Hera will approach within 13 km next month

articles.title: SA Liberal senator Leah Blyth quits shadow ministry to join One Nation
articles.summary:
South Australian Liberal senator Leah Blyth has left the Coalition front bench and joined One Nation, AAP and the ABC reported on Thursday morning. She had been the opposition's defence infrastructure spokeswoman and is a former SA Liberal Party president.

Blyth said she had lost confidence in the opposition's ability to deal with immigration, spending and energy, and that she could no longer tell voters the Liberal Party could "save this country", according to the ABC. The ABC reported it was understood she was unlikely to receive a winnable Senate spot at the next election. AAP said the move would give One Nation five Senate seats. AAP's report did not include a response from Opposition Leader Angus Taylor.
keyFacts: Blyth was the Coalition's defence infrastructure spokeswoman
She becomes One Nation's first South Australian senator, the ABC says
AAP says One Nation will hold five Senate seats

articles.title: US formally proposes new tariffs on 14 economies, including 20% extra on China
articles.summary:
The US Trade Representative has proposed new tariffs on 14 trading partners after completing an eight-month Section 301 investigation into what it calls structural excess industrial capacity, Reuters reported. The step follows reports earlier this week that a proposal was expected; the final list covers China, the EU, India, Japan, South Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan and seven others.

A senior US official said China would face a proposed extra 20 per cent, and that duties would not exceed caps in existing trade deals, Reuters reported. Officials said a comment period and hearing would follow, which could delay implementation to January. The ABC reported Australia is not among the countries affected. China has rejected the accusations, RTÉ reported.
keyFacts: Section 301 probe covered 16 partners; 14 face proposed tariffs
China faces a proposed extra 20%, officials say
ABC reports Australia is not affected

articles.title: Wall Street falls sharply as AI shares, inflation data and tariff plans weigh
articles.summary:
US shares fell heavily on Wednesday, the last full session before Thanksgiving. By late morning in New York the Nasdaq Composite was down about 3.8 per cent and the S&P 500 about 2.5 per cent, Reuters reported, with Nvidia down more than 8 per cent and the Philadelphia semiconductor index down 7.3 per cent.

AP reported that data released on Wednesday showed the PCE price index rose 3.8 per cent in the year to October, up from 3.6 per cent, while third-quarter growth was revised up to a 4.3 per cent annual rate. Reuters said the newly proposed US tariffs added to selling, and that the Nasdaq 100 briefly fell 20 per cent below its record close.
keyFacts: Nasdaq down about 3.8% by late morning, Reuters says
US PCE inflation 3.8% in October, AP reports
Nvidia fell more than 8% after Monday's rebound

articles.title: US Army detonates nearly five tonnes of lead azide at Iowa ammunition plant
articles.summary:
The US Army carried out a controlled detonation of about five tons of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown on Wednesday morning, Iowa Public Radio and AP reported. The blast followed several delays and legal challenges by environmental groups, after a federal appeals court allowed it to proceed.

An Army general said surveillance showed all barrels had been removed. FEMA's administrator cited preliminary EPA data showing no detectable lead in the air, Iowa Public Radio reported. AP said the EPA took more than 1,200 samples beforehand and that residents within 20 miles were told to shelter in place. Governor-elect Rob Sand called for transparency, and Iowa's senators sought clearer information.
keyFacts: About five tons, in 68 barrels, detonated on 25 November (US time)
EPA preliminary data showed no detectable airborne lead, FEMA says
Residents within 20 miles told to shelter in place

articles.title: US regulator authorises SpaceX to deploy up to one million data centre satellites
articles.summary:
The US Federal Communications Commission has authorised SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites designed as orbital data centres, CNBC and the Lynnwood Times reported. SpaceX applied in January for the system, which it calls Starmind, to provide solar-powered computing in orbit.

The Lynnwood Times reported FCC chairman Brendan Carr said the agency was granting such an authorisation for the first time. According to the paper, the order requires the first satellite to be launched by November 2033 and the full constellation by 2040, or the licence lapses, and SpaceX must provide debris-mitigation details before operating above 600 kilometres. The FCC sought public comment on the application earlier this year.
keyFacts: Authorisation covers up to one million satellites
Full deployment required by 2040, the Lynnwood Times reports
SpaceX applied in January 2026

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed four Houthi drones over Ras Tanura
articles.summary:
The Saudi-led coalition said its air defences destroyed four drones over Ras Tanura, the site of a major oil terminal, on Wednesday morning, with no casualties in an initial assessment, Al Jazeera reported. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said a strike on the Houthi-held port of Hodeidah had targeted military capabilities and that targets in Saada and Amran were also destroyed.

Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree had urged workers at Saudi Red Sea ports, including Jeddah, to evacuate and told shipping companies to withdraw vessels. The interceptions follow a Houthi drone strike on a Riyadh tower on Tuesday that Saudi authorities said injured at least 11 people.
keyFacts: Four drones destroyed over Ras Tanura, coalition says
Coalition says it struck targets in Hodeidah, Saada and Amran
Houthis told Saudi port workers to evacuate

articles.title: Gaza ministry says Israeli strike killed northern security director and his family
articles.summary:
Gaza's Interior Ministry said an Israeli air strike on a home in the Shati refugee camp at dawn on Wednesday killed Muhammad Majid Abu al-Awf, director of the Internal Security Service in northern Gaza, Al Jazeera reported. The ministry said his wife and two daughters, aged 15 and 13, were also killed.

A source at al-Shifa Hospital confirmed four family members died, according to Al Jazeera. The strike came less than 24 hours after the service's director general, Naim Abu Nahal, was killed. Al Jazeera's report did not include comment from the Israeli military.
keyFacts: Strike hit a home in Shati refugee camp, ministry says
Four members of one family killed, hospital source says
Follows killing of the service's director general a day earlier

articles.title: UK warns firms supplying Ukraine they could be targets of Russian sabotage
articles.summary:
Britain's Ministry of Defence and National Protective Security Authority warned that companies supporting military procurement or supplying Ukraine's armed forces could be targeted by Russian sabotage, Al Jazeera and Reuters reported. The warning said such activity typically used proxies and simple methods such as arson.

Security Minister Dan Jarvis said recent sabotage attempts across Europe showed the seriousness of the threat. The ministry said it would hold closed briefings for infrastructure and defence sector leaders. Russia's embassy in London denied the claims, saying Russia had no plans or intention to attack the UK, and accused Ukraine of staging sabotage, which Kyiv has denied.
keyFacts: Warning covers firms in defence supply and Ukraine support
Officials say proxies typically use methods such as arson
Russian embassy denies any plans to attack the UK

articles.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine is waiting for US to set date for four-way peace talks
articles.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Wednesday that Kyiv was waiting for the United States to set a date for the next round of negotiations, which he said should now include Europe, Ukrinform and Interfax-Ukraine reported. He made the comments after meeting Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna in Kyiv.

The previous US-mediated round, involving Ukraine, the US and Russia, was held in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 November, Anadolu reported. Interfax-Ukraine said presidential office head Kyrylo Budanov had earlier suggested a four-party meeting could happen before Christmas. Russian presidential aide Yury Ushakov said no agreement had been reached on a meeting involving European representatives, according to Anadolu.
keyFacts: Zelenskyy wants next round to include Europe
Last round held in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 November
Kremlin aide says no agreement yet on European participation

articles.title: Two eastern Libyan officers die after Ukraine's drone attack on Russian ship
articles.summary:
Two officers of the eastern-based Libyan National Army have died from wounds suffered in the drone attack near Benghazi port that Ukraine has claimed, the LNA said, according to Al Jazeera. The LNA named them as Al-Taher Abdullah al-Sadiq and Lieutenant Ali Mohammed al-Said, and said they died on Tuesday.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said seven Ukrainian naval drones sank a Russian corvette in the attack and that 10 people were injured. The LNA said it would retaliate at a time and place of its choosing. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said Ukraine was exercising its right to self-defence, Al Jazeera reported.
keyFacts: LNA says two officers died of wounds on Tuesday
Zelenskyy says seven naval drones sank a Russian corvette
LNA says it will retaliate

articles.title: 26 workers trapped after river floods unlicensed gold mine in West Java
articles.summary:
Rescuers are searching for workers trapped in an unlicensed open-pit gold mine in Bogor district, West Java, after a nearby river overflowed during heavy rain on Monday, Al Jazeera reported. West Java police spokesman Hendra Rochmawan said 26 people had yet to be evacuated.

The Jakarta search and rescue office said the workers were in a mine about 100 metres deep with narrow access, and that teams were monitoring water levels. The site is in the Pongkor area, about 60 kilometres south of Jakarta, where state miner Antam operates. Local media reported authorities had closed about 30 gold pits in another part of Bogor last week.
keyFacts: Police say 26 people yet to be evacuated
Mine is about 100 metres deep, rescuers say
Flooding followed a river overflow on Monday

articles.title: Bangladesh wage board raises garment workers' minimum pay by 36%
articles.summary:
Bangladesh's government-appointed garment wage board has agreed to raise the monthly minimum wage from 12,500 taka to 17,500 taka, about $US136, after weeks of protests, its chairman said on Wednesday, according to Al Jazeera. Protesters had sought 30,000 taka, and it was unclear whether they would accept the offer.

Labour representative Babul Akhter said workers were not completely satisfied but the result was not entirely bad. The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association said the protests had cost the industry an estimated $US428 million. The new rate takes effect in December, with the higher pay due in January.
keyFacts: Minimum wage rises from 12,500 to 17,500 taka a month
Protesters had sought 30,000 taka
Industry body puts protest cost at $US428 million

articles.title: WHO chief calls on US to lift fuel blockade on Cuba during Havana visit
articles.summary:
World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called for the US fuel blockade on Cuba to be lifted, saying on Tuesday during a three-day visit that sanctions were putting children's lives at risk, Al Jazeera reported. He said the WHO would contribute $US2 million for Cuba's immunisation program and medical equipment, and met President Miguel Diaz-Canel.

Tedros said Cuban life expectancy fell from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 in 2025, the first decline since records began, figures that predate the blockade imposed in January. Washington says the measure aims at political change and that food and medicine exports are legally exempt.
keyFacts: WHO pledges $US2 million for immunisation and equipment
Life expectancy fell to 74.4 years in 2025, Tedros says
US says food and medicine are exempt

articles.title: Lubanga-led rebel group says it is withdrawing from areas near Congo's Bunia
articles.summary:
The Convention for the Popular Revolution, led by convicted war criminal Thomas Lubanga, said on Tuesday it would halt its advance towards Bunia, capital of Congo's Ituri province, and withdraw from recently seized areas after days of fighting with government forces, Al Jazeera reported.

The group had captured Iga-Barriere, about 25 kilometres north of Bunia, a day earlier. It said the withdrawal followed talks mediated by Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni. The World Health Organization said on Sunday that fighting near a hospital in Ituri had forced health workers to evacuate, disrupting the Ebola response.
keyFacts: Group says it will halt advance on Bunia
Iga-Barriere, 25 km north of Bunia, was seized a day earlier
Withdrawal follows talks mediated by Uganda's Museveni

articles.title: Annual inflation rises to 4.9% in October, above forecasts, ABS figures show
articles.summary:
Consumer prices rose 4.9 per cent in the 12 months to October, up from 4.3 per cent in September, according to figures released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics on Wednesday. The trimmed mean measure watched by the Reserve Bank rose to 3.8 per cent, above the 3.6 per cent economists had expected, the ABC reported.

The ABS said transport costs rose 10.6 per cent over the year, driven by fuel, while electricity prices rose 25.2 per cent after Commonwealth energy rebates ended. Some economists quoted by the ABC said rising inflation and unemployment posed a difficult mix for the RBA, which next meets on 8 December.
keyFacts: Headline CPI 4.9%, up from 4.3% in September
Trimmed mean 3.8%, above 3.6% forecast
Electricity up 25.2% as rebates ended, ABS says

articles.title: Albanese and Wale sign Australia–Solomon Islands treaty in Canberra
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale signed a bilateral treaty in Canberra on Wednesday, following reports that Honiara will not renew its 2022 security pact with China. A joint statement said the treaty reflects the Solomon Islands' choice of Australia as its primary security partner and that there will be no foreign military or security base in the country.

The statement lists budget support, infrastructure, education, labour mobility and police support. AAP reported Australia's pledges total about $985 million, citing a leaked message from Deputy Prime Minister Francis Sade. Wale declined to confirm the China pact decision, citing a confidentiality clause, according to the ABC.
keyFacts: Treaty signed in Canberra on Wednesday
No foreign military or security base, joint statement says
AAP reports pledges of about $985 million

articles.title: Greens back Labor's trust tax in exchange for higher private jet fuel excise
articles.summary:
The Greens agreed on Wednesday to support Labor's legislation imposing a minimum 30 per cent tax on some discretionary trusts, in exchange for raising fuel excise on private jets, AAP reported via SBS. Under the deal, the excise on private jet fuel would rise to the motorist rate of 53.7 cents a litre, from 3.56 cents.

Greens senator Nick McKim said the changes would make the tax system fairer. The Coalition opposed the measures. Small business and industry groups had forecast a $1 billion impact, and the Business Council of Australia said employers would be affected twice, according to AAP.
keyFacts: Minimum 30% tax on some discretionary trusts
Private jet fuel excise to rise to 53.7 cents a litre
Coalition opposed the measures

articles.title: Senate passes digital duty of care bill; Coalition says it would likely repeal it
articles.summary:
The Senate has passed the Online Safety Amendment (Digital Duty of Care) Bill with the support of the Greens and several crossbench senators, according to the ABC and The Epoch Times. The bill, which allows maximum penalties of up to 5 per cent of a platform's global revenue, returns to the House of Representatives to approve Senate amendments.

Communications Minister Anika Wells said earlier that her talks with US ambassador David Brat, who had criticised the penalties, were useful, AAP reported. Opposition spokesman Andrew Hastie called the bill heavy-handed and said a Coalition government would likely repeal it. The Coalition and One Nation opposed the bill.
keyFacts: Passed Senate with Greens and crossbench support
Penalties up to 5% of global revenue
Returns to the House to approve amendments

articles.title: Government exempts pensioners from private health insurance rebate cut to win Greens
articles.summary:
The federal government will exempt all pensioners, including service pension and veteran payment recipients, from planned cuts to the private health insurance rebate for people over 65, the ABC reported on Wednesday. The change clears the way for the bill to pass the Senate with Greens support, after the Coalition and crossbench earlier defeated it.

According to the ABC, the carve-out gives up about half of the $3 billion in forecast savings that were to go to aged care. Health Minister Mark Butler said the government recognised the realities of the Senate. Independent MP Monique Ryan described the exemption as a win for older Australians.
keyFacts: All pensioners exempted from rebate cut
About half of $3 billion savings forgone, ABC says
Greens support clears Senate path

articles.title: Government formally apologises to LGBTQ defence personnel over past discrimination
articles.summary:
Defence Minister Richard Marles delivered a formal apology on Wednesday to current and former defence personnel who were discriminated against under past policies on homosexuality, according to the Department of Defence and the ABC's parliament coverage. Reuters reported the apology was to LGBTQ veterans who faced discrimination in the military.

The government announced in October that it would apologise and move to remove historical convictions related to homosexual conduct in defence service, according to a ministerial release at the time. Defence published the apology under the title of an apology to personnel shamed for who they were.
keyFacts: Apology delivered by Defence Minister Richard Marles
Covers current and former personnel
Follows October plan to remove historical convictions

articles.title: WA regulator says Chevron deliberately vented gas at Gorgon rather than leaking it
articles.summary:
Western Australia's Department of Water and Environmental Regulation has found that methane plumes detected at Chevron's Gorgon gas project in August came from deliberate venting through approved infrastructure, not a leak, the ABC reported on Wednesday. The department said the company vented reservoir carbon dioxide while its carbon capture system was constrained.

Environment Minister Matthew Swinbourn said there was no evidence of an unauthorised emissions source. Chevron said it worked constructively with the regulator. Greens MLC Sophie McNeill tabled a whistleblower claim that the release was deliberate. Satellite estimates put emissions at an average of 4.9 tonnes an hour, according to the ABC.
keyFacts: Regulator says release was venting, not a leak
Carbon capture system was constrained at the time
Satellites estimated 4.9 tonnes an hour

articles.title: Emergency warnings issued as out-of-control bushfire spreads on Flinders Island
articles.summary:
An out-of-control bushfire started by lightning on Tasmania's Flinders Island has forced evacuations, with emergency warnings in place for Killiecrankie, Leeka and Mount Tanner on Wednesday, AAP reported. About 3,000 hectares burned on Tuesday before the fire moved south after a wind change, and some residents were told it was too late to leave.

Nearly 40 firefighters, 12 parks staff, five helicopters and three aircraft were working on the fire, according to AAP. Tasmania Fire Service incident controller Steven Richardson said it was too early to say whether destroyed structures included homes. Parks Minister Nick Duigan said more resources were being sent.
keyFacts: About 3,000 hectares burned on Tuesday
Emergency warnings for Killiecrankie, Leeka, Mount Tanner
Five helicopters and three aircraft deployed

articles.title: Forecasts show unprecedented ocean heat for Great Barrier Reef this summer
articles.summary:
CSIRO and Bureau of Meteorology forecasts show ocean temperatures along Australia's east coast about 2C above normal in coming months, the ABC reported on Wednesday. Scientists said the Great Barrier Reef could face its seventh mass bleaching event in about a decade, and a heat-stress scale has been extended to cover higher levels.

Reef Authority chief scientist Roger Beeden said it was likely to be a challenging summer. The Australian Marine Conservation Society called for an emergency response plan. A spokesperson for Environment Minister Murray Watt said existing processes were strong, according to the ABC.
keyFacts: East-coast waters forecast about 2C above normal
Reef could face seventh mass bleaching in a decade
Conservation group seeks emergency plan

articles.title: Asian chip stocks fall sharply as AI doubts return; Taiwan index drops up to 7.9%
articles.summary:
Asian share markets fell on Wednesday as doubts about the artificial intelligence boom returned, reversing gains made after Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia's chief executive, Al Jazeera reported. South Korea's Kospi fell more than 6 per cent and Taiwan's Taiex dropped as much as 7.9 per cent in morning trade. Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 3.6 per cent.

Chipmakers led the declines, with Tokyo Electron down 13.5 per cent, SK Hynix down 9.9 per cent and Samsung Electronics down 9.1 per cent, according to Al Jazeera. Hong Kong's Hang Seng rose as much as 1.3 per cent.
keyFacts: Kospi down more than 6%
Taiex down as much as 7.9%
Nikkei 225 down 3.6%

articles.title: ASX 200 falls after higher-than-expected inflation figures
articles.summary:
Australian shares fell on Wednesday after inflation data came in above forecasts, AAP reported. The S&P/ASX 200 was down 70.5 points, or 0.81 per cent, at 8,655.9 by midday, a day after the index ended an eight-session losing run.

Raw materials stocks fell 2.4 per cent, with BHP down almost 3 per cent and Rio Tinto about 2 per cent, according to AAP. Harvey Norman fell 4.6 per cent after reporting that its four-month profit nearly halved, while Tyro rose almost 15 per cent after reaffirming guidance and announcing a share buyback.
keyFacts: ASX 200 down 0.81% at midday
Materials sector down 2.4%
Harvey Norman down 4.6% on profit fall

articles.title: China launches Shenzhou-24 with first foreign astronaut, from Pakistan
articles.summary:
China launched the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft from the Jiuquan launch centre at 8:18am Beijing time on Wednesday, carrying the first foreign astronaut to fly to its Tiangong space station, Xinhua reported. The China Manned Space Agency said the launch was a complete success.

The crew are commander Tang Hongbo, flight engineer Wu Yi and Pakistani payload specialist Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, according to Xinhua and AP. Ali is due to return on Shenzhou-23 after a short stay, while the other two will remain about six months. Xinhua said more than 90 experiments are planned.
keyFacts: Launched 8:18am Beijing time from Jiuquan
Crew includes Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali
More than 90 experiments planned

articles.title: Eisenkot's Yashar party agrees coalition pact with Lieberman's party in Israel
articles.summary:
Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party said on Tuesday it had agreed to sign a coalition agreement with Avigdor Lieberman's party, the first such alliance since Israel's 27 October election, Al Jazeera and Reuters reported. Yashar won 21 seats and Lieberman's party seven, while Likud holds 53 of the Knesset's 120 seats.

Eisenkot has until 6 December to form a government, with a possible 14-day extension. The left-wing Democrats, with eight seats, suspended talks, and leader Yair Golan has said he prefers a government without Benjamin Netanyahu that includes Arab parties, according to Al Jazeera.
keyFacts: First coalition pact since 27 October election
Yashar 21 seats, Lieberman's party seven
Deadline to form government is 6 December

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition orders Hodeidah evacuation; Houthis threaten Saudi Red Sea ports
articles.summary:
The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen issued an evacuation order for civilians at the Red Sea port of Hodeidah, saying it was for their safety, Al Jazeera reported on Wednesday. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group would target Jeddah port and other Saudi Red Sea ports if Hodeidah were attacked.

Separately, Iran's Revolutionary Guards chief Ahmad Vahidi warned that future wars could extend beyond the region and urged neighbouring states to reconsider security ties with the United States, according to Al Jazeera.
keyFacts: Coalition issues Hodeidah evacuation order
Houthis threaten Jeddah and other Saudi ports
IRGC chief warns of wider conflict

articles.title: Indigenous children's commissioner to issue annual report cards on governments
articles.summary:
National Commissioner for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Children Sue-Anne Hunter said on Wednesday she would publish yearly report cards on all Australian governments and name those failing Indigenous children, the ABC reported from her National Press Club address.

Hunter said Indigenous children are 9.6 times as likely to be in out-of-home care and about 27 times as likely to be in youth detention as other children. Her requests include raising the age of criminal responsibility to 14. She said she was not ruling out a national inquiry, and her first review, into child protection in the Pilbara, is under way.
keyFacts: Annual report cards on all governments
Calls for criminal responsibility age of 14
First review examines Pilbara child protection

articles.title: NSW ICAC finds culture of misogyny across prison system, makes 10 recommendations
articles.summary:
The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption has found a widespread culture of misogyny and sexualised behaviour across the state's prisons, the ABC reported on Wednesday. The Operation Targo report described a boys' club culture within Corrective Services NSW.

Commissioner Helen Murrell SC said the culture tolerated harassment and abuse of staff. The commission made no findings of corrupt conduct, saying the evidence did not meet the threshold. Corrective Services NSW and the Department of Communities and Justice have accepted all 10 recommendations, according to the ABC. Corrections Minister Anoulack Chanthivong was approached for comment.
keyFacts: Operation Targo report released Wednesday
No corrupt conduct findings made
All 10 recommendations accepted

articles.title: Tasmania's upper house passes ban on conversion practices
articles.summary:
Tasmania's Legislative Council passed legislation banning conversion practices on Wednesday, AAP reported. The bill, which passed the lower house in October, returns there for a final procedural stage before becoming law. AAP said Tasmania would become the sixth Australian jurisdiction with such a ban, after NSW, Victoria, Queensland, South Australia and the ACT.

Premier Jeremy Rockliff supported the bill, while Treasurer Eric Abetz and Deputy Premier Guy Barnett voted against it, according to AAP. Equality Tasmania's Rodney Croome described it as a momentous day.
keyFacts: Passed Legislative Council on Wednesday
Returns to lower house for final stage
Would be sixth jurisdiction with a ban

articles.title: NT government confirms it is examining 'castle law' for home intruders
articles.summary:
The Northern Territory government has confirmed it is looking at a so-called castle law, which would remove a resident's duty to retreat from an intruder, the ABC reported on Wednesday. Chief Minister Lia Finocchiaro said options remained on the table.

Education Minister Jo Hersey, who had referred to the idea in a Facebook comment, told Question Time it was not government policy. University of Sydney professor Tyrone Kirchengast said the Territory would be the first Australian jurisdiction to explicitly legislate such a law. No date has been set for legislation, according to the ABC.
keyFacts: Law would remove duty to retreat from intruders
Chief Minister says options on the table
No legislation date set

articles.title: NSW says Sydney fire ant detection is part of a larger infestation
articles.summary:
The NSW government said on Wednesday that a red imported fire ant nest found and treated in Auburn at the weekend is part of a larger infestation, the ABC reported. Commonwealth authorities first detected the ants at the Enfield Intermodal Logistics Centre on 23 September.

Agriculture Minister Tara Moriarty said the ants appeared to have arrived in infested imported goods. A taskforce will trace supply chains and inspect high-risk sites, and detection dogs have been deployed in Auburn, according to the ABC. Residents have been asked to report nests and not to destroy them.
keyFacts: Auburn nest part of larger infestation
Ants first found at Enfield on 23 September
Taskforce to trace imported supply chains

articles.title: NSW to open public hospital theatres to IVF patients as Calvary plans to end service
articles.summary:
NSW Health Minister Ryan Park said on Wednesday that operating theatres at John Hunter Hospital will be made available to Hunter IVF patients, the ABC reported. Catholic provider Calvary Health Care plans to stop IVF at Newcastle Private and Hunter Valley Private hospitals on religious grounds as part of a takeover being assessed by the ACCC.

The ACCC is expected to decide by 10 December. Park said the arrangement would last as long as necessary. According to the ABC, elective abortions, voluntary assisted dying and gender reassignment would also stop at the hospitals if the licences transfer.
keyFacts: John Hunter Hospital theatres opened to IVF patients
ACCC decision on takeover due by 10 December
Calvary to end IVF on religious grounds

articles.title: Parliamentary AI inquiry recommends payment scheme for creators whose work trains AI
articles.summary:
The federal Joint Select Committee on artificial intelligence made 46 recommendations on Tuesday, including a scheme to pay creators whose work is used to train AI models, the ABC reported. Labor, Liberal and independent members backed the report, and draft laws are expected early next year.

Independent senator David Pocock dissented, calling the report overly optimistic and seeking a three-year copyright freeze. ARIA's Annabelle Herd rejected the report, and News Corp's Michael Miller criticised frameworks based on voluntary licensing deals, according to the ABC.
keyFacts: 46 recommendations from joint committee
Proposes payment scheme for creators
Pocock dissented, seeking copyright freeze

articles.title: Alaska withdraws from agreement to share voter records with US Justice Department
articles.summary:
Alaska Lieutenant Governor Nancy Dahlstrom announced on Monday that the state was withdrawing, effective immediately, from a 2025 agreement with the US Justice Department on voter records, Al Jazeera and AP reported. She said circumstances had changed, and the state said no voters had been removed under the agreement.

Democratic state senator Bill Wielechowski said the timing was intended to end a lawsuit before the incoming governor's administration could settle it. A Justice Department spokesperson said a formal response would follow, according to the report.
keyFacts: Withdrawal effective immediately
State says no voters removed under deal
Justice Department to respond formally

articles.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia to leave US for Spain after judge's self-deport order
articles.summary:
Kilmar Abrego Garcia, whom the US government mistakenly deported to El Salvador in 2025, will self-deport to Spain, according to a person familiar with the matter cited by AP and the ABC. A judge told him on Tuesday, US time, to self-deport, ending his challenge to removal to a country in Africa.

Maryland senator Chris Van Hollen said he was relieved and described Abrego Garcia as a free man. The administration had described the original deportation as an administrative error. His lawyers and the advocacy group CASA did not comment, the ABC reported.
keyFacts: Judge ordered self-deportation on Tuesday
Abrego Garcia to go to Spain
Was wrongly deported to El Salvador in 2025

articles.title: Russian strikes kill three in Odesa and Kyiv regions, Ukrainian officials say
articles.summary:
A Russian strike in Ukraine's Odesa region killed two people and injured three, including a child, Governor Oleh Kiper said late on Tuesday, according to Reuters. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said drone debris started a fire in a 16-storey building in the capital, injuring two.

In the Kyiv region, an overnight attack killed a man in Bila Tserkva district and damaged trucks and a commercial site, Governor Tymur Tkachenko said, the Kyiv Independent reported. Reuters and the Kyiv Independent said they could not independently verify all details.
keyFacts: Two killed in Odesa region, governor says
One killed in Bila Tserkva district
Two injured in Kyiv building fire

articles.title: Government extends $217.6 million in family violence funding as 16 Days campaign begins
articles.summary:
Social Services Minister Tanya Plibersek announced $217.6 million to extend services addressing violence against women, AAP reported on Wednesday, the United Nations day for the elimination of violence against women. AAP said the extension lifts the federal commitment to $4.6 billion.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said every woman and child had the right to feel safe. The 16 Days of Activism campaign, which focuses on ending gender-based violence, runs until 10 December, according to AAP.
keyFacts: $217.6 million extension announced
Federal commitment rises to $4.6 billion
16 Days campaign runs to 10 December

articles.title: NT mid-year budget update forecasts 7.1% growth and future surplus
articles.summary:
Northern Territory Treasurer Bill Yan's mid-year budget update forecasts economic growth of 7.1 per cent in 2026-27, up from an earlier 5.8 per cent forecast, AAP reported on Wednesday. Revenue is forecast to be $155 million higher, and an operating surplus of $370 million is projected by 2029-30.

Opposition Leader Selina Uibo said the update offered no cost-of-living relief. Yan acknowledged that cost-of-living pressures remained for Territory households, according to AAP.
keyFacts: Growth forecast 7.1% for 2026-27
Revenue $155 million higher than forecast
$370 million surplus projected by 2029-30

articles.title: Poll finds 55% of US adults want Iran war ended regardless of terms
articles.summary:
A University of Maryland and Ipsos survey of 1,022 US adults found 55 per cent agreed the war with Iran should end now regardless of the terms, Al Jazeera reported. Agreement was 80 per cent among Democrats, 59 per cent among independents and about 25 per cent among Republicans.

Twenty-one per cent favoured continuing the current approach and 18 per cent supported escalation, according to the poll. Poll director Shibley Telhami said the public mood was to end the war now.
keyFacts: Survey of 1,022 US adults
55% back ending war regardless of terms
18% support escalation

articles.title: Protected witness gives evidence of alleged payments at Queensland CFMEU inquiry
articles.summary:
A protected witness using a pseudonym gave evidence remotely on Wednesday to Queensland's commission of inquiry into the CFMEU, with his image and voice altered, AAP reported. The hearing was closed to the public.

The witness alleged that a subcontractor paid union officials for contracts and that drugs were widely used on construction sites. The allegations are untested and have not been proven, AAP noted. The inquiry, led by commissioner Stuart Wood KC, is due to deliver its final report in December 2027.
keyFacts: Witness gave evidence under a pseudonym
Allegations untested, AAP notes
Final report due December 2027

articles.title: Solomon Islands tells China it will not renew 2022 security pact, ABC confirms
articles.summary:
The Solomon Islands government has told Beijing it will not renew its 2022 security agreement with China when the five-year term ends in April 2027, the ABC reported on Tuesday, confirming an earlier Nine Newspapers report through its own sources.

Prime Minister Matthew Wale is in Canberra and is due to sign a treaty with Australia on Wednesday, under which Australia would provide about $980 million in extra funding, according to the ABC. Foreign Minister Penny Wong has previously called the 2022 pact a major setback for Australia. Opposition leader Manasseh Sogavare said the country should weigh what it stands to lose from the decision.
keyFacts: Pact's five-year term ends in April 2027
Australia treaty due to be signed on Wednesday
Australia to provide about $980 million, ABC reports

articles.title: Shanghai Communist Party chief Chen Jining placed under investigation
articles.summary:
Chinese state media announced on Tuesday that Shanghai's Communist Party secretary, Chen Jining, is under investigation by the party's Central Commission for Discipline Inspection over what it called serious violations of discipline and law, the ABC reported. No further details were given.

Chen has led Shanghai since 2022 and was previously Beijing's mayor, environment minister and president of Tsinghua University. The ABC said he is the fourth member of the 21-member Politburo to be investigated this term. Analysts quoted by the ABC said they could not say why Chen had been targeted.
keyFacts: Announcement made by Chinese state media on Tuesday
Chen has been Shanghai party secretary since 2022
Fourth Politburo member investigated this term, ABC says

articles.title: US expected to propose new tariffs on 16 trading partners after trade probe, Reuters says
articles.summary:
The Trump administration could announce the results of a Section 301 investigation into alleged excess industrial capacity as soon as Tuesday or Wednesday, Reuters reported, citing three unnamed people. The probe covers 16 trading partners, including China, the European Union, India, Japan, South Korea, Mexico and Vietnam.

The US Trade Representative is expected to propose duties on top of existing tariffs, partly replacing global import taxes struck down by the US Supreme Court in February, according to Reuters. Rates and exemptions were not known. The USTR and White House did not respond to Reuters. China has rejected the accusations, saying its exports reflect competitive advantages.
keyFacts: Section 301 probe covers 16 trading partners
Duties would partly replace tariffs struck down in February
Officials did not comment, Reuters says

articles.title: AI shares fall back on Wall Street as Anthropic slips below its IPO price
articles.summary:
Shares in artificial intelligence companies fell on Tuesday, a day after a sharp rally, AP reported. By early afternoon in New York, Nvidia was down about 7 per cent after rising 31.5 per cent on Monday, while the Nasdaq was down 1.3 per cent and the S&P 500 0.3 per cent. The Dow Jones index was up 0.9 per cent.

Anthropic shares fell below their $US83 initial public offering price, according to AP and CNBC, less than a week after the company's market debut. AP said CoreWeave fell 11.6 per cent. The Conference Board's consumer confidence survey showed confidence rose among Democrats and independents and slipped among Republicans.
keyFacts: Nvidia down about 7% a day after a 31.5% gain
Anthropic traded below its $US83 IPO price
Dow rose while Nasdaq fell, AP reported

articles.title: Aviation passenger protection bills unlikely to pass Senate before Christmas, ABC reports
articles.summary:
Labor's four-bill aviation consumer protection package, which passed the House of Representatives in June, is unlikely to clear the Senate before Christmas, the ABC reported. The bills would set airline and airport obligations during disruptions, add accessibility standards and create an Independent Aviation Ombudsman.

Shadow Transport Minister Bridget McKenzie said airlines and airports should pay compensation for disrupted flights, backing her own bill for automatic payouts. Transport Minister Catherine King said mandatory compensation would damage the aviation sector. The ABC cited departmental analysis estimating compensation could add $24 to each ticket. An airline industry group said such schemes do not address the causes of delays.
keyFacts: Package passed the lower house in June
Coalition wants mandatory compensation for disruptions
Department estimates $24 added per ticket, ABC says

articles.title: Victorian Liberals pledge to close Richmond safe injecting room before Saturday election
articles.summary:
Victorian Liberal leader Jess Wilson announced on Tuesday that a Coalition government would close Melbourne's medically supervised injecting room in Richmond and move its services to a recovery facility, AAP reported. The state election is on Saturday.

Premier Ben Carroll said the facility was established and saving lives. Labor cites a review finding it managed 6,000 overdoses and saved up to 63 lives, according to AAP. Greens leader Ellen Sandell said Victoria needed more such sites. Separately, RedBridge modelling suggests Labor could lose almost half its seats, its founder Kos Samaras told AAP.
keyFacts: Coalition would move services to a recovery facility
Labor says the room has saved up to 63 lives
Victorians vote on Saturday

articles.title: Repayments would take almost half a median income despite price falls, Cotality says
articles.summary:
