A median-income household buying a median-priced home would spend 49.5 per cent of pre-tax income on repayments, according to Cotality figures to the end of September reported by the ABC. The calculation assumes a 20 per cent deposit and a 30-year loan.

Cotality said the median home price was 8.2 times median household income, down from a record 8.7 times in March. Adelaide was the least affordable capital relative to incomes. Rents rose 49.4 per cent over five years. Cotality's Gerard Burg said higher mortgage rates had offset much of the benefit of falling prices. The figures exclude the Reserve Bank's November rate rise.
keyFacts: Repayments would take 49.5% of median pre-tax income
Price-to-income ratio eased to 8.2 from 8.7
Rents up 49.4% over five years

articles.title: ASIC review finds more than 3,200 internal complaints at big four accounting firms
articles.summary:
An Australian Securities and Investments Commission review recorded 3,215 internal complaints across Deloitte, PwC, KPMG and EY between July 2023 and June 2026, the ABC reported. Of 558 audit-related complaints given to ASIC, 35 raised concerns about audit conduct or misuse of client information, and 523 covered wider issues, including alleged bullying and sexual harassment.

The most common audit concerns involved falsified or poorly documented work, according to the review. Senator Deborah O'Neill, who chairs a Senate inquiry, criticised the findings. KPMG pointed to an action plan, PwC said audit quality was its highest priority, Deloitte said figures were not directly comparable and EY said its processes were robust.
keyFacts: 3,215 internal complaints recorded over three years
558 audit-related complaints provided to ASIC
All four firms defended their processes

articles.title: AMA report says one in 10 mental health patients waits almost a day in emergency
articles.summary:
About one in 10 mental health patients waits almost 24 hours in hospital emergency departments before being admitted, according to the Australian Medical Association's public hospital report card, the ABC reported. More than half of those later admitted wait over seven hours.

The AMA said Australia has 27 specialised public mental health beds per 100,000 people, and emergency presentations for mental illness almost doubled between 2014-15 and 2024-25. AMA president Michael Bonning said getting help before a crisis was becoming impossible. Vice-president Sarah Whitelaw said the national mental health agreement now being negotiated was a chance to change course.
keyFacts: One in 10 waits almost 24 hours for admission
27 public mental health beds per 100,000 people
Presentations almost doubled over a decade

articles.title: SA parliamentary committee says 2021 law changes undermined ICAC's independence
articles.summary:
A South Australian parliamentary committee reviewing the state's anti-corruption laws found that 2021 amendments, passed with bipartisan support, undermined the Independent Commission Against Corruption's independence, the ABC reported. The Crime and Public Integrity Policy Committee tabled its review on Tuesday.

The committee recommended ICAC be allowed to start its own investigations and refer evidence directly to the Director of Public Prosecutions, but did not recommend widening the definition of corruption. Commissioner Emma Townsend welcomed the referral change, saying it would cut delays. The Malinauskas government said it would carefully consider the recommendations and has not made a decision.
keyFacts: Committee tabled its review on Tuesday
Recommends direct referrals to the DPP
Government yet to decide on recommendations

articles.title: Malaysia's Anwar says more than 6,500 Rohingya will be returned to Myanmar in December
articles.summary:
Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim told parliament on Tuesday that more than 6,500 Rohingya refugees would be sent back to Myanmar, Al Jazeera reported. He said 1,500 people would leave on three navy vessels on 6 and 7 December, and 5,303 would be flown back during December at Myanmar's expense.

Anwar said many asylum seekers had suffered atrocities but that Malaysia could no longer afford to host them, according to Al Jazeera. Rights groups have criticised the returns. The announcement came days after the International Court of Justice ruled Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya. Malaysia said last week it planned to resettle 10,000 Rohingya in Turkey.
keyFacts: 1,500 to leave by navy vessels on 6–7 December
5,303 to be flown back at Myanmar's expense
Rights groups oppose the returns

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says Riyadh financial district tower targeted again; 11 injured
articles.summary:
The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said a tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District was targeted on Tuesday in what its spokesman called a terrorist attack, Al Jazeera reported. The Saudi Press Agency said 11 people were injured, according to Gulf News.

The coalition did not name the building, but three witnesses told AFP the target was the Public Investment Fund tower, which was damaged in a Houthi attack on 19 November. Authorities were investigating at the site, Al Jazeera said. Al Jazeera's live coverage attributed the attack to the Houthis.
keyFacts: Second attack on the district in under a week
Saudi Press Agency reported 11 injured
Witnesses say Public Investment Fund tower was hit

articles.title: Iran's parliament speaker says no talks with US until seven conditions are met
articles.summary:
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who is also the country's chief negotiator, said Iran would not negotiate with Washington until seven conditions were met, Gulf News reported on Tuesday. Reports said the conditions include lifting the US naval blockade.

The head of the Revolutionary Guards navy, Ali Ozmaei, separately warned vessels against using unauthorised routes through the Strait of Hormuz, according to Gulf News. The Iranian army said two oil tankers had caught fire after striking a mine and said they had not complied with Tehran's transit rules.
keyFacts: Ghalibaf is Iran's chief negotiator
Conditions reportedly include lifting the US blockade
Iranian navy warned ships over Hormuz routes

articles.title: Israeli strike kills head of Hamas internal security in Gaza, officials say
articles.summary:
An Israeli air strike in Gaza killed Brigadier General Naim Abu Nahl, director of Hamas's internal security apparatus, medics and police said, according to Al Jazeera. Gaza's interior ministry confirmed his death, and four others were wounded, Al Jazeera's correspondent reported.

The Israeli military and Shin Bet said in a joint statement they had struck a senior Hamas figure, and Israel's Kan broadcaster, citing Israeli sources, named him as the target. Reuters, cited by Al Jazeera, said the service pursues Palestinians suspected of collaborating with Israel. The strike comes during the ceasefire that began in October 2025, which both sides accuse each other of breaching.
keyFacts: Abu Nahl led Hamas's internal security service
Israeli military and Shin Bet confirmed a strike
Four others were wounded, Al Jazeera reports

articles.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill at least three, including UNRWA worker, officials say
articles.summary:
Israeli air strikes killed at least three people in Gaza, including a worker for the UN agency UNRWA, according to the agency and local health officials, AAP reported. Medics named the worker as Adel al-Helo, who was near a water well in the Jabalia refugee camp. Three others were wounded.

An UNRWA spokesperson said initial reports suggested the strike hit a target near a well staffed by agency workers. A separate strike on a vehicle in western Gaza City killed two people, medics said. The Israeli military said it was checking the UNRWA report and did not immediately comment on either strike.
keyFacts: UNRWA worker killed near a well in Jabalia
Two killed in a separate strike on a vehicle
Israeli military said it was checking reports

articles.title: House counsel disputes Justice Department account of search of Ilhan Omar's home
articles.summary:
Court documents unsealed on Monday showed federal prosecutors told a court that the US House of Representatives' general counsel, Matthew Berry, declined to be involved in the October search of Representative Ilhan Omar's home, Al Jazeera reported. Berry called the Justice Department's claim that he agreed with its position categorically false.

A magistrate judge ordered the department to let Omar assert constitutional protections over seized material, according to Al Jazeera. The administration is investigating Omar over alleged immigration fraud. Omar's lawyers have said the search was neither justified nor lawful, and Omar says she was naturalised in 2000. Her office did not respond to Al Jazeera.
keyFacts: Documents were unsealed on Monday
Judge allowed Omar to assert protections over seized items
Omar's lawyers say the search was unlawful

articles.title: Appeals court lets Iowa lead azide detonation proceed; Trump says he ordered a hold
articles.summary:
The US Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit denied an emergency bid by environmental groups to stop the Army detonating about 4.5 tonnes of lead azide at its Middletown, Iowa plant, lifting its earlier stay on Monday, ABC News (US) reported.

President Donald Trump said on social media he had ordered the military to hold off until the court and incoming Governor Rob Sand agreed, and said he would hold Sand responsible for any harm if they did not. Sand said he deferred to the administration while calling for transparency. The Army said destroying the material in place was the only responsible option.
keyFacts: Eighth Circuit lifted its administrative stay
Trump said he ordered the military to hold off
Army says on-site destruction is the only option

articles.title: Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia kills at least two and wounds more than 40, officials say
articles.summary:
A Russian air strike on the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia killed at least two people and wounded more than 40, including an infant, according to local officials cited by Al Jazeera on Tuesday.

The strike came as Ukraine said its attacks on a Russian warship and a cargo vessel off the coast of Libya were legitimate self-defence, Al Jazeera reported. Kyiv has claimed responsibility for the Libya attacks. Moscow has said it will respond to Ukrainian strikes on its oil refineries, according to Al Jazeera's coverage.
keyFacts: At least two killed in Zaporizhzhia
More than 40 wounded, including an infant
Figures from local Ukrainian officials

articles.title: Labor strikes deal with Greens to pass digital duty of care laws, adding right to sue
articles.summary:
The Albanese government reached an agreement with the Greens on Tuesday to pass its digital duty of care legislation through the Senate, the ABC reported. Under the deal, Australians would gain a private right of action allowing them to sue social media companies over harm.

The maximum penalty would rise to up to 5 per cent of a platform's global revenue, up from the government's original proposal of up to $109.2 million, according to the ABC. Greens leader David Shoebridge said the changes would take power back from big tech. The Coalition said it remained opposed, citing free speech concerns.
keyFacts: Deal secures Senate passage with Greens support
Maximum fine rises to 5% of global revenue
Coalition opposes the bill over free speech concerns

articles.title: Wong uses Senate address to pitch UN Security Council bid and frame AI as security issue
articles.summary:
Foreign Minister Penny Wong delivered a foreign policy statement to the Senate on Tuesday titled "Securing Australia's future in a changing world", SBS News reported. She outlined six shifts she said were reshaping the world, including growing coercion, changing great-power behaviour, weaponised economic ties and weaker collective institutions.

Wong argued artificial intelligence was a national security challenge on which Australia should help lead, according to SBS. She promoted Australia's bid for a non-permanent UN Security Council seat for 2029–30, with the vote due in June 2028. She said Australia would keep its US alliance while seeking cooperation with both the US and China.
keyFacts: Speech delivered in the Senate on 24 November
Australia seeking a 2029–30 Security Council seat
Wong describes AI as a national security challenge

articles.title: Revolutionary Guards say three tankers hit mines and caught fire in Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary:
The naval arm of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said on Monday that three tankers it described as violating its directives had struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire, according to Iranian state media cited by Iran International. It said one was hit near the southern coast and two east of the strait while under US air escort.

The claims could not be independently verified, Iran International reported, and no ships were named. The Jerusalem Post reported that US Central Command had not responded. The IRGC said US military cover was no substitute for following its instructions.
keyFacts: IRGC says three tankers hit mines within hours
No ships named and claims not independently verified
IRGC says vessels were under US air escort

articles.title: US Treasury flags $US14.7 billion in possible Iranian shadow banking and adds sanctions
articles.summary:
The US Treasury said on Monday (US time) that its Financial Crimes Enforcement Network had identified about $US14.7 billion in financial activity between January 2025 and August 2026 potentially linked to Iranian shadow banking. The largest flagged flow, about $US2.6 billion, ran from mainland China-based banks to UAE-based banks, the department said.

The US also sanctioned 22 entities and eight people as part of efforts against the networks, Iran International reported. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the department would keep cutting financial lifelines it said fund Iran's military and allied groups. Iran had not publicly responded to the measures at the time of reporting.
keyFacts: FinCEN analysis covers January 2025 to August 2026
Networks most prominent in UAE, Hong Kong and Singapore
22 entities and eight people sanctioned

articles.title: Australia and Singapore sign essential supplies and carbon storage agreements
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Singapore's Prime Minister Lawrence Wong held their annual leaders' meeting in Canberra on Tuesday, according to Singapore's Prime Minister's Office. The two countries signed a memorandum of understanding on essential supplies covering food, pharmaceuticals, medical products and farm inputs, extending an April arrangement on fuel and LNG.

They also signed an agreement on cross-border carbon capture and storage and launched a programme on low-emissions products, the office said. Wong said both sides intended to work together on artificial intelligence governance and testing. He noted Singapore Airlines had operated the first flight into Western Sydney International Airport the night before.
keyFacts: Essential supplies pact expanded beyond fuel
Cross-border carbon capture and storage deal signed
Meeting held in Canberra on 24 November

articles.title: ASX 200 rises 1.8% to end eight-session losing run as tech stocks lead
articles.summary:
The S&P/ASX 200 closed up 1.8 per cent at 8,726 points on Tuesday, ending a run of eight consecutive daily losses, the ABC reported. The gains followed a rally on Wall Street after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive.

Technology shares rose 2.8 per cent, the strongest sector, while energy was the only sector to fall, according to the ABC. Of the top 200 stocks, 176 rose. The Australian dollar was little changed at about 66.27 US cents. Monthly consumer price figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics are due on Wednesday.
keyFacts: ASX 200 closed at 8,726 points
Technology sector rose 2.8%
176 of 200 stocks finished higher

articles.title: Oil prices hover near three-month lows as supply concerns outweigh Hormuz risks
articles.summary:
Brent crude fell 66 US cents to $US88.71 a barrel on Tuesday afternoon (Sydney time), after closing on Monday at its lowest level since 31 August, Reuters reported. US West Texas Intermediate fell 60 US cents to $US79.57.

Analysts cited by Reuters pointed to rising crude supply and expectations of a surplus, which they said were offsetting shipping risks in the Strait of Hormuz. Deutsche Bank estimated oversupply at about 1.7 million barrels a day, according to the report. Traders were also watching Iranian claims that tankers had struck mines in the strait.
keyFacts: Brent traded at $US88.71 a barrel
Monday's close was lowest since 31 August
Deutsche Bank estimates 1.7 million bpd oversupply

articles.title: Iran-based operation used AI to create fake journalist writing on Australia, ABC reports
articles.summary:
An Iran-based influence operation used ChatGPT accounts to create a fictitious journalist who wrote about Australia's role in the US-Iran war and posted the material on X, the ABC reported on Tuesday. OpenAI had described the wider operation in a report last month, but that report did not mention the Australian content, according to the ABC.

The ABC said Foreign Minister Penny Wong was expected to raise the operation in federal parliament on Tuesday. A Queensland University of Technology researcher said the material showed how AI could be used to produce persuasive content at scale. OpenAI had not responded to the ABC's request for comment.
keyFacts: Fake persona wrote about Australia's role in the war
OpenAI report on the operation did not cite the Australian posts
Wong expected to raise the issue in parliament

articles.title: New York's top court rules social media firms not liable over 2022 Buffalo shooting
articles.summary:
New York's Court of Appeals ruled 4-3 on Monday (US time) that Google's YouTube, Meta's Instagram, Reddit and Snap could not be held liable over the 2022 mass shooting at a Tops supermarket in Buffalo, in which 10 Black people were killed, the Times of Israel and Reuters reported. Families of victims had argued the platforms helped radicalise the gunman.

The majority found the shooter's actions were so extraordinary that they broke the chain of causation as a matter of law, according to the reports. A lawyer for the plaintiffs said his clients were considering their legal options.
keyFacts: Ruling was decided 4-3
Lawsuits targeted YouTube, Instagram, Reddit and Snap
Ten people were killed in the May 2022 attack

articles.title: ABC to close ABC Entertains channel and treat YouTube as a primary platform
articles.summary:
The ABC will reduce its broadcast television channels from four to three by closing ABC Entertains, formerly ABC Me, managing director Hugh Marks announced on Tuesday while outlining the broadcaster's 2027 strategy, the ABC reported. He said the ABC would treat YouTube as a primary distribution platform.

The measures are expected to save about $50 million a year in total, according to the report. Marks said changes to news and current affairs were likely, with details expected in the first quarter of 2027. The ABC has previously announced redundancies, including 76 positions in the 2026 financial year.
keyFacts: ABC Entertains channel to close
Total savings estimated at about $50 million a year
News division changes expected early 2027

articles.title: Bukele names three Salvadoran soldiers killed in Haiti, citing accidental explosion
articles.summary:
El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele named three soldiers killed during the country's deployment in Haiti and said an accidental explosion during a mission caused their deaths, the Associated Press reported. He said families would receive $US200,000 plus monthly payments, and troops who wished to leave Haiti could do so without reprisal.

About 2,500 Salvadoran troops were sent to Haiti last month after four soldiers went missing in an attack in gang-held territory, according to AP. They have not been found. On Monday, US Democratic lawmakers wrote to senior officials accusing the administration of failing to sanction Haiti's political and economic elite.
keyFacts: Three soldiers named by Bukele
Families to receive $US200,000 and monthly income
Four soldiers missing since October remain unfound

articles.title: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive
articles.summary:
Nvidia's board said on Monday (US time) it had unanimously voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, chief executive and director, effective immediately, according to a statement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. The board said it had received input from senior levels of the US government and was confident his return posed no national security risk. Colette Kress remains chief financial officer.

The board said an independent committee's investigation into reports Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort would continue, and it formed a national security and export control committee. President Donald Trump welcomed the move, the ABC reported. Lawmakers from both parties, including Senator Elizabeth Warren and Representative Don Bacon, criticised it.
keyFacts: Board vote to reinstate Huang was unanimous
Board says US government input informed its decision
Investigation into foreign intelligence reports continues

articles.title: US shares jump as Nvidia rises more than 30% after Huang's return
articles.summary:
US share markets rose sharply on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang, ending a seven-session losing streak for the S&P 500, according to Yahoo Finance and the Associated Press. In afternoon trade the S&P 500 was up about 4.7%, the Nasdaq Composite about 6.4% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average about 3%, or roughly 1,450 points.

Nvidia shares were up about 32% at midday, Yahoo Finance reported, with other chip and AI stocks also higher. The S&P 500 fell almost 9% last week and had entered correction territory. US crude oil was down about 3% at around $US81 a barrel, and the 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 4.94%.
keyFacts: S&P 500 had fallen for seven straight sessions
Nasdaq up more than 6% in afternoon trade
Nvidia shares rose about 32% at midday

articles.title: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler in all-stock deal valued at $US43.9 billion
articles.summary:
Cybersecurity company CrowdStrike said on Monday it had agreed to acquire rival Zscaler in an all-stock deal valuing Zscaler at about $US43.9 billion, according to a statement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. Zscaler shareholders would receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each share, which the companies said was a premium of about 34% to Zscaler's 20 November close.

The companies said the deal is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's 2028 financial year, subject to Zscaler shareholder and regulatory approvals. Zscaler founder Jay Chaudhry, whose group holds about 34% of Zscaler shares, has agreed to vote in favour and will join CrowdStrike's board. CrowdStrike also reported quarterly revenue of $US1.58 billion, up 28%.
keyFacts: Zscaler holders to own about 15.9% of combined firm
Companies forecast about $US500 million in cost savings
Deal needs shareholder and regulatory approval

articles.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine sank Russian corvette at Libyan port; Kremlin vows response
articles.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday that Ukrainian forces sank the Russian corvette Merkury at a naval base in Benghazi on Sunday and hit a cargo ship he said Russia used to carry weapons, Al Jazeera reported. Libya's eastern-based administration lodged a complaint with the UN, saying the attacks breached Libyan sovereignty.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the defence ministry was handling the matter and that Russia would keep striking Ukraine in response, according to Al Jazeera. He described recent attacks on Russian shipping, including in the Baltic Sea, as a dangerous trend. The UN mission in Libya called for an independent investigation into the Benghazi attacks, the Times of Israel reported.
keyFacts: Zelenskyy names the corvette Merkury as sunk
Eastern Libyan authorities complained to the UN
UN mission in Libya seeks an independent inquiry

articles.title: Russia summons Estonian diplomat over planned closure of border crossings
articles.summary:
Russia's Foreign Ministry said on Monday it had summoned Estonia's chargé d'affaires in Moscow to protest Tallinn's decision to close all road crossings on their shared border from 1 December, The Moscow Times reported. Estonia announced the closure, for at least six months, after its security services said they had foiled a Moscow-linked plot against a local drone maker.

The ministry called Estonia's accusations unfounded and also accused it of tacitly letting Ukraine use its airspace for drone attacks on north-western Russia. Estonia's foreign ministry rejected that claim on Monday, saying it had never allowed its territory to be used for another country's military operations. Russia said it reserved the right to take further diplomatic measures.
keyFacts: Estonia plans to shut three road crossings from 1 December
Russia accuses Estonia of aiding Ukrainian drone strikes
Estonia denies letting its territory be used

articles.title: US trade chief says Canada deal close but raises concerns over China ties
articles.summary:
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Washington and Ottawa were making progress towards a trade agreement and were close to finding common ground, The Canadian Press reported. He made the comments in an interview with Fox News.

Greer criticised Canada's decision to allow in more Chinese electric vehicles and to widen tariff relief for some Chinese steel and aluminium products. He said the two governments differed in philosophy, with Canada favouring freer trade while the US focused on problems caused by globalisation. He said most goods traded between the countries remained duty-free. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has said a deal is possible but not yet agreed, the report said.
keyFacts: Greer says sides are close to a landing zone
He criticised Canada's easing of curbs on Chinese EVs
Most US-Canada trade remains duty-free, Greer said

articles.title: Mexico says US extradition order exists for captured cartel leader 'El Chapo Isidro'
articles.summary:
Mexico's Security Minister Omar Garcia Harfuch said on Monday that a US extradition order exists for Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro', Reuters reported. Mexican military forces detained him in Sinaloa state on Friday night, along with two other leaders of his organisation.

Meza Flores is on the FBI's list of ten most wanted fugitives. Mexican officials previously said several people were killed in violence linked to his capture. The Reuters report did not say when an extradition might take place.
keyFacts: Garcia Harfuch confirmed the US extradition order
Meza Flores was detained in Sinaloa on Friday night
He is on the FBI's ten most wanted list

articles.title: Thailand plans to stop exports of chemicals used in Myanmar rare earth mining
articles.summary:
Thailand plans to stop exporting chemicals used in rare earth mining to Myanmar, citing pollution of rivers that flow into northern Thailand, Reuters reported. Deputy Prime Minister Yodchanan Wongsawat announced the plan on Saturday, saying it would cover rare earth production bound for Myanmar and other relevant countries, without giving further detail.

The government said on Sunday it also plans to declare the Thai side of the Kok River a pollution control zone. Unregulated rare earth mining in Myanmar has been linked to river contamination in northern Thailand. Thailand, China and Myanmar are due to hold talks from 24 to 26 November, according to the Thai government.
keyFacts: Plan announced by Deputy PM Yodchanan Wongsawat
Kok River to become a pollution control zone
Thai, Chinese and Myanmar talks set for 24–26 November

articles.title: Canada begins recruiting commissioners for wrongful conviction review body
articles.summary:
Canada's Justice Minister Sean Fraser announced on Monday that recruitment had begun for commissioners of the new Miscarriage of Justice Review Commission, according to a Department of Justice statement. The independent body, created by a law Parliament passed in December 2024, will replace the current system in which the justice minister reviews claims of wrongful conviction.

The commission will have a chief commissioner and four to eight commissioners, each appointed for up to seven years. The department said that in 24 years under the current system it received 236 completed applications and the minister ordered remedies for 36 people. Until the commission starts work, the minister will keep his power to order new trials or appeals.
keyFacts: Commission will operate at arm's length from government
Current system received 236 completed applications in 24 years
Commission to have up to nine members

articles.title: India pledges about 15,000 crore rupees to Nepal during Prime Minister Shah's visit
articles.summary:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah held talks in New Delhi on Monday during Shah's first visit to India since taking office, according to a joint statement from India's Prime Minister's Office. India said it would provide 15,000 crore rupees, including a 3,500 crore rupee grant for post-flood reconstruction and an 11,500 crore rupee credit line for energy projects.

The leaders adopted a joint vision covering trade, connectivity, energy and water, and exchanged eight memorandums of understanding. India opened Kandla port to Nepal's transit trade, and the foundation stone was laid for the 669-megawatt Lower Arun hydropower project. Modi accepted an invitation to visit Nepal, with dates yet to be set.
keyFacts: Package includes a 3,500 crore rupee reconstruction grant
Eight memorandums of understanding were exchanged
Modi accepted an invitation to visit Nepal

articles.title: Iran says Qatar and Pakistan mediation continues after Trump threatens its vessels
articles.summary:
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said on Monday that mediation by Pakistan and Qatar was continuing despite what he described as a lack of seriousness from Washington, Gulf News reported. He said Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz quickly if US conditions were met.

In a Fox News interview broadcast on Sunday, President Donald Trump said Iranian vessels that challenged US forces would end up at the bottom of the sea, according to Gulf News. Baghaei said US threats would strengthen Iran's resolve. Separately, a maritime security analyst said the US had struck a tanker carrying Iranian oil, which neither government had confirmed, the report said.
keyFacts: Baghaei says Iran could reopen Hormuz quickly under a deal
Trump made the threat in a Fox News interview
Reported US strike on a tanker is unconfirmed

articles.title: Houthi media say Saudi strike on Hodeida killed four; Riyadh has not commented
articles.summary:
Houthi-run media said a Saudi attack on the Yemeni port city of Hodeida killed four people and wounded 18, hitting a building of the Public Telecommunications Corporation, according to Gulf News and the Times of Israel. Saudi Arabia had not commented on the claim, Gulf News reported.

The report follows a Houthi claim on Sunday that a strike on a fuel station in Sanaa wounded six people, which Saudi Arabia said involved its interception of a drone. The casualty figures from Hodeida have not been independently confirmed.
keyFacts: Houthi media report four dead and 18 wounded
Telecommunications building was hit, Houthis say
No comment from Saudi Arabia

articles.title: Rental affordability index shows renters in regional areas facing the biggest squeeze
articles.summary:
Rents remained unaffordable across much of Australia over the past year, with regional areas worsening most, according to the 2026 Rental Affordability Index by SGS Economics, commissioned by National Shelter and reported by the ABC. Regional Queensland was the least affordable region, with rent taking more than 32% of the average renting household's income, and regional NSW was less affordable than Sydney for a second year.

Among capitals, Perth was least affordable and the ACT most affordable, while Hobart recorded the largest year-on-year decline. SGS principal Ellen Witte said the decline in capital cities had slowed. National Shelter's Jackson Hills said unaffordability was spreading into higher income groups. The index excludes the Northern Territory.
keyFacts: Regional Queensland is the least affordable region
Perth is the least affordable capital city
Average regional tenant spends 31% of income on rent

articles.title: US House Democrats propose green card route for long-term residents with removal orders
articles.summary:
Four House Democrats, led by Representative Lateefah Simon, have introduced the Protect Our Neighbors Act, which would let certain people with old deportation orders apply for permanent residency, Newsweek reported. Eligibility would be limited to those whose removal orders were based only on certain immigration violations and who had lived in the US for at least 10 years since the order.

The bill would also make final removal orders expire after 10 years unless renewed by the Department of Homeland Security. Newsweek said the bill faces steep odds while Republicans control both chambers. A Congressional Research Service report estimated 1.6 million people on ICE's non-detained docket had final removal orders.
keyFacts: Bill introduced by four House Democrats
Removal orders would lapse after 10 years
Republicans control both chambers of Congress

articles.title: Chalmers says mid-year update will show net savings as jobless forecast rises
articles.summary:
Treasurer Jim Chalmers told parliament on Monday that the mid-year budget update would show a net saving, with new spending more than offset by cuts, the ABC reported. He said the update would be released after 8 December.

Chalmers said unemployment would peak above 5 per cent, compared with 4.5 per cent forecast in the budget, and that growth would be well below 2 per cent for the next two years. He said inflation was not expected to return to the Reserve Bank's 2–3 per cent target band until the end of 2027. Opposition Leader Angus Taylor called for Chalmers to be sacked, while Chalmers accused the Coalition of opposing savings measures in the Senate.
keyFacts: Unemployment now forecast to peak above 5 per cent
Mid-year update due after 8 December
Inflation seen back in target band by end of 2027

articles.title: Government to keep maximum PBS prescription cost at $25 until 2030
articles.summary:
The federal government will introduce legislation to keep the maximum general cost of medicines on the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme at $25 a script until the end of the decade, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Monday. Health Minister Mark Butler said the measure would cost about $242 million over three years and would appear in the mid-year budget update.

NCA NewsWire reported the co-payment had been cut to $25 on 1 January and was due to start rising with indexation in 2027. Butler said separately that the government lacked Senate support for its plan to reduce the private health insurance rebate for people aged 65 and over, and was negotiating with the Greens.
keyFacts: Maximum general script price held at $25 until 2030
Cost put at about $242 million over three years
Over-65s rebate cut lacks Senate numbers, Butler says

articles.title: Poland says Russia made two attempts to kill Ukrainian-American rapper
articles.summary:
Poland's Foreign Ministry said an alleged Russian plot to kill Ukrainian-American rapper Albert Vasiliev, known as Kyivstoner, was the second attempt on his life, after an earlier plan was foiled in Poland in August, Al Jazeera reported. A ministry spokesperson confirmed the alleged plot to AP on Sunday, and Polish authorities said a Russian national was detained on 7 August.

Denmark expelled a Russian diplomat on Friday over an alleged plan to kill Vasiliev at a concert near Copenhagen, and two Danish men have been charged. Russia's embassy in Copenhagen called the allegations unsubstantiated. Russia's FSB has accused Vasiliev of supplying drones for an alleged Ukrainian attack, which he denies, according to Danish broadcaster DR.
keyFacts: Poland says it foiled a first plot in August
Denmark expelled a Russian diplomat on Friday
Russia calls the allegations unsubstantiated

articles.title: BHP plans to double South Australian copper output by 2040
articles.summary:
BHP said on Monday it plans to double copper production from its Copper South Australia operations to 650,000 tonnes a year by 2040, according to an investor presentation reported by Investing.com. The ABC reported the plan would cost between $US14.2 billion and $US18.1 billion, with a final investment decision expected in the first half of 2027.

BHP said the South Australian operations would provide about a third of its planned copper growth to 2035, when it aims to produce about 2 million tonnes a year, up from about 1.4 million now. The company's shares rose about 2 per cent on the ASX on Monday.
keyFacts: Target of 650,000 tonnes of copper a year by 2040
Cost estimated at $US14.2–18.1 billion
Final investment decision expected in first half of 2027

articles.title: Death toll from Russian strike on apartment block in Dymer rises to at least 10
articles.summary:
The death toll from a Russian drone strike on a five-storey apartment building in Dymer, north of Kyiv, has risen to at least 10, Kyiv regional military administration head Tymur Tkachenko said on Monday, according to Ukrinform. Earlier reports had put the toll at four, and rescuers have pulled a child out alive.

AFP, via Gulf News, reported Ukraine's emergency service said 11 people, including two children, were unaccounted for during the search, and a teenager was among the dead. Tkachenko said a separate strike on a supermarket in Vyshneve killed two people and wounded eight. Italian agency LaPresse, citing the Kyiv Independent, later reported a toll of 11.
keyFacts: At least 10 dead in Dymer, regional head says
11 people, including two children, were missing
Separate supermarket strike in Vyshneve killed two

articles.title: Indonesia says 24 killed in sweets factory fire as search continues
articles.summary:
Indonesian authorities said 24 people were killed in Saturday's fire at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia confectionery factory in Banten province, up from an earlier toll of three, Reuters reported. Banten's search and rescue head said 24 body bags of remains had been recovered and about 30 people were still missing.

Police said DNA identification could take weeks and that a bag might hold remains of more than one person, so the final toll was unclear, according to Al Jazeera. A presidential labour adviser said preliminary reports pointed to an air-conditioner short circuit. The parent company, United Family Food, did not respond to Reuters' request for comment.
keyFacts: Toll rises from three to 24
About 30 people still missing
Preliminary reports point to an electrical fault

articles.title: Belgian airports shut for a day as unions strike against austerity
articles.summary:
Belgian air traffic controller Skeyes said it could not provide normal services from 7am to 9pm local time on Monday because of a national strike, with only emergency and safety-critical flights continuing, Al Jazeera reported. Brussels-Charleroi airport said the strike would shut all of the country's airports for the day.

Unions called the nationwide day of action against austerity measures, with a large demonstration planned in Brussels and possible disruption to transport, schools and public offices. Prime Minister Bart De Wever is negotiating a budget aimed at saving €10 billion. An airline group said it was the 11th strike to affect Belgian airspace in 11 months.
keyFacts: Air traffic services suspended from 7am to 9pm
Strike is against government austerity plans
Government seeking €10 billion in budget savings

articles.title: South Korea's Kospi falls as much as 5.8% as AI sell-off spreads to Asia
articles.summary:
Seoul's Kospi index fell as much as 5.8 per cent on Monday and was down 3.2 per cent at 04:30 GMT, after Friday's slump on Wall Street, Al Jazeera reported. Hong Kong's Hang Seng and China's CSI 300 each fell about 0.6 per cent, while Taiwan's Taiex rose 2.5 per cent after its worst week since 1991. Japan's markets were closed for a holiday.

The S&P 500 fell 3.7 per cent on Friday, entering a correction, and the Nasdaq dropped 5.3 per cent, according to the report. US stock futures were up more than 2 per cent during the Asian session.
keyFacts: Kospi fell as much as 5.8% during the session
Taiwan's Taiex rebounded 2.5%
US futures rose after Friday's losses

articles.title: ASX 200 falls for an eighth straight session as banks weigh on market
articles.summary:
The S&P/ASX 200 closed 0.3 per cent lower at 8,571 points on Monday, its eighth consecutive daily fall, the ABC reported. Banks were the largest drag, with Commonwealth Bank down 2.2 per cent and Westpac down 1.9 per cent, while miners gained, led by BHP.

AAP reported the local market had its worst week since 2022 last week, after a sell-off in technology shares linked to artificial intelligence. The Australian dollar rose to about 66.35 US cents, and gold was trading at about $US3,600 an ounce, according to the ABC.
keyFacts: ASX 200 closed down 0.3% at 8,571
Eighth straight session of losses
Banks fell while miners rose

articles.title: Australian factory activity contracts further in November, S&P Global survey shows
articles.summary:
S&P Global's flash manufacturing purchasing managers' index for Australia fell to 48.7 in November from 49.6 in October, RTTNews reported on Monday. A reading below 50 indicates contraction.

The survey showed new manufacturing orders fell for the first time in five months, at the sharpest rate since August 2021, and new business in the services sector also began to decline, according to RTTNews. The ABC reported the data came as UBS cut its 2027 growth forecast for Australia, and ahead of October inflation figures due on Wednesday.
keyFacts: Flash manufacturing PMI fell to 48.7 from 49.6
New orders fell at fastest pace since August 2021
October inflation data due Wednesday

articles.title: WHO says fighting near Congo hospital is putting Ebola patients and staff at risk
articles.summary:
World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said heavy fighting since Saturday near a hospital in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ituri province had disrupted the Ebola response and put patients and health workers at grave risk, Al Jazeera reported. He said medical staff had been sheltering in a maternity ward for more than 24 hours and that WHO was working to arrange their safe exit.

WHO figures as of 17 November showed 5,678 deaths from 11,613 Ebola cases in the country. The agency said on Saturday that high-level transmission was continuing, with Ituri and North Kivu the worst affected provinces.
keyFacts: Fighting near an Ituri hospital since Saturday
WHO records 5,678 deaths from 11,613 cases
Staff sheltering in a maternity ward, WHO says

articles.title: Woman in Nvidia scandal was in contact with China's spy agency, reports say
articles.summary:
Alice Huang, the woman at the centre of the scandal involving Nvidia's chief executive Jensen Huang, was in contact with an official from China's Ministry of State Security from spring 2025 until this autumn, ABC News in the US reported, citing sources familiar with US intelligence. The New York Times first reported the claims.

ABC said it was not clear whether US intelligence had evidence she passed on inside information. Her Singapore-based company, Megaspeed, was acquiring Nvidia chips during part of that period and has been under federal investigation since 2024, according to the sources. The White House and State Department did not immediately comment.
keyFacts: Contacts reportedly ran from spring 2025 to autumn 2026
Unclear if any inside information was passed on
Megaspeed under federal investigation since 2024, sources say

articles.title: Indonesia's Prabowo to nominate two vice-president candidates after Gibran's resignation
articles.summary:
Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto was set to submit the names of two vice-presidential candidates to parliament on Monday, state news agency Antara reported, citing an upper house deputy speaker, according to Reuters. The names had not been made public.

The nominations follow the resignation of Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka, the son of former president Joko Widodo, amid legal cases over the validity of his qualifications. Parliament is scheduled to choose the new vice-president on 11 December after vetting the two candidates, Reuters reported.
keyFacts: Two names to be sent to parliament on Monday
Follows resignation of Gibran Rakabuming Raka
Parliament to vote on 11 December

articles.title: South Korea's education minister resigns over university entrance exam cheating rules
articles.summary:
South Korea's Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned on Sunday, saying he took responsibility for confusion caused by last-minute measures against AI-assisted cheating in last week's national college entrance exam, Reuters reported. President Lee Jae Myung accepted the resignation and ordered a review of how national exams are managed.

The rules had been tightened after the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam said they had cheated using a miniature camera, a smartphone and AI, according to Reuters. More than 550,000 students registered for the entrance exam. Choi acknowledged preparation had been inadequate and rules had changed repeatedly.
keyFacts: Minister resigned on Sunday
President ordered review of exam management
More than 550,000 students registered for the exam

articles.title: China sets 2030 targets for aged care and childcare as population ages
articles.summary:
China's government has published a plan setting 2030 targets for aged care and childcare services, posted on the National Development and Reform Commission's website, Reuters reported. It aims for nursing care beds to make up 73 per cent of beds in aged care institutions and for community care to reach 70 per cent of older people, with about 2,000 public nursing homes to be renovated.

The plan also aims to extend childcare centres to all prefecture-level cities and raise enrolment of children under three by six percentage points from 2025 levels. Official data showed China's population fell for a fourth straight year in 2025, according to Reuters.
keyFacts: Targets set for 2030
About 2,000 public nursing homes to be renovated
Under-3 childcare enrolment to rise six points

articles.title: Israeli rights group reports 350% rise in incidents against West Bank medics
articles.summary:
Physicians for Human Rights Israel released a report on Monday documenting a 350 per cent increase in incidents involving Palestinian healthcare workers in the occupied West Bank between 2022 and 2024, which it attributed to Israeli soldiers and settlers, Al Jazeera reported. The report was based on interviews with 25 medics.

The incidents described include assaults, threats at gunpoint and searches, according to the report. Al Jazeera cited WHO figures recording 233 attacks on healthcare in the West Bank last year. The article did not include a response from the Israeli government or military, and the claims have not been independently verified.
keyFacts: Report cites 350% rise from 2022 to 2024
Based on interviews with 25 medics
No Israeli response included in the report coverage

articles.title: US intelligence chief defends Trump calling Putin a 'friend'
articles.summary:
US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said on Sunday that Russian President Vladimir Putin was not America's friend in Ukraine, while describing President Donald Trump's use of the word as appropriate for building rapport, Al Jazeera reported, citing AP. Clayton spoke on ABC's This Week and also told CNN he trusted Trump on the language he used.

Trump greeted Putin as "my friend" when he met him and Chinese President Xi Jinping at APEC in Shenzhen on 19 November. Outgoing Republican congressman Don Bacon criticised Trump's approach to Putin, according to the report.
keyFacts: Clayton says Putin is not America's friend in Ukraine
He called Trump's remarks appropriate
Trump met Putin and Xi at APEC on 19 November

articles.title: US Army moves to detonate lead azide stores in Iowa despite court pause on permit
articles.summary:
The US Army planned to detonate about 4.4 tonnes of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown on Monday, according to a state health department fact sheet cited by Al Jazeera. A federal appeals court paused the Environmental Protection Agency's emergency permit on Friday.

The Justice Department said in a filing that an emergency exception allowed the blasts to proceed, Al Jazeera reported. A court declaration said the material had dried out and formed crystals, raising the risk of explosion. Plaintiffs represented by Earthjustice say residents had about a week's notice and that lead dust could spread widely.
keyFacts: About 4.4 tonnes of lead azide set for detonation
Appeals court paused the EPA permit on Friday
Justice Department cites an emergency exception

articles.title: Taylor calls for Bowen to resign after COP31 ends without a deal
articles.summary:
Opposition Leader Angus Taylor said Climate and Energy Minister Chris Bowen should resign after the COP31 talks he co-led ended without an agreement, and said net zero should be scrapped, the ABC and Reuters reported. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese did not say whether he would remove Bowen.

Bowen said strongly held red lines among parties had prevented a deal. Reuters reported Australia spent about $150 million on its COP31 role. The Marshall Islands delegation said Pacific nations had been let down, and European negotiators said Saudi Arabia had led resistance to fossil fuel language, which the Turkish presidency said did not reflect preferential treatment.
keyFacts: Taylor says Bowen should resign
Albanese did not say whether Bowen would be moved
Australia spent about $150 million on COP31, Reuters says

articles.title: Independent MP Monique Ryan introduces bill for public register of lobbyist meetings
articles.summary:
Independent MP Monique Ryan introduced a private member's bill on Monday that would create a public register of meetings between lobbyists and ministers and public servants, with penalties for failing to disclose them, the ABC reported. Independent MP Kate Chaney and Senator Jacqui Lambie said they supported the bill.

Ryan has published her own meeting diary, according to the ABC. Private member's bills need government or opposition support to pass, and neither major party had announced a position on the proposal in the ABC's coverage.
keyFacts: Bill proposes a public register of lobbyist meetings
Penalties would apply for non-disclosure
Backed by Kate Chaney and Jacqui Lambie

articles.title: Low-risk small business websites to be exempt from digital duty of care laws
articles.summary:
Communications Minister Anika Wells confirmed that low-risk small business websites would be exempt from the government's proposed digital duty of care laws, the ABC reported on Monday. Business groups had said firms were unsure whether the laws, which carry penalties above $100 million, applied to them.

Greens senator Sarah Hanson-Young said she was optimistic about reaching a deal on the bill this week. The Greens want an amendment allowing individuals to sue technology companies, according to the ABC. Wells noted a parliamentary inquiry had backed considering such a right of action. It is the final sitting week of the year.
keyFacts: Low-risk small business sites to be exempt
Penalties under the laws exceed $100 million
Greens seek a right for individuals to sue

articles.title: COP31 climate talks in Antalya end without an agreement
articles.summary:
The COP31 climate summit in Antalya ended on Sunday without a final agreement, after a draft that did not mention fossil fuels was rejected about 44 hours after the scheduled close, the ABC reported. CBS News said European countries opposed the text, arguing it placated fuel exporters, while the ABC reported Russia and Saudi Arabia supported leaving fossil fuels out.

Australia's Climate Minister Chris Bowen, who co-led the talks with Türkiye, called the result "very disappointing". Ireland's climate minister said the talks had been taken over by some oil states. The ABC said the last UN climate talks to fail to reach a consensus deal were in Copenhagen in 2009.
keyFacts: Draft rejected about 44 hours after the summit's scheduled close
EU states refused a text that left out fossil fuels
Bowen called the outcome 'very disappointing'

articles.title: Government has four sitting days left to pass key bills before parliament's summer break
articles.summary:
Federal parliament returns on Monday for its last sitting week of 2026, with the government seeking to pass bills including a digital duty of care for online platforms and gas export reservation rules, AAP reported. The Greens want platforms fined 10 per cent of global revenue for breaches, while the Coalition says it will oppose the bill, calling it censorship.

AAP said Labor needs the opposition's support for the gas rules, which would let companies set aside up to 20 per cent of exports for local use. A Newspoll published in The Australian on Monday had Opposition Leader Angus Taylor ahead of Anthony Albanese as preferred prime minister for the first time, according to AAP.
keyFacts: Four sitting days remain before the summer break
Gas rules would reserve up to 20% of exports for local use
Newspoll has Taylor ahead as preferred PM for the first time

articles.title: Zelenskyy asks US to approve Patriot missile deliveries after strike on building near Kyiv
articles.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Sunday urged Washington to approve delivery of Patriot interceptor missiles, saying partners had already paid for them through a NATO-coordinated program, Al Jazeera reported. He said Russia fired about 2,700 attack drones, 1,460 guided bombs and 165 missiles at Ukraine over the past week.

A Russian strike early on Sunday partly collapsed a five-storey apartment building in Dymer, north of Kyiv. Rescuers recovered two bodies while searching for 11 missing people, according to Interfax citing Radio Liberty. Russia's defence ministry said it struck a cargo ship near Odesa and energy sites in Zaporizhzhia; those claims were not independently verified.
keyFacts: Zelenskyy says the missiles are paid for but await US approval
Two bodies recovered and 11 missing after Dymer strike
Russia says it hit a cargo ship near Odesa; not verified

articles.title: UKMTO reports tanker incident in Gulf of Oman; Iran says two tankers hit mines
articles.summary:
The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said on Sunday it had received a report of an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman and that investigations were under way, ABC News (US) reported. Separately, Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said, via state media, that two tankers on unauthorised routes struck sea mines north of Ghanem Island and stopped.

It was not confirmed whether the two reports referred to the same event. The incidents follow attacks on two tankers in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday reported by UKMTO, according to CBS News. No casualties had been reported in the Sunday incidents.
keyFacts: UKMTO says it is investigating a tanker incident
IRGC says two tankers hit mines north of Ghanem Island
Unclear whether the reports describe the same event

articles.title: Russian vessel hit by suspected sea drone at Benghazi naval base, eastern Libya says
articles.summary:
A suspected sea drone hit a Russian vessel at a naval base in Benghazi on Sunday, causing an explosion and a brief fire, according to Libya's eastern-based government, Al Jazeera reported. Reuters reported an unspecified number of people were injured.

The eastern administration said the ship had docked to refuel and take on supplies under a cooperation agreement with Russia, and that it had opened a joint investigation with Moscow into who was responsible. It said the fire was under control, called the attack a breach of Libya's sovereignty, and said Libya was not a party to the war between Russia and Ukraine. No group had claimed responsibility.
keyFacts: Explosion and brief fire on Russian vessel at Benghazi base
Eastern Libyan government and Russia open joint investigation
No claim of responsibility reported

articles.title: Drone attacks near Khartoum kill four and damage UN building, officials say
articles.summary:
Drone attacks blamed on Sudan's Rapid Support Forces killed four people in and around Khartoum early on Sunday and damaged a United Nations building, according to local reports and UN officials cited by Al Jazeera. A drone that hit a home in northern Omdurman killed three people and wounded nine, and a child was killed south of the capital.

UN humanitarian coordinator Denise Brown said a UN building was damaged while staff were inside, and the UN's humanitarian office called the danger to staff unacceptable. A Sudanese army source told AFP the drones were launched from Ethiopia; that claim was not independently verified, and Ethiopia has denied similar accusations before.
keyFacts: Four killed in drone attacks in and around Khartoum
UN building damaged with staff inside, UN says
Army source alleges drones came from Ethiopia; unverified

articles.title: Settlers burn cars in several West Bank villages; Eisenkot and Ben-Gvir dispute blame
articles.summary:
Israeli settlers attacked several Palestinian villages in the central occupied West Bank early on Sunday, burning 12 vehicles and spray-painting slogans in Ramallah and el-Bireh areas, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported, according to Al Jazeera. Incidents were reported in Kafr Malik, Deir Abu Mash'al and Deir al-Sudan.

Gadi Eisenkot, who has been asked to form Israel's next government, described the attacks as Jewish terrorism and blamed ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich. Ben-Gvir rejected that and said Eisenkot was jumping to conclusions. The Israeli military said police and forensic investigators were being sent to collect evidence.
keyFacts: Wafa reports 12 vehicles burned in Ramallah and el-Bireh areas
Eisenkot blamed far-right ministers; Ben-Gvir rejected it
Israeli military says investigators sent to the sites

articles.title: Houthis say Sanaa fuel station strike wounded six; Saudis say they intercepted a drone
articles.summary:
Houthi-run media said an air attack on a state oil company fuel station in Sanaa on Sunday wounded six employees, and a health ministry spokesperson said Saudi aircraft carried it out, Al Jazeera reported. The Saudi-led coalition did not comment on that claim.

Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said Saudi air defences destroyed a Houthi drone launched towards Riyadh, and hours earlier said a ballistic missile aimed at the western Red Sea coast region was intercepted. He reported no casualties. Saudi authorities say Houthi attacks have killed 26 people in the kingdom since September.
keyFacts: Houthi media say six wounded at a Sanaa fuel station
Coalition says it intercepted a drone and a ballistic missile
Saudi authorities say Houthi attacks have killed 26 since September

articles.title: Wong to frame AI as a national security challenge in major foreign policy speech
articles.summary:
Foreign Minister Penny Wong will deliver a foreign policy statement to parliament on Tuesday that treats artificial intelligence as a national security challenge, the ABC reported. The ABC said the speech, titled "Securing Australia's future in a changing world", effectively stands in for a foreign policy white paper, the last of which was released in 2017.

Wong will say AI makes foreign interference faster, cheaper and harder to detect, citing reported Iranian and Russian influence operations. She will also say Australia is strengthening cyber resilience and legislating mandatory AI safety standards. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke has said data centre ownership structures are a national security concern.
keyFacts: Speech to parliament scheduled for Tuesday
ABC says it effectively replaces a foreign policy white paper
Wong to cite AI-enabled foreign interference

articles.title: Lowy index finds US lead over China in Asia at its narrowest; Australia drops to sixth
articles.summary:
The Lowy Institute's 2026 Asia Power Index found the gap between the United States and China at its narrowest, with the authors attributing a record fall in US diplomatic influence partly to the war with Iran, the ABC reported. China ranked ahead of the US on economic relationships and diplomatic influence.

The index's authors wrote that the change owed more to US missteps than to gains by Beijing, while researcher Jack Sato said the US still holds a clear overall lead. Australia slipped one place to sixth, behind Russia. India rose to third, and Indonesia recorded the region's steepest fall in diplomatic influence, according to the report.
keyFacts: US-China gap narrowest on record, Lowy says
China ahead on economic ties and diplomatic influence
Australia falls one place to sixth

articles.title: Lebanon's president demands Israeli withdrawal and criticises Iranian interference
articles.summary:
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun said on Saturday that Lebanon faces Israeli occupation and interference from influential parties in Iran's government, in a speech on the eve of the country's independence anniversary, Al Jazeera reported. He demanded Israel withdraw from all Lebanese territory, stop attacks and return captives.

Aoun also told armed groups to hand over their weapons and pledged to bring all arms under state control. Al Jazeera said a June framework agreement between Lebanon and Israel has stalled, with Hezbollah refusing to disarm and Israel continuing strikes, including in Nabatieh, Bint Jbeil and Marjayoun districts on Saturday.
keyFacts: Aoun demands Israeli withdrawal from all Lebanese territory
He accused parts of Iran's government of interference
June Lebanon-Israel framework deal has stalled

articles.title: Gas exporters split at Senate hearing on plan to reserve gas for local use
articles.summary:
Gas exporters gave differing accounts of their domestic supply records at a Senate committee hearing on the government's gas reservation bill, the ABC reported. Under the plan, exporters must supply up to 20 per cent of annual production locally, targeting 110 per cent of forecast demand.

APLNG said it had supplied more than 1,900 petajoules to the domestic market, and Santos said it supplied the equivalent of 26 per cent of its export volumes to the east coast. Shell said must-sell provisions were unnecessary. The Grattan Institute said the 110 per cent target was too high. Senator David Pocock said the bill had loopholes; Santos rejected his argument.
keyFacts: Bill would require up to 20% of production for local supply
Exporters disputed each other's domestic supply records
Pocock says bill has loopholes; Santos disagrees

articles.title: Timor-Leste says Chinese and Russian firms interested in Greater Sunrise gas project
articles.summary:
Timor-Leste's government says Russian and Chinese companies have shown interest in developing the Greater Sunrise gas field, about 500 kilometres north of Darwin, the ABC reported. Woodside sold its 33.4 per cent stake back to Timor-Leste last month, giving the government full control.

Petroleum Minister Francisco da Costa Monteiro said the field could be developed soon, and the government plans to fund it with 30 per cent equity and 70 per cent project finance. Energy analyst Saul Kavonic told the ABC the field was not commercially viable and a Russian role was unlikely. Past estimates put development costs between $US14.1 billion and $US20.5 billion.
keyFacts: Field lies about 500km north of Darwin
Woodside sold its 33.4% stake to Timor-Leste last month
Analyst says the project is not commercially viable

articles.title: Three dead and 36 missing after fire at Indonesian sweets factory
articles.summary:
A fire at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia confectionery factory in Banten province, near Jakarta, killed at least three workers and left 36 unaccounted for, officials said on Sunday, according to the ABC and Al Jazeera. The fire started on Saturday afternoon at the plant, which makes Milkita products.

Indonesia's search and rescue agency said 15 people had been rescued, four of whom were taken to hospital. A rescue official told AP the fire was still burning in several places more than 12 hours after it began. Survivors told local media it started near a cooling unit on the third floor, and authorities said the cause was under investigation.
keyFacts: At least three killed and 36 missing, officials say
15 people rescued, four taken to hospital
Cause under investigation

articles.title: COP31 presidency releases final text for approval as talks run two days over time
articles.summary:
Organisers of the COP31 climate talks in Antalya released what they called a final deal text early on Sunday, after negotiations ran past the Friday deadline, Reuters reported via RTÉ. COP31 president Murat Kurum told a late-night plenary he believed all parties could agree on the text, and said concerns over fossil fuels and adaptation finance had been addressed.

The ABC reported the text keeps a call to electrify the global economy but does not name fossil fuels. Delegations had until 0300 GMT to object, with an approval session set for Sunday morning in Antalya. The African Group of Negotiators said it was disappointed with several outcomes, according to MyJoyOnline. Any deal needs consensus.
keyFacts: Final text released early Sunday after talks overran by two days
ABC reports the text does not name fossil fuels
Approval session set for Sunday morning, Antalya time

articles.title: Bahrain says Iranian attack caused fire at industrial site; Iran says it targeted US bases
articles.summary:
Bahrain's Defence Force said its air defences intercepted a number of Iranian aerial attacks late on Saturday, Al Jazeera reported. The Interior Ministry said one attack caused a fire and material damage at a civilian industrial facility, with no injuries.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted US positions at the al-Riffa and Awali bases and claimed to have destroyed two US Patriot radars, according to Al Jazeera. Bahrain and the US military did not confirm that claim, Euronews reported. Euronews also said maritime agency UKMTO reported two tankers struck by projectiles while leaving the Gulf. Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi called the US blockade of Iran an act of war.
keyFacts: Bahrain says it intercepted several Iranian attacks late Saturday
Fire at a civilian industrial facility; no injuries reported
IRGC claim of destroyed Patriot radars not confirmed by Bahrain or US

articles.title: Russian cargo ship hit by drones in Gulf of Finland; Finland says Ukraine likely behind it
articles.summary:
The Russian cargo ship Sparta II caught fire after being hit by drones in international waters west of Gogland island on Saturday, Finland's Defence Forces said, according to the ABC and Reuters via SBS. The ship, bound for Kaliningrad, later drifted into Finnish waters. Its 16 crew left in lifeboats and were taken aboard a Russian vessel.

A Finnish armed forces spokesperson said Ukraine was likely responsible. Ukraine had not commented in the reports. The ABC said the ship is under US sanctions. Finland imposed temporary air and sea restrictions in the eastern Gulf of Finland, and Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said the war was spilling into neighbouring areas. Estonia sent a navy vessel to help.
keyFacts: Sparta II hit by drones west of Gogland island
All 16 crew evacuated
Finland imposed temporary air and maritime restrictions

articles.title: NATO's Rutte pledges to defend Poland; alliance council to discuss missile incident Monday
articles.summary:
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said in Warsaw on Saturday that the alliance would defend Poland, after Polish authorities said Russian missiles came down in the country's south-east on Friday, AFP reported via CP24. The new development is that NATO's North Atlantic Council will discuss the incident on Monday.

Rutte said NATO would establish what happened and look for any gaps in defences. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Poland would ask NATO to strengthen detection and surveillance, and Warsaw has called the incident an intentional provocation. The Kremlin had not commented on the incident in earlier AFP reports. The US-based Institute for the Study of War said it believed Russia fired the weapons deliberately.
keyFacts: Rutte visited Warsaw on Saturday
North Atlantic Council to discuss the incident on Monday
Tusk to ask NATO for stronger detection and surveillance

articles.title: UN weapons talks agree to work on autonomous weapons rules within two years
articles.summary:
Countries at the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons in Geneva agreed on Friday to 'elaborate' an instrument on lethal autonomous weapons within two years, Al Jazeera reported, citing AFP. The Globe and Mail said the target date is 2028.

Nearly 100 countries had pushed for binding rules to be adopted quickly, but the United States, Russia and Israel opposed this, and decisions require consensus, Al Jazeera reported. Swiss chair Julien Thoeni said some countries rejected the word 'negotiate'. The Stop Killer Robots coalition called the mandate watered down, and Human Rights Watch called the outcome disappointing. Supporters of the decision said it keeps talks going.
keyFacts: CCW members agreed to elaborate an instrument within two years
US, Russia and Israel opposed fast adoption of binding rules
Decisions at the CCW require consensus

articles.title: Eleven killed in violence during capture of Mexican cartel leader, officials say
articles.summary:
Mexico's Defence Ministry said at least 11 people were killed in violence surrounding the capture of alleged cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in Sinaloa, according to Al Jazeera and The Times of Israel. The ministry said the dead were seven gunmen and four soldiers. The capture was reported earlier; the death toll is new.

Meza Flores, known as "Chapo Isidro", is on the FBI's ten most wanted list and faces charges in Mexico and the US. Mexican officials said US intelligence assisted the operation but gave few details, The Times of Israel reported.
keyFacts: At least 11 killed, according to Mexico's Defence Ministry
Ministry says seven gunmen and four soldiers died
Meza Flores is on the FBI's ten most wanted list

articles.title: Gaza authorities say nine killed in 48 hours as displaced residents protest
articles.summary:
Gaza's Health Ministry said at least nine people were killed over 48 hours, taking the death toll since the October 2025 ceasefire to 1,661, Al Jazeera reported. Displaced residents near the so-called Yellow Line protested on Saturday as Israeli air strikes continued, according to Al Jazeera's correspondent.

Gaza's housing ministry said 350,000 families are homeless. A local mayor in central Gaza said more than 500 housing units in his area had been destroyed in under a month and described it as gradual displacement. Gaza's civil defence said it had recovered 129 bodies and remains. Israel's military has said previous strikes targeted militants; it was not quoted on these figures.
keyFacts: Health Ministry: nine killed in 48 hours
Toll since October 2025 ceasefire put at 1,661
Housing ministry says 350,000 families are homeless

articles.title: Wall Street closes sharply lower as Nasdaq falls more than 5% and Nvidia drops 14%
articles.summary:
US shares fell heavily on Friday, with the Nasdaq closing down more than 5 per cent and the S&P 500 down 3.7 per cent, according to AFP via SBS News. Nvidia shares closed 14.01 per cent lower. The close confirms the S&P 500's seventh straight losing session, reported earlier as under way.

Anthropic shares, priced at US$83 in their initial public offering, closed below US$89 after trading above US$110 on Thursday, AFP reported. ABC News said the S&P 500 is now in a correction, more than 10 per cent below its 6 October record. Analysts cited by AFP pointed to doubts about returns on AI spending and a US move to restrict Chinese remote access to Nvidia chips.
keyFacts: Nasdaq closed down more than 5%, S&P 500 down 3.7%
Nvidia closed 14.01% lower
Anthropic shares closed below US$89, versus a US$83 IPO price

articles.title: Poland says Russian cruise missile landed on its territory during strikes on Ukraine
articles.summary:
A Russian Kh-101 cruise missile came down on farmland near Nowy Lipowiec in south-eastern Poland on Friday morning, Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said, according to reports cited by The Daily Caller. Polish authorities said a second suspected missile and a drone also entered Polish airspace. No injuries were reported.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the incident was a deliberate provocation and that Warsaw was certain the weapons came from Russia, AFP reported via SBS News. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte described it as dangerous, according to the BBC. The Kremlin had not commented, AFP said. The incident happened during a large Russian missile and drone attack on Ukraine.
keyFacts: Kh-101 missile landed near Nowy Lipowiec, officials say
Tusk called it a deliberate provocation
No injuries reported; Kremlin had not commented

articles.title: Nvidia shares fall 14% after report SEC is examining possible accounting issues
articles.summary:
Nvidia shares closed 14.01 per cent lower on Friday, AFP reported via SBS News, after Reuters reported that US Securities and Exchange Commission enforcement staff were examining potential accounting issues at the company. Reuters cited two people briefed on the matter and could not determine when the inquiry began or its scope, according to 24/7 Wall St.

The SEC declined to comment and Nvidia did not immediately respond, 24/7 Wall St reported. The Wall Street Journal had reported earlier in the week that the SEC was investigating whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors. The company has been led by interim chief executive Colette Kress since Jensen Huang resigned on 12 November.
keyFacts: Reuters reported SEC staff examining potential accounting issues
SEC declined to comment
Nvidia closed down 14.01% on Friday

articles.title: UK and EU sign deals on youth mobility, food trade and carbon markets at Brussels summit
articles.summary:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and EU leaders signed agreements on youth mobility, agri-food trade and linking carbon markets at a summit in Brussels on Friday, ABC News reported. The deals still need approval from the UK and EU parliaments.

Under the youth scheme, 100,000 young people from each side could live, work or study on the other side each year, according to ABC News and Xinhua. The food deal aims to remove most routine border checks from March 2028. The UK government estimates the deals could add up to 0.5 per cent to GDP by 2040. Burnham said rejoining the EU was not off the table. Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said Burnham had no mandate for the deal.
keyFacts: 100,000 young people a year from each side under youth scheme
Food checks to be removed from March 2028
Deals still need parliamentary approval

articles.title: Taiwan's share index falls almost 18% in its worst week since 1991
articles.summary:
Taiwan's benchmark TAIEX index fell 6.23 per cent on Friday, taking its loss for the week to almost 18 per cent, its worst week since 1991, the Taipei Times reported, citing Bloomberg. The index, which is more than 70 per cent technology stocks, has fallen more than a quarter from its 6 October record.

Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission has tightened short-selling rules twice this month, most recently cutting the cap on intraday short-sale orders to 1 per cent of 30-day average volume, according to the report. Global funds have sold a net US$56 billion of Taiwanese shares this quarter. AFP reported that markets in Tokyo and Seoul also fell between 5 and 6.2 per cent on Friday.
keyFacts: TAIEX fell 6.23% on Friday, almost 18% for the week
Regulator tightened short-selling curbs twice this month
Index more than 25% below its October record

articles.title: French Senate gives final approval to law presuming police shootings are lawful
articles.summary:
The French Senate voted 205 to 110 on Friday to give final approval to a law presuming that police officers who use their weapons acted lawfully unless there is proof otherwise, Reuters reported. Critics have described it as a "licence to kill".

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the government supports the law to protect officers working in dangerous conditions, according to Reuters. Left-wing parliamentarians said they would refer it to the Constitutional Council. A UN special rapporteur wrote to French authorities warning it could fuel impunity. Rights groups, unions and some lawmakers said it would lead to more deaths, while supporters said it gives officers appropriate legal protection.
keyFacts: Senate vote 205 to 110
Left-wing MPs plan Constitutional Council challenge
UN rapporteur raised impunity concerns

articles.title: Denmark expels Russian defence attache over alleged plot to kill Ukrainian rapper
articles.summary:
Denmark is expelling Russia's defence attache, Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said on Friday, after the Danish intelligence service PET said it suspected Russian intelligence of planning to kill a Ukrainian rapper at a concert near Copenhagen, Al Jazeera reported, citing AFP. The attache has seven days to leave.

PET said three people were stopped in a car near the venue, where police found firearms and knives. Two people have been charged with attempted murder and assisting a foreign intelligence service. Police suspect a banned gang helped plan the alleged attack. Russia's embassy called the expulsion vengeful and said no evidence of Russian involvement had been presented.
keyFacts: Russian defence attache given seven days to leave
Two charged with attempted murder
Russia's embassy says no evidence was presented

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted three missiles fired at Riyadh
articles.summary:
The Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government said it intercepted three ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh overnight, Al Jazeera reported. Emergency alerts were issued for the capital and southern Saudi Arabia.

The attack followed coalition strikes on Friday on Houthi-held sites, including Sanaa and the port of Hodeidah, and came days after Houthi missiles hit the Public Investment Fund tower, the country's tallest building, according to Al Jazeera. The Houthis have threatened Saudi Arabia's financial district and Red Sea ports including Jeddah.
