The Houthis had not commented on the interceptions in Al Jazeera's report, and no damage was reported.
keyFacts: Three ballistic missiles intercepted, coalition says
Emergency alerts issued for Riyadh and the south
Follows coalition strikes on Hodeidah and Sanaa

articles.title: Paris court sentences three police officers over 2020 racist assault on music producer
articles.summary:
A Paris criminal court on Friday sentenced three police officers over the 2020 assault on music producer Michel Zecler, finding racism was an aggravating factor, Al Jazeera reported, citing AFP. Each received five years, with between three and four years suspended.

Security footage recorded the assault outside Zecler's Paris studio in November 2020. The court found his account consistent and said a falsified police report damaged the officers' credibility, according to the report. The officers had said Zecler was not wearing a mask and had tried to grab a weapon. Zecler's lawyer said justice had been done. AFP noted guilty verdicts in police violence cases are rare in France.
keyFacts: Three officers each sentenced to five years, partly suspended
Court found racism an aggravating factor
Assault was filmed in November 2020

articles.title: ABC says IDF gave no evidence for claim its former Gaza freelancer was a Hamas operative
articles.summary:
The ABC says the Israel Defense Forces has not provided evidence for its claim that Roshdi Al Sarraj, a Gaza freelancer engaged by the ABC in 2023, was a Hamas operative, despite repeated requests since 3 October. Al Sarraj was killed in an Israeli air strike in October 2023.

The IDF listed him as a Hamas operative in October 2026. An initial IDF reply cited Palestinian Islamic Jihad before being edited to say Hamas, the ABC reported. The IDF says a redacted document reported by The Australian shows him as a Hamas squad deputy commander; the ABC said it could not verify it. The Committee to Protect Journalists said its investigation found no evidence he was a combatant.
keyFacts: IDF alleges Al Sarraj was a Hamas operative
ABC says requests for evidence went unanswered
CPJ found no evidence he was a combatant

articles.title: Russia launches hundreds of drones and missiles at Ukraine, killing at least 12 over a day
articles.summary:
Russia launched 404 drones and 84 cruise missiles at Ukraine overnight into Friday, along with ballistic and hypersonic missiles, the Kyiv Independent reported, citing Ukraine's Air Force. The Air Force said 462 weapons were intercepted or suppressed. Ukrainian officials said attacks over the past day killed 12 people and injured 82.

In Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said a ballistic missile damaged the Podilskyi Bridge and two other bridges were hit, according to AP. The Energy Ministry said power plants and substations were struck. The attack came hours after Vladimir Putin said Russia would respond to Ukrainian strikes on the Kerch Bridge to Crimea.
keyFacts: 404 drones and 84 cruise missiles launched, Ukraine says
Three Kyiv bridges damaged, according to the mayor
12 killed and 82 injured across Ukraine over a day

articles.title: COP31 talks run past deadline as countries split over fossil fuel wording
articles.summary:
UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, went past their scheduled Friday close with no agreed text, Reuters and AFP reported. A draft released on Thursday removed references to moving away from fossil fuels and dropped a $US120 billion adaptation finance target, according to Reuters.

AFP said about a dozen countries, including France and Panama, wrote calling for a clear transition away from fossil fuels, and an EU official said the draft was not ambitious enough. Reuters reported Saudi Arabia and other producers had objected to the earlier wording. Australia's Chris Bowen, who is presiding over negotiations, said he would keep working for as long as needed.
keyFacts: Talks continued past the Friday deadline
Latest draft omits fossil fuel transition language
Draft dropped $US120 billion adaptation finance target

articles.title: S&P 500 heads for seventh straight loss as chip stocks fall sharply
articles.summary:
The S&P 500 was down 2.2 per cent in Friday afternoon trading in New York, about 10 per cent below its 6 October record and on track for a seventh straight daily fall, AP reported. The Nasdaq was down 3.6 per cent and the Dow 0.7 per cent.

AP said chipmakers led the decline, with AMD and Broadcom each down more than 10 per cent and Nvidia down about 7 per cent. Anthropic shares were down about 11 per cent but remained above the $US83 IPO price, according to AP. The 10-year US Treasury yield fell to 4.94 per cent. Reuters reported markets were pricing a December Fed rate rise as near certain.
keyFacts: S&P 500 down 2.2% in afternoon trade
Index about 10% below its October record
Nasdaq down 3.6% as chip stocks fell

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition strikes Houthi targets including Hodeidah port
articles.summary:
The Saudi-led coalition said on Friday it struck Houthi weapons and smuggling targets, including at Yemen's Red Sea port of Hodeidah, and carried out operations in Sanaa, AP reported. Al Jazeera said the coalition also cited operations in Saada and Taiz, and its correspondent in Sanaa described the strikes as the heaviest of the conflict.

The coalition said it intercepted five drones and a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis, with Riyadh among the targets, according to AP. The Houthis threatened to attack Saudi Red Sea ports including Jeddah if Hodeidah was struck, and warned airlines to avoid most Saudi airspace, Al Jazeera reported.
keyFacts: Coalition says it hit targets at Hodeidah and in Sanaa
Coalition says five drones and a missile intercepted
Houthis threaten Saudi ports including Jeddah

articles.title: Australia and China agree to hold talks on artificial intelligence
articles.summary:
Australia and China have agreed to hold talks on artificial intelligence, ABC News reported. The agreement came from a meeting in Beijing on Friday night between Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Premier Li Qiang, which also covered trade, climate, health and tourism.

Earlier on Friday Albanese met President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on the sidelines of APEC. Separately, Australia signed a technology declaration with the United States aimed at protecting AI supply chains from Chinese interference, according to the ABC. Albanese is due back in Australia on Saturday after 11 days overseas covering COP31, the ASEAN summit in Manila and APEC.
keyFacts: Agreement followed Albanese's meeting with Li Qiang
Australia also signed an AI supply chain declaration with the US
Albanese returns after 11 days overseas

articles.title: France seeks UN Security Council meeting after strikes damage embassies in Kyiv
articles.summary:
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said France is seeking a UN Security Council meeting after Russian attacks on Kyiv killed civilians and damaged the Austrian and Dutch embassy buildings, European Pravda reported. Barrot said Russia would have to answer for the attacks.

Africanews, citing AFP and AP, said staff at both embassies were unhurt in Thursday's strikes. Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen said the Dutch embassy was hit by a projectile. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the EU would summon Russia's ambassador, according to European Pravda. Russia's embassy in the Netherlands had accused The Hague of taking part in the war, Africanews reported.
keyFacts: France requests a UN Security Council meeting
Austrian and Dutch embassies damaged; no staff hurt
EU to summon Russia's ambassador, Kallas says

articles.title: Trump says US firms building AI data centres overseas will face a tax
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump said on Friday that American technology companies building AI data centres in other countries would face what he called a tremendous tax, AP reported. He gave no details and said he had not yet told his own officials about the plan.

Trump also urged communities to accept data centres and to seek concessions from developers, according to AP and Spectrum News. Spectrum said the Senate passed bipartisan permitting legislation on Thursday, which now goes to the House. AP noted data centres were a significant issue in the midterm elections. Google and Meta say they are being more open with communities, according to the reports.
keyFacts: Trump announced no details of the proposed tax
He said officials had not yet been told
Senate passed permitting bill on Thursday

articles.title: Gaza civil defence says Israeli strikes killed six people on Friday
articles.summary:
Israeli strikes killed six people in Gaza on Friday, according to Gaza's civil defence agency, AFP reported. Spokesman Mahmoud Bassal said four died in a strike south-west of Bureij refugee camp, one in a drone strike on a tent in Deir al-Balah and one north of Nuseirat.

The Israeli military told AFP it had targeted several militants. The strikes followed an Israeli tank operation in central Gaza that the army said was aimed at a tunnel. AFP's tally puts Palestinian deaths since the October 2025 ceasefire at more than 1,600. Israel's military says seven soldiers and one civilian contractor have been killed in that period.
keyFacts: Civil defence reports six killed in three locations
Israeli military says it targeted militants
AFP tally: more than 1,600 Palestinians killed since ceasefire

articles.title: Russian diesel tankers sent under US deal arrive in Brazil instead
articles.summary:
Tankers carrying Russian diesel sent under a fuel arrangement between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin have arrived in Brazil rather than the United States, The Moscow Times and Kyiv Post reported, citing The Maritime Executive. The Moscow Times said US buyers declined the cargoes over sanctions risks.

The Leruo and Primorye anchored at Itacoatiara on the Amazon, and a third tanker, Beast, was listed as bound for Brazil, according to the reports. Kyiv Post said Trump announced the deal on 9 October, promising more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel. The US Treasury has authorised related transactions until April 2027, Kyiv Post reported.
keyFacts: Two tankers anchored at Itacoatiara, Brazil
Each vessel carries about 40,000 tonnes
US buyers declined cargoes over sanctions risks, report says

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan crosses India's Odisha coast; officials report no deaths
articles.summary:
Cyclone Akvan made landfall near Gopalpur in India's Odisha state on Friday and weakened into a deep depression by the afternoon, according to the India Meteorological Department, PTI reported. Odisha's Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said no major damage or deaths had been reported.

Chief Secretary Anu Garg said about 372,000 people had been moved to shelters, according to PTI. The state deployed 423 rescue teams. Railways cancelled dozens of trains, and tourists were barred from coastal areas including Puri and Gopalpur. The IMD said rain would ease from Saturday, with an orange alert in place for 14 districts.
keyFacts: Landfall near Gopalpur completed by late morning
About 372,000 people moved to shelters
No deaths reported, state minister says

articles.title: Pakistani minister visits India for first time since 2025 conflict
articles.summary:
Pakistan's climate change minister Musadik Malik arrived in New Delhi on Friday, the first visit by a Pakistani federal minister since the two countries' four-day conflict in May 2025, Al Jazeera reported. He is attending a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation dialogue forum that Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi was due to open.

Neither government has announced a bilateral meeting, according to Al Jazeera. Pakistan's Foreign Office said its participation reflected its role as an SCO member. India's foreign ministry said its policy towards Pakistan was unchanged. India's suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty remains in place, the report said.
keyFacts: First Pakistani federal minister in India since May 2025
Visit is for an SCO forum in New Delhi
No bilateral meeting announced

articles.title: Spanish court grants bail to US activist facing extradition over alleged Hamas funding
articles.summary:
Spain's High Court granted conditional bail to American activist James "Fergie" Chambers, who left Aranjuez prison near Madrid on Friday after nearly five months in custody, Al Jazeera and Reuters reported. The United States is seeking his extradition over the alleged laundering of $US7.5 million that it says went to Tunisia and supported Hamas.

Chambers is not charged with terrorism and denies wrongdoing, according to the report. His lawyer said the US had acknowledged translation errors in an FBI affidavit, which the court said could delay a decision. Chambers has applied for asylum and cannot be extradited while that claim is pending.
keyFacts: Released on conditional bail after nearly five months
US alleges $US7.5 million was laundered
Pending asylum claim blocks extradition for now

articles.title: Xi tells Albanese China-Australia ties have seen a 'full turnaround'
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on Friday on the sidelines of APEC, their fifth formal meeting, AAP reported. According to AAP, Xi congratulated Albanese for leading a "full turnaround" in relations. Xinhua's readout said ties were developing steadily, AFP reported.

Albanese said both countries had worked to stabilise the relationship and would not be defined by their differences, according to AFP. AAP said no agreements were reported. Albanese is due in Beijing for talks with Premier Li Qiang and a business roundtable, where Australian firms are seeking wider market access, including for beef, which faces a 55 per cent tariff above China's quota, AAP said.
keyFacts: Fifth formal meeting between Albanese and Xi
No agreements reported from the Shenzhen talks
Talks with Premier Li Qiang to follow in Beijing

articles.title: Trump says decision on new Iran strikes can wait until next year
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump indicated he would not decide on renewed major strikes on Iran until next year, Reuters reported on Thursday (US time). He told Reuters he would discuss it after the start of the year and told Fox News, "We'll see what happens after January 1". He told Axios and Israel's Channel 12 he was not rushing.

Iran's Foreign Ministry said US claims that Iran was developing chemical and biological weapons were an attempt to justify military action, Reuters said. Gulf News, citing Axios, said options under discussion for a joint US-Israeli operation included strikes on suspected nuclear sites. A Pentagon official put the war's cost at $US48.3 billion as of 13 November.
keyFacts: Trump points to a decision after 1 January
Iran rejects US claims about weapons programs
Pentagon puts war cost at $US48.3 billion

articles.title: ASX 200 falls for seventh straight day, down about 5 per cent for the week
articles.summary:
Australian shares fell for a seventh consecutive session on Friday, with all 11 sectors lower, AAP reported. At lunchtime the S&P/ASX 200 was down 1.17 per cent at 8,625.2, according to AAP. IBTimes reported the index at 8,594.2 in the afternoon, down 1.56 per cent and about 5.4 per cent for the week. AAP said it was likely the worst week since early 2020.

Analysts cited weakness on Wall Street and in AI-related stocks, which Anthropic's share debut did not reverse, AAP said. Technology shares fell about 5 per cent and gold was near a 14-month low. Monash IVF fell more than 20 per cent after a trading update, AAP reported. The Australian dollar was near 66.5 US cents.
keyFacts: Seventh straight daily fall for the ASX 200
Weekly loss of about 5 per cent
Technology sector down about 5 per cent on Friday

articles.title: US Senate rejects resolution to end US involvement in Iran war, 51-48
articles.summary:
The US Senate on Thursday voted 51-48 against a war powers resolution that would have directed President Trump to withdraw US forces from hostilities with Iran, Reuters reported via Al Jazeera. The House passed a similar measure 220-204 in September. Republicans Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Rand Paul voted in favour and Democrat John Fetterman voted against.

Democratic Senator Tim Kaine said the 3 November midterm results showed the war was unpopular. Republicans who opposed the measure restated their support for the military campaign, according to the report. Republicans control the Senate until 3 January, when the new Congress, in which Democrats won both chambers, begins, Reuters said.
keyFacts: Senate vote was 51-48 against the resolution
Three Republicans backed it; one Democrat opposed
New Congress begins on 3 January

articles.title: US approved licences for about 879,000 AI chips to China, House data shows
articles.summary:
The US Commerce Department approved exports of about 879,000 advanced Nvidia and AMD chips to Chinese companies between December 2025 and May 2026, according to licensing data released by the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Reuters reported. Approvals included 150,000 chips for Tencent and 75,000 for Alibaba. Companies had sought to ship 3.4 million chips. It is unclear how many shipments took place.

Former US official Chris McGuire said more than 30 per cent went to firms the Pentagon lists as Chinese military companies, raising questions about the security review. Nvidia said approvals carried strict conditions and limited volumes and that it has stopped shipping H200 chips to China. AMD did not respond, Reuters said.
keyFacts: About 879,000 chip export licences approved
Committee chair Brian Mast released the data
Nvidia says it has stopped H200 shipments to China

articles.title: Japan's Nikkei drops more than 4 per cent as AI share sell-off spreads
articles.summary:
Japan's Nikkei 225 fell more than 4 per cent in early trading on Friday, following overnight losses on Wall Street, Xinhua and Reuters reported. Xinhua said that at 10am Tokyo time the index was down 2,505.50 points, or 4.21 per cent, at 56,938.71, while the broader Topix was down 1.76 per cent.

Xinhua said concern about AI-related stocks continued to weigh on sentiment. Reuters reported the Nikkei down 4.28 per cent at 56,899.52 at one point, with technology stocks tracking declines in the US. On Wall Street on Thursday, Nvidia fell 3.3 per cent and AMD 7.7 per cent, according to Reuters reporting carried by Al Jazeera.
keyFacts: Nikkei down about 4.2 per cent in early trade
Topix down 1.76 per cent
Losses followed falls in US tech shares

articles.title: US appeals court lets Trump end deportation protections for Venezuelans
articles.summary:
A US appeals court has allowed the Trump administration, for now, to end Temporary Protected Status for Venezuelans, which covers about 600,000 people, Al Jazeera reported, citing Reuters and AP. The status shields holders from deportation. The decision does not end the underlying legal challenges, and the administration has also filed an emergency request with the Supreme Court.

The administration says the protection was always meant to be temporary and that conditions in Venezuela have improved since the US operation in January that removed Nicolás Maduro. Rights advocates say his government remains largely in place, according to the report. The US State Department continues to advise against travel to Venezuela.
keyFacts: About 600,000 Venezuelans hold TPS
Ruling lets the protections lapse for now
Underlying legal challenges continue

articles.title: One Nation pledges to scrap Victoria's climate department and VNI West
articles.summary:
One Nation would abolish the climate change section of Victoria's energy and environment department if it formed government, Barnaby Joyce said while campaigning in Kerang on Friday, the ABC reported. He said a royal commission would examine renewable energy deals and refer any suspected corruption to prosecutors.

Joyce also said One Nation would seek to revoke approved permits for the VNI West transmission line and build new coal-fired power stations, according to the ABC. Energy Minister Jaclyn Symes has previously said the government could have worked more closely with affected communities on the line, the ABC said. Victorians vote on 28 November.
keyFacts: Pledge to abolish the climate change department
Royal commission into renewable energy deals proposed
Party would seek to revoke VNI West permits

articles.title: Judge lets Trump's defamation suit against NYT and Penguin Random House proceed
articles.summary:
A federal judge in Tampa, Florida, ruled on Thursday that Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against The New York Times and Penguin Random House can go ahead, Reuters reported via Al Jazeera. Judge Steven Merryday dismissed two of Trump's claims but found the rest plausibly alleged defamation.

The suit cites statements in a book by Peter Baker and articles by Susanne Craig and Russ Buettner, which Trump says were false and aimed at harming his 2024 campaign. The Times and Penguin deny defaming him and argued that some statements were opinion and that the suit was legally flawed, according to the report. Press freedom groups have criticised Trump's lawsuits against media outlets.
keyFacts: Judge Steven Merryday allowed most claims to proceed
Two of Trump's claims were dismissed
Defendants deny defamation

articles.title: Democrats say law firm gave Trump administration $US11.8m in free legal work
articles.summary:
Democratic lawmakers Jamie Raskin, Richard Blumenthal and Adam Schiff said law firm Kirkland & Ellis has provided at least $US11.8 million in free legal services to the Trump administration, Reuters reported via Al Jazeera. They said the work went to agencies including the Commerce and Defense departments and called it evidence of coercion of major law firms.

Kirkland said in a November letter, obtained by Reuters, that its agreement with the White House had had little impact on its pro bono work. Its lawyer did not respond to Reuters. The Democrats said they had sought records from nine other firms. The three are due to lead investigations when the new Congress begins on 3 January.
keyFacts: Democrats cite at least $US11.8m in free services
Kirkland says the deal had little impact on pro bono work
Records sought from nine other firms

articles.title: Four dead after migrant boat capsizes off Senegal as Canaries arrivals rise
articles.summary:
Four bodies were recovered after a migrant boat capsized near Yenne, south of Dakar, Boubacar Seye of the group Horizons Sans Frontieres told Reuters, as reported by Al Jazeera. A local official said at least 50 people were on board. Searches continued and the number missing was unclear.

Spain's Interior Ministry said 24,364 migrants reached the Canary Islands between 1 January and 15 November, up from 14,690 a year earlier, including 11,037 in the first half of November. The UN refugee agency says nearly 600 people have died this year trying to reach the islands. Senegal's President Faye has asked for an assessment of irregular migration.
keyFacts: At least 50 people were reportedly on board
Canaries arrivals up about two-thirds this year
UNHCR reports nearly 600 deaths on the route in 2026

articles.title: Six killed in suspected gas explosion at Tbilisi apartment building
articles.summary:
Six people, including a child, were killed when a suspected gas explosion partly collapsed a five-storey apartment building in Tbilisi, Georgia, on Thursday morning, AFP reported via Al Jazeera. A three-year-old girl was rescued alive after several hours.

Georgia's Interior Minister Sulkhan Tamazashvili said preliminary findings pointed to a blast on the fifth floor when a resident tried to switch on a gas heater. Supplier Tbilisi Energy said the apartment was registered as unoccupied and had used no gas for a year. Prosecutors have opened a criminal investigation into possible safety breaches, and 28 families are being moved to hotels, according to the report.
keyFacts: Six dead, including a child
Preliminary finding points to a gas heater
Criminal investigation opened into safety breaches

articles.title: Russian strike on Kryvyi Rih kills two and wounds 60, officials say
articles.summary:
A Russian attack on Kryvyi Rih, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy's hometown, killed a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman on Friday night, city administration head Oleksandr Vilkul said. Regional officials said 60 people were wounded, including six children.

Vilkul said about 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and an industrial site were damaged, and that later missiles struck rescuers and utility crews, according to Al Jazeera, citing AFP and AP. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk described Friday's landing of Russian missiles in Poland as a deliberate provocation. Russian authorities said a Ukrainian attack in Luhansk killed six people; that claim has not been independently verified.
keyFacts: Officials said a boy, 7, and a woman, 20, were killed
60 people were wounded, including six children, officials said
About 25 apartment buildings and a hospital were damaged, Vilkul said

articles.title: COP31 talks stay deadlocked as EU signals it could walk away over fossil fuel wording
articles.summary:
Climate talks at COP31 in Antalya went into an extra day on Saturday with no agreement on whether the final text should refer to fossil fuels, RTÉ and The Irish Times reported. The new development is that the EU is understood to be prepared to walk away rather than accept weak wording, according to The Irish Times, and a third draft due on Saturday morning had not appeared by lunchtime.

RTÉ said Saudi Arabia and its allies oppose the EU's preferred wording, while Panama has said it will not accept a text that omits fossil fuels. Negotiations chair Chris Bowen said he still believed a deal was possible. Any agreement requires consensus.
keyFacts: Talks ran into an extra day on Saturday without a deal
The Irish Times said the EU is prepared to walk away rather than accept weak text
Panama said it will block a text without fossil fuel wording, RTÉ reported

articles.title: Mexico captures alleged cartel leader 'El Chapo Isidro', on FBI's most wanted list
articles.summary:
Mexico's National Defence Secretariat said special forces captured Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, known as "Chapo Isidro", in a raid in Sinaloa state on Friday night local time, along with two other gang leaders. The FBI lists him among its ten most wanted fugitives and alleges he leads a group that trafficked heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl and marijuana into the US.

The Mexican government said US intelligence assisted, without giving details, according to the ABC, citing AFP and AP. CBS News reported violence in Sinaloa after the arrest, including gunfire near a baseball game in Guasave. Meza-Flores faces charges in Mexico and the US, where a reward of up to $US5 million had been offered.
keyFacts: Mexico's defence ministry announced the capture in Sinaloa
The FBI lists Meza-Flores among its ten most wanted
CBS reported violence in Sinaloa after the arrest

articles.title: Trump says he will work with Democrats to cap credit card interest at 10%
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump said on Saturday he would work with the incoming Democrat-controlled Congress to cap credit card interest rates at 10 per cent, telling Fox News Channel he would do it, according to AP. Senator Elizabeth Warren, expected to chair the Senate Banking Committee, has said she supports a cap.

Trump proposed the cap in January, and banks opposed it, warning that cards could be cancelled or rewards cut, AP reported. An August New York Fed survey put the median card rate at about 22.2 per cent. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau figures show about 195 million Americans held cards in 2024 and paid $US160 billion in interest.
keyFacts: Trump backed a 10% cap in a Fox News interview on Saturday
Banks have opposed the proposal, AP reported
The median US card rate is about 22.2%, New York Fed data show

articles.title: FBI national crime database suffers suspected breach, US media report
articles.summary:
The FBI's National Crime Information Center, which police use to share warrant and background-check information, has suffered a suspected breach, CNN and NBC reported on Friday, citing two people briefed on the matter, according to Al Jazeera. NBC separately reported an apparent cyberattack on the US Department of Agriculture.

President Donald Trump appeared to confirm the FBI hack in a television interview on Saturday, saying it was "not good", Al Jazeera reported. The FBI and the Agriculture Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment, and FBI Director Kash Patel has not commented publicly. The breach has not been officially confirmed by the bureau.
keyFacts: CNN and NBC reported a suspected breach of the FBI's NCIC system
Trump appeared to confirm the hack in a Saturday interview
The FBI has not officially confirmed the breach

articles.title: US judge approves Bayer's $US7.25 billion Roundup cancer settlement
articles.summary:
A St Louis judge on Friday approved a settlement under which Bayer will pay up to $US7.25 billion over as long as 21 years to resolve claims that its Roundup weedkiller caused non-Hodgkin lymphoma, AP reported. Circuit Judge Timothy Boyer described the payouts as fair and adequate in a written order.

AP said participants could receive on average between $US10,000 and $US165,000, depending on factors including exposure and illness severity. Bayer denies that Roundup causes cancer, and its chief executive Bill Anderson called the settlement a milestone. Some plaintiffs' lawyers say the payments are too small, and the approval could be appealed. The cancer link remains disputed between the WHO's cancer agency and the US EPA.
keyFacts: The settlement is worth up to $US7.25 billion over 21 years
Bayer denies Roundup causes cancer
The approval can still be appealed, AP reported

articles.title: US jury finds man guilty of starting fire that became deadly Palisades blaze
articles.summary:
A federal jury in Los Angeles on Friday found Jonathan Rinderknecht guilty of arson-related charges over the fire that grew into the January 2025 Palisades Fire, NBC Los Angeles and ABC7 reported. Prosecutors alleged he started the Lachman Fire on New Year's Day 2025, which rekindled days later in strong winds. The Palisades Fire killed 12 people and destroyed thousands of structures.

It was a retrial; the first trial ended in a mistrial in June with jurors split 10-2 in favour of acquittal. Prosecutors cited phone location data and online search records. His lawyer, Steve Haney, argued the evidence was circumstantial and that fireworks could have caused the blaze. Sentencing is set for March 2027.
keyFacts: Rinderknecht was found guilty at a retrial on Friday
His first trial ended in a 10-2 mistrial in June
Sentencing is set for 17 March 2027

articles.title: New national rules for home birth midwives take effect in January
articles.summary:
From January, every midwife attending a home birth must hold an endorsement requiring extra training and 5,000 hours of work to qualify for professional indemnity insurance, AAP reported. Secondary midwives were previously exempt, and two midwives are required at a home birth.

The federal government says the change makes home birth safer and closes insurance gaps. Midwives and mothers say it could halve the number of home births, and rallies were planned around Australia on Saturday. Senators from several parties have asked Assistant Health Minister Rebecca White to reverse the change. White said the decision was made more than 18 months ago and that public home birth services remain unchanged.
keyFacts: The rules apply to all home birth midwives from January
Opponents say home births could fall by half or more
White said public home birth services are unchanged

articles.title: Victorian Labor pledges health funding as parties dispute VicHealth's future
articles.summary:
Victorian Premier Ben Carroll pledged $14.4 million so emergency patient transport staff can transfer long service leave, and said Labor would keep 132 nursing positions at Werribee Mercy Hospital, AAP reported. Carroll said the Coalition would make large cuts and One Nation wants to privatise hospitals; both parties' positions on those claims were not reported.

The parties also differ on VicHealth, which the government plans to merge into the Department of Health after a December review. Opposition Leader Jess Wilson has committed to keeping it independent, a position backed by the Public Health Association and the AMA, AAP said. One Nation's Barnaby Joyce said the party faced a difficult task. Victorians vote on 28 November.
keyFacts: Labor pledged $14.4m for patient transport staff leave
Labor plans to absorb VicHealth; Wilson pledges to keep it independent
The state election is on 28 November

articles.title: Malaysia says it will resettle 10,000 Rohingya refugees in Turkey
articles.summary:
Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said on Friday that Malaysia will resettle 10,000 Rohingya refugees in Turkey through a skills training program, AAP reported. He said the government would work with Turkish authorities and the UN refugee agency and would consider the consent of those involved. Turkey's foreign ministry did not immediately respond.

The announcement came a day after the International Court of Justice ruled Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. A Myanmar government spokeswoman called the ruling unfair and said it was a nine-to-six decision. UNHCR figures show Malaysia had about 193,000 registered refugees from Myanmar at the end of February.
keyFacts: Malaysia plans to resettle 10,000 Rohingya in Turkey
Turkey had not responded, AAP reported
Myanmar called the ICJ genocide ruling unfair

articles.title: Honda and Toyota recall 1.6 million US vehicles over Takata airbag risk
articles.summary:
Honda and Toyota are recalling about 1.6 million vehicles in the US because their Takata airbag inflators could rupture, the ABC reported, citing Reuters. Both companies said no injuries, crashes or ruptures have been linked to the recalled vehicles.

The US road safety regulator NHTSA said the companies saw early evidence of degradation risk. Honda's recall covers 810,592 older US vehicles, while Toyota's covers 790,000 vehicles worldwide, including 314,000 in the US. Inflators will be replaced. Defective Takata inflators have been linked to at least 28 US deaths since 2009. Lexus has also recalled more than 7,000 vehicles in Australia, the ABC said.
keyFacts: About 1.6 million US vehicles are being recalled
The companies said no injuries are linked to these vehicles
Lexus has recalled more than 7,000 vehicles in Australia

articles.title: Fire at Iraqi power station near Basra kills at least four
articles.summary:
A fire at the Hartha power station north of Basra killed at least four people and injured 35, according to the Iraqi News Agency, as reported by Al Jazeera on Saturday. The civil defence directorate said the blaze at the station and nearby houses had been brought under control.

Operations at the 800-megawatt plant were halted, the agency said. The cause has not been confirmed. Footage shared online showed smoke and burnt-out cars near the site, according to Al Jazeera. Iraq's electricity grid has faced long-running shortfalls, and previous substation fires have caused power cuts in the country.
keyFacts: At least four people died and 35 were injured, state media said
The 800-megawatt Hartha station was shut down
The cause of the fire has not been confirmed

articles.title: India's Congress youth wing protests at Meta offices over account restrictions
articles.summary:
The youth wing of India's opposition Congress party protested outside Meta offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram on Friday, according to Al Jazeera, citing Anadolu and Reuters. In Hyderabad, protesters entered the building and scuffled with police. The party alleges Meta restricted Instagram accounts of its leaders on 19 November at the request of the ruling BJP.

BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accused protesters of vandalising the Hyderabad office. A party social media official told Reuters two accounts had been restored but thousands remain restricted. Police registered a complaint against four Youth Congress leaders in Mumbai. Meta had not commented on the allegations.
keyFacts: Protests were held at Meta offices in three Indian cities
Congress alleges accounts were restricted at the BJP's request
The BJP accused protesters of vandalism

leftOut.title: Qatar's emir and Egypt's president discuss Gaza ceasefire during Cairo visit
leftOut.summary:
Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani arrived in Cairo on Thursday for an official visit at the invitation of Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, Al Jazeera reported. Qatar said the visit aimed to strengthen investment and energy ties and coordinate efforts to reduce regional tensions.

Egypt's presidential spokesman said the leaders called for political solutions and for preventing wider conflict. Sisi called on all parties to uphold the Gaza ceasefire and allow humanitarian aid. Qatar's Emiri Diwan said they discussed joint mediation to consolidate the ceasefire.
keyFacts: The emir visited at Sisi's invitation
Both leaders called for the Gaza ceasefire to be upheld
Qatar and Egypt are joint mediators

leftOut.title: Analysis examines Italian objections to Ukraine's strikes on Russian ships off Libya
leftOut.summary:
An Al Jazeera explainer examined why Italy has objected to Ukrainian strikes on Russian vessels off Libya. Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said the attacks violated Libya's sovereignty and that Rome had no prior knowledge of the plan.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the vessels were legitimate targets and Kyiv did not intend to harm Libya. The piece cited the Kiel Institute as saying Italy has given Ukraine more than three billion euros in military aid, and noted Libya supplied about a quarter of Italy's crude oil imports last year, according to an analyst.
keyFacts: Tajani said the strikes violated Libyan sovereignty
Ukraine says the ships were legitimate targets
Libya is a major crude supplier to Italy

leftOut.title: Analysis looks at Andalusia's PP-Vox government ahead of Spain's snap election
leftOut.summary:
An Al Jazeera analysis examined the governing coalition between the conservative People's Party and the far-right Vox party in Andalusia ahead of Spain's snap general election on Sunday. Polls cited in the piece put the PP first, the Socialists second and Vox third.

PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo has said he would prefer a minority government supported by Vox but has not ruled out a coalition, according to the article. An academic quoted said the PP's earlier deal with Vox in Andalusia helped normalise the party.
keyFacts: Spain holds a snap general election on Sunday
Polls put the PP ahead without a majority
Andalusia has had a PP-Vox government since May

leftOut.title: Report says cost of a US Thanksgiving meal has risen about 11% on last year
leftOut.summary:
The Century Foundation estimated a typical Thanksgiving meal in the United States costs about 11 per cent more than last year, Al Jazeera reported. It said turkey prices were up 26 per cent and green beans almost 37 per cent.

The American Farm Bureau forecast a 6 per cent rise for a 10-person meal, its first increase since 2022, while Walmart said its holiday meal package was 12 per cent cheaper. A LendingTree survey found about a third of hosts felt financially strained, according to the report.
keyFacts: The Century Foundation estimates an 11% rise
The Farm Bureau forecasts a 6% rise
Walmart says its meal package is cheaper

leftOut.title: Analysis says Labor is moving into election mode at the halfway point of its term
leftOut.summary:
Political analyst Michelle Grattan wrote, in a piece republished by the ABC from The Conversation, that Labor is moving into election mode, noting its national campaign committee met for the first time on Monday. She pointed to a worsening economy, including a rate rise, higher unemployment and rising inflation.

Asked whether he planned to retire, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said no. Labor MP Ed Husic said the prime minister had earned the right to choose his timing. The next federal election is due by May 2028.
keyFacts: Labor's campaign committee met on Monday
Albanese said he does not plan to retire
The next election is due by May 2028

leftOut.title: Analysis examines end of Solomon Islands' security pact with China
leftOut.summary:
An ABC analysis examined Solomon Islands' decision to end its 2022 security pact with China, after it signed a treaty with Australia this week worth about $740 million. The treaty declares Solomon Islands will not host a foreign military base.

Prime Minister Matthew Wale said the uncertainty of recent years was over. Opposition leader Manasseh Sogavare said the country had given up sovereignty to Australia and called for the treaty to be tabled. An academic said Chinese police would leave by the end of the month, which neither government has confirmed.
keyFacts: The Australian treaty is worth about $740 million
Sogavare has called for the treaty to be tabled
Departure of Chinese police is unconfirmed

leftOut.title: Barbie exhibition opens at Melbourne Museum on Saturday
leftOut.summary:
A Barbie exhibition developed by London's Design Museum will open at Melbourne Museum on Saturday and run until May 16, the ABC reported. The Australian showing includes more than 250 objects, among them 150 dolls, and toy maker Mattel is a partner.

The exhibition includes one-off dolls of tennis players Evonne Goolagong Cawley and Ash Barty, according to the local curator. The ABC said the show drew about 144,000 visitors in London, making it one of the Design Museum's most popular exhibitions.
keyFacts: The exhibition runs from November 28 to May 16
It includes about 150 dolls
Mattel is a partner

leftOut.title: Former NZ leaders call for review of MMP voting after election overhang
leftOut.summary:
Former New Zealand prime ministers Geoffrey Palmer and Helen Clark are among those calling for a review of the country's mixed-member proportional voting system after the November 7 election, AAP reported. Preliminary results give Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's coalition 67 of 131 seats, helped by an overhang from National's electorate wins.

Labour leader Chris Hipkins said National held power only through manipulating the system. ACT leader David Seymour said he was unsure a broader inquiry would help. Final results were expected on November 27.
keyFacts: Preliminary results give the coalition 67 of 131 seats
National's party vote was about 29%
Final results were due on November 27

leftOut.title: Khawaja says he felt personally attacked by Cummins over ball-tampering comments
leftOut.summary:
Former Test batter Usman Khawaja said he felt personally attacked by Australian captain Pat Cummins, who had described several accusations as nonsense at a press conference, AAP reported. Khawaja made the comments in an 80-minute interview on a cricket podcast.

Khawaja said he had sent Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg a draft team statement admitting to ball-tampering in 2018, which was not used. He said he always wanted Cummins to stay captain, and again declined to say which players knew of the tampering beforehand.
keyFacts: Khawaja spoke in an 80-minute podcast interview
He says he sent a draft statement to Todd Greenberg
He declined to name players who knew

leftOut.title: Former students of Sydney Catholic school sue over alleged historical abuse by priest
leftOut.summary:
Three former students of Our Lady of Dolours school in Sydney are taking civil claims to the NSW Supreme Court alleging they were assaulted by parish priest Paul Francis Cahill in the 1970s and 1980s, the ABC reported. Cahill died in 2017. The claims are being brought through law firm Maurice Blackburn.

The allegations have not been tested in court. The Diocese of Broken Bay said it takes concerns seriously but declined an interview, while the Archdiocese of Sydney did not respond and Catholic Schools NSW declined to comment, according to the ABC.
keyFacts: Three former students have lodged claims
The priest died in 2017
The allegations have not been tested in court

leftOut.title: Doctors tell Four Corners pregnancy discrimination is affecting careers in medicine
leftOut.summary:
Several doctors told the ABC's Four Corners they faced disadvantage in training and pay after becoming pregnant. One trainee said a three-year training offer was withdrawn months after she disclosed her pregnancy and replaced with a two-year contract.

NSW Health said it does not comment on individual cases and that recruitment must be merit-based and lawful. The Attorney-General's office said it is carefully considering an October report by the Sex Discrimination Commissioner, to which the government has not yet responded.
keyFacts: A trainee says her training offer was reduced after disclosure
NSW Health says recruitment is merit-based
The government has not responded to an October report

leftOut.title: Visiting sailors offer to ferry Flinders Island residents away from bushfire
leftOut.summary:
A Victorian family sailing around Flinders Island offered residents boat rides away from the bushfire burning on the island, the ABC reported. Oliver Hordern, 21, said only one stranded resident accepted, as others had boats and planned to defend their homes.

The ABC said the fire has burned almost 15,000 hectares and damaged or destroyed six homes. An emergency warning remained for northern areas including Killiecrankie, where residents were told it was too late to leave. More than 60 firefighters were working on the fire, with rain forecast for Saturday.
keyFacts: One resident accepted a boat ride
The fire has burned almost 15,000 hectares
Rain is forecast for Saturday

leftOut.title: Parents of boy killed in Oregon school shooting seek records from gunman's mother
leftOut.summary:
The parents of five-year-old Rhoam Summer, who was killed in the October 15 shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, filed a petition on November 23 in Deschutes County Circuit Court, The Bulletin reported. It asks the court to order the 16-year-old gunman's mother to produce records on the purchase and ownership of the shotgun used.

The petition also seeks the teenager's online activity. Family lawyer Tim Williams said the family plans a wrongful death suit. The mother's lawyer did not respond to questions, according to The Bulletin.
keyFacts: The petition was filed on November 23
It seeks records on the shotgun's ownership
The family is preparing a wrongful death suit

leftOut.title: DHS says Venezuelan man arrested in Utah over stickers urging Trump's assassination
leftOut.summary:
US Immigration and Customs Enforcement arrested Venezuelan national Héctor Alejandro Mujica-Hernández in Provo, Utah, on October 16, the Department of Homeland Security said, according to KUTV. DHS alleges he distributed stickers encouraging President Donald Trump's assassination at a meeting of a local anti-ICE group.

DHS said the FBI alerted investigators to threats found in his online activity, and that he entered the US legally in 2016 and overstayed his visa. KUTV's report did not state any charges, and did not include a response from the man.
keyFacts: The arrest took place on October 16
DHS says he overstayed a visa issued in 2016
No charges were stated in the report

leftOut.title: Young Texas Republicans urge their party to 'grow up' after midterm losses
leftOut.summary:
Members of the Tarrant County Young Republicans in Texas met in Fort Worth on November 23 to discuss the party's losses in the November 3 midterm elections, AP reported. Some members said the party needed to 'grow up' and show more humility, citing infighting.

The group's leaders said they were listening to members to identify better candidates and policies before 2028. Tarrant County, long a Republican stronghold, voted Democratic in the midterms, according to the report.
keyFacts: The meeting was held in Fort Worth on November 23
Members criticised party infighting
Tarrant County voted Democratic in the midterms

leftOut.title: AP report examines debate over Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang
leftOut.summary:
An AP report examined criticism of Nvidia's decision to reinstate chief executive Jensen Huang, who resigned after admitting an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy and after reports of a relationship with a subordinate. The board said it had received US government assurances that Huang is not a national security concern, but did not address the misconduct allegations.

Critics quoted said the move signalled impunity for powerful men. Huang told employees he had made mistakes and was in therapy, according to a report cited by AP. He is expected to appear before the Senate Banking Committee next week.
keyFacts: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang
The board cited US government security assurances
Huang is due before a Senate committee next week

leftOut.title: SA court refuses interim supervision order for Snowtown accomplice Mark Haydon
leftOut.summary:
A South Australian Supreme Court judge on Thursday refused the Crown's application for an interim supervision order over Mark Ray Haydon, who was convicted in 2006 of assisting offenders in the Snowtown murders, AAP reported. Haydon, 67, has completed his sentence and was paroled in May 2024.

Justice Kristopher Handshin said the court lacked jurisdiction to impose an order solely because of the seriousness of the offending, and noted reports reflected Haydon's progress. AAP said there was agreement he posed a low risk. His current order expires on Friday. The Crown's application for a new order continues, and the matter returns to court on 28 April.
keyFacts: Haydon was convicted of seven counts of assisting an offender
His current order expires on Friday
The matter returns to court on 28 April

leftOut.title: Two men appear in UK court charged over burglary at Prince William's Norfolk home
leftOut.summary:
Two men appeared at Norwich Magistrates' Court charged with burglary and trespassing on a protected site over a break-in at Anmer Hall, Prince William's home on the Sandringham estate, on Monday evening, AAP reported.

Prosecutor John Cooper told the court the men and a third suspect, who has not been arrested, triggered motion sensors shortly before 6pm and allegedly took six pairs of cufflinks and a clock. Police found the two men in nearby woodland about 7.15pm. Neither entered a plea, and both were remanded in custody while prosecutors seek the Attorney General's consent for the trespass charge.
keyFacts: The men are aged 34 and 32
Six pairs of cufflinks and a clock were allegedly taken
A third suspect has not been arrested

leftOut.title: US grand jury charges Thomas Markle Sr with possessing child abuse material
leftOut.summary:
A US grand jury has charged Thomas Markle Sr, 82, father of the Duchess of Sussex, with two counts of possessing child sexual abuse images, according to court documents in California, AAP reported, citing PA. Each count carries a maximum of 20 years in prison.

The filing says he possessed 35mm film negatives on or about 30 October and 4 November. AAP said the FBI detained him on 6 November after seizing material from two Los Angeles storage units. First assistant US attorney Bill Essayli said Markle is presumed innocent. A Florida court-ordered evaluation found him competent to stand trial, and he remains in custody.
keyFacts: He faces two counts
Each carries up to 20 years in prison
Prosecutors say he is presumed innocent

leftOut.title: Inquest into 2020 death of NSW girl Biddy Porter hears closing submissions
leftOut.summary:
The NSW State Coroner was due to hear closing submissions on Thursday in the inquest into the death of 10-year-old Bridgette "Biddy" Porter, who died at a rural property in July 2020, AAP reported.

A NSW Supreme Court judge ruled in 2021 that the 14-year-old charged over her death was not criminally responsible because of mental illness. The inquest has heard evidence about the family's disagreements over medical matters and warning signs in the weeks before the death, AAP said. The teenager remains in a forensic facility. Details of the death are subject to a non-publication order.
keyFacts: Biddy Porter died on 8 July 2020
The teenager was found not criminally responsible in 2021
State Coroner Teresa O'Sullivan is hearing the inquest

leftOut.title: Eastern Libyan forces vow retaliation after officers die in Ukrainian drone attack
leftOut.summary:
The Libyan National Army's general command vowed to retaliate at a time and place of its choosing after two Libyan naval officers died following a Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian warship at the Benghazi naval base, AAP reported. The LNA said the officers were pronounced dead on Tuesday evening.

Local officials said at least four drones were intercepted and two struck the corvette, and a Libyan official said at least 10 people were wounded. Two officials said sea drones were launched from a Ukrainian-run base in western Libya. Ukrainian officials had said Kyiv's forces did not target Libyans and did not immediately respond on Wednesday.
keyFacts: Two Libyan naval officers died
At least 10 people were wounded, a Libyan official said
Ukraine says it did not target Libyans

leftOut.title: Pope Leo says it is troubling COP31 ended without clear climate commitments
leftOut.summary:
Pope Leo said at his weekly general audience in St Peter's Square on Wednesday that it was troubling the COP31 climate talks ended without the international community adopting clear commitments, Reuters reported.

The talks ended on Sunday after the European Union and others rejected a final text proposed by COP31 presidents Turkey and Australia as too weak. Reuters said it was the first time since Copenhagen in 2009 that UN climate talks failed to adopt a deal. The pope called for a renewed sense of shared responsibility.
keyFacts: The remarks were made at Wednesday's general audience
COP31 ended on Sunday without an agreed deal
Turkey and Australia jointly presided over COP31

leftOut.title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed to Saturday because of nor'easter
leftOut.summary:
Macy's postponed its Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York to Saturday 28 November because of a nor'easter, The Times of Israel reported, citing the company. Macy's said it was the first postponement in the parade's 100-year history.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani warned of sustained winds of 30 to 40 miles per hour with gusts up to 65 miles per hour. The storm coincided with the Thanksgiving travel period, when up to 80 million people were expected to travel, according to the report.
keyFacts: The parade moves to Saturday 28 November
Macy's says it is the first postponement in 100 years
Gusts of up to 65 mph were forecast

leftOut.title: ABC analysis says inflation figures overshadowed government's legislative wins
leftOut.summary:
An ABC analysis by David Speers argued that higher-than-expected inflation figures overshadowed a week in which Labor secured several end-of-year deals with the Greens. The piece noted the private health insurance rebate for over-65s will be wound back with pensioners exempted, and that discretionary trusts will face a minimum 30 per cent tax on distributions.

Speers wrote that headline inflation rose from 4.3 to 4.9 per cent, with fuel accounting for about half the increase, and that the Treasurer faces pressure before next month's mid-year budget update. The piece cited Newspoll showing Labor's primary vote at 27 per cent, down from 36 per cent a year earlier.
keyFacts: Analysis piece by ABC's David Speers
Headline inflation rose to 4.9%
Newspoll has Labor's primary vote at 27%

leftOut.title: Analysts say Victoria's new upper house rules could boost One Nation
leftOut.summary:
AAP reported that One Nation could gain significant influence in Victoria's upper house under new voting rules, even if it wins few lower house seats at Saturday's state election. The rules require voters to number at least five parties above the line or five candidates below it.

One Nation deputy leader Colleen Harkin named government spending, emissions reduction and First Nations recognition as areas the party could resist. Monash University's Zareh Ghazarian was quoted as expecting One Nation to win at least one seat in each of the eight regions. Animal Justice Party MP Georgie Purcell said the change could wipe out the crossbench.
keyFacts: Voters must number at least five parties above the line
Academic expects One Nation seat in each of eight regions
Victorian election is on Saturday

leftOut.title: Pakistan's first astronaut boards China's Tiangong space station
leftOut.summary:
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became the first Pakistani in orbit and the first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong space station after the Shenzhou-24 crew docked early on Wednesday, Al Jazeera reported. He is expected to stay five to 10 days.

Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif described the mission as evidence of the friendship between Pakistan and China, while Chinese President Xi Jinping also said the joint mission reflected close ties between the two countries, according to Al Jazeera. The launch itself was reported on Wednesday.
keyFacts: Ali docked with Tiangong early on Wednesday
Expected to stay five to 10 days
Launch was reported in an earlier update

leftOut.title: Survey finds 38% of Muslim students in UK report Islamophobia at university
leftOut.summary:
A report by the Federation of Student Islamic Societies found 38 per cent of Muslim students in the UK said they had experienced Islamophobia at university, Al Jazeera reported. The survey covered 715 students at 63 universities.

Women were more likely to report being targeted than men, at 42 per cent compared with 34 per cent. Of those affected, 68 per cent said they did not feel able to report it. The federation has asked universities to adopt a definition of Islamophobia and the government to review its Prevent program, according to Al Jazeera.
keyFacts: Survey of 715 students at 63 universities
38% report experiencing Islamophobia
68% of those affected did not feel able to report it

leftOut.title: Feature examines Gaza prisoners held by Israel after completing sentences
leftOut.summary:
An Al Jazeera feature examined the cases of Gaza prisoners who remain in Israeli custody after completing their sentences. It profiled Fadi Zughra, arrested in 2016 while fishing, who finished an eight-and-a-half-year sentence in early 2025 but is still detained.

The Palestinian Commission of Detainees and Ex-Detainees Affairs says 48 Gaza prisoners remain held after their sentences ended, and prisoner groups say Israel uses its 2002 Unlawful Combatants Law to detain them. The feature cited B'Tselem figures that 9,187 Palestinians were held on security grounds at the end of June 2026. The article did not include an Israeli response.
keyFacts: Commission says 48 Gaza prisoners held past their sentences
Groups cite 2002 Unlawful Combatants Law
B'Tselem says 9,187 held on security grounds in June

leftOut.title: Turkish military helicopter crash near Eskisehir kills five crew
leftOut.summary:
A Turkish Air Force AS-532 helicopter crashed shortly after taking off from Eskisehir on a training flight, killing all five crew members, Turkey's Ministry of National Defence said, according to Al Jazeera. The crash happened near Yorukakcayir village, about 15 kilometres west of the city centre.

The ministry said the wreckage had been reached but did not give a cause. Al Jazeera noted that an army Sikorsky S-70 crashed near Malatya on 12 November, killing four crew, and that no official explanation has been given for that crash.
keyFacts: Five crew killed on a training flight, ministry says
Crash site about 15 km west of Eskisehir
No cause given

leftOut.title: South African court gives suspended sentence to Zimbabwean who tried to fight for Russia
leftOut.summary:
A South African court on Tuesday sentenced Zimbabwean man Tafadzwa Sithole to five years in prison, wholly suspended for five years, after he pleaded guilty to breaching the country's foreign military assistance law, Al Jazeera and AP reported.

Sithole was arrested at Johannesburg's OR Tambo airport on 8 November while trying to board a flight to Russia. He told the court he had agreed to fight for Russia for payment after applying online. He is due to be deported to Zimbabwe, and four other accused are negotiating plea deals, according to the report.
keyFacts: Five-year sentence suspended for five years
Arrested at OR Tambo airport on 8 November
Four other accused negotiating plea deals

leftOut.title: NSW MP named in Israeli government dossier criticises response to his complaint
leftOut.summary:
NSW Labor MP Anthony D'Adam, who was named in a September 2025 Israeli Ministry of Diaspora Affairs dossier alongside senators Lidia Thorpe and Mehreen Faruqi, said authorities had downplayed his concerns, AAP reported.

D'Adam wrote to Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke in January, and his complaint was referred to the Counter Foreign Interference Taskforce. He described a reply received in November as dismissive and said the dossier had a chilling effect. AAP said ASIO, the AFP and the Israeli embassy were contacted for comment; their responses were not included in the report.
keyFacts: D'Adam named in a 2025 Israeli ministry dossier
Complaint referred to foreign interference taskforce
ASIO, AFP and Israeli embassy contacted for comment

leftOut.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon found guilty of murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies
leftOut.summary:
A NSW Supreme Court jury found former police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon guilty on Wednesday of murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies, the ABC reported. The jury returned unanimous verdicts after about two hours of deliberation.

The Crown said Lamarre-Condon went to Baird's Paddington home in February 2024 disguised as a food delivery driver and shot both men. He gave evidence that he acted in self-defence. He was also found guilty of a 2023 break, enter and steal offence, according to the ABC.
keyFacts: Unanimous verdicts after about two hours
Killings occurred in February 2024
Accused claimed self-defence

leftOut.title: Rudy Giuliani receives Presidential Medal of Freedom at private ceremony
leftOut.summary:
Former New York mayor Rudy Giuliani received the Presidential Medal of Freedom at a private White House ceremony on Tuesday, US time, the ABC reported. The White House press pool was not invited.

President Donald Trump pardoned Giuliani in 2025 and had promised him the award. The ABC noted a 2023 defamation judgment of $US148 million against Giuliani and his disbarment. Giuliani said he was honoured and humbled. Fewer than 700 people have received the medal.
keyFacts: Private ceremony on Tuesday, US time
Press pool not invited
Trump pardoned Giuliani in 2025

leftOut.title: ABC analysis argues higher inflation is unlikely to bring a rate rise
leftOut.summary:
An analysis piece by ABC money correspondent Jessica Irvine examined why interest rates are not widely expected to rise despite annual inflation reaching 4.9 per cent in the year to October.

The article was published hours after the Australian Bureau of Statistics released the October consumer price figures. It sets out the author's view of the Reserve Bank's likely response rather than reporting new developments. The RBA's next decision is due on 8 December.
keyFacts: Labelled as analysis by the ABC
Follows 4.9% annual CPI figure
RBA next meets on 8 December

leftOut.title: Economists forecast October inflation rise ahead of ABS release
leftOut.summary:
NAB economists forecast annual headline inflation will rise from 4.3 per cent to 4.7 per cent when the Australian Bureau of Statistics releases October consumer price figures on Wednesday, AAP reported. They said higher fuel costs and the card surcharge ban that began on 1 October were the main drivers.

NAB's Taylor Nugent said he expected October to be the peak. Treasurer Jim Chalmers told question time inflation would be higher than the government would like, citing oil prices in October, according to AAP. The official figures had not been released at the time of the report.
keyFacts: NAB forecasts 4.7% annual headline inflation
ABS releases October figures on Wednesday
Chalmers says inflation will be higher than wanted

leftOut.title: Melanoma researcher Georgina Long named joint winner of Prime Minister's Prize for Science
leftOut.summary:
Professor Georgina Long, medical director of Melanoma Institute Australia, was named co-recipient of the 2026 Prime Minister's Prize for Science on Tuesday night, AAP and the ABC reported. AAP said her work with the late Richard Scolyer helped lift survival from advanced melanoma above 50 per cent.

The prize was shared with subatomic physicist Anthony Thomas, according to AAP. Other awards went to Mark Smythe, Asha Bowen, Malcolm Macintosh and Chris Matthews. Long told AAP that teachers help make curiosity part of life.
keyFacts: Long is a joint winner of the top science prize
Prize shared with physicist Anthony Thomas
Awards announced on Tuesday night

leftOut.title: Two arrested after break-in at Prince William's Norfolk home
leftOut.summary:
Norfolk police said two men were arrested on suspicion of burglary and trespass at a property on the Sandringham estate after reports of suspicious activity on Monday night, AAP reported. The property, Anmer Hall, was unoccupied and the family was not present.

Police used dogs, drones and a helicopter in the search, according to AAP. The two men were in custody on Tuesday and had not been charged. The Sun newspaper first reported the break-in. Anmer Hall is used by the Prince and Princess of Wales mainly for holidays.
keyFacts: Two men arrested on suspicion of burglary
House was unoccupied at the time
No charges laid as of Tuesday

leftOut.title: Victorian business groups seek greater role with next state government
leftOut.summary:
Victorian business groups told AAP they want a greater say in decisions after Saturday's state election. Victorian Chamber of Commerce and Industry chief executive Sally Curtain said business had been locked out of key decisions and called for clarity on the COVID debt payroll levy.

Tim Piper of the Victorian Congress of Employer Associations said businesses wanted to work closely with the next government. At a radio leaders' forum on Tuesday, Premier Ben Carroll defended the state's debt, while Opposition Leader Jess Wilson pointed to $26 billion in planned savings, according to AAP.
keyFacts: Victorians vote on Saturday
Business groups seek more consultation
Coalition cites $26 billion in planned savings

leftOut.title: Jury to begin deliberations in Lamarre-Condon double murder trial
leftOut.summary:
A NSW Supreme Court jury is due to be reduced from 15 to 12 members by ballot on Wednesday morning before beginning deliberations in the trial of former police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon, AAP reported. He has pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in Sydney in February 2024.

Prosecutors allege he planned the killing of Mr Baird and shot Mr Davies to remove a witness. Lamarre-Condon told the court he acted in self-defence and that the second death occurred during a struggle, according to AAP. Prosecutors rejected his offered manslaughter plea.
keyFacts: Jury ballot set for Wednesday morning
Accused has pleaded not guilty to two murders
Trial has run for about 10 weeks

leftOut.title: Inquest hears evidence over Aboriginal man's death in Kalgoorlie prison
leftOut.summary:
A coronial inquest in Perth into the death of Linton Phillip Ryan, 32, at Eastern Goldfields Regional Prison in April 2025 heard that a police constable made light of the man's suicide threat in a voice message, AAP reported. The inquest began on Monday.

Counsel assisting told the inquest Ryan was moved to a cell without a scheduled mental health assessment, according to AAP. The inquest is examining whether he should have been taken to hospital and more closely observed. The evidence has not yet been the subject of findings.
keyFacts: Inquest began in Perth on Monday
Ryan died in prison in April 2025
No findings have yet been made

leftOut.title: Pacific nations look to own coalitions after COP31 ends without deal
leftOut.summary:
Pacific island nations are turning to their own climate coalitions after the COP31 talks in Turkey ended without an agreement, AAP reported. Tuvalu's climate minister Maina Talia said Tuvalu could not accept the outcome and that Tuvalu and Ireland would host a conference on moving away from fossil fuels next year.

Fiji's Lynda Tabuya said she was deeply disappointed but that responsibility lay with all parties, according to AAP. Talks president Chris Bowen said the disagreements had been insurmountable. The COP28 agreement on transitioning away from fossil fuels remains in place.
keyFacts: COP31 ended without an agreement
Tuvalu and Ireland to host a fossil fuel conference
COP28 agreement remains in force

leftOut.title: Ukraine says attacks on Russian ships off Libya were self-defence
leftOut.summary:
Ukraine said its attacks on a Russian warship and a cargo vessel off the coast of Libya were legitimate acts of self-defence and that it was not extending the war, Al Jazeera reported on Tuesday. Kyiv has claimed responsibility for the attacks.

Russia has said it will respond to Ukrainian attacks, including strikes on its oil refineries, according to Al Jazeera. Ukrainian security service footage released earlier showed a sea drone attacking the corvette near Benghazi, which has not been independently verified.
keyFacts: Ukraine calls the Libya strikes self-defence
Kyiv has claimed responsibility
Russia says it will respond

leftOut.title: Singapore Airlines begins daily flights at Western Sydney International Airport
leftOut.summary:
Singapore Airlines began daily services between Western Sydney International Airport and Singapore from 23 November, according to Infrastructure Minister Catherine King. Singapore's Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said in Canberra on Tuesday that the airline had flown the inaugural flight into the new airport the previous night.

The service uses Airbus A350-900 aircraft with 303 seats, the minister's office said. Flights leave Western Sydney just before midnight and arrive at Changi Airport around 5am, while return flights depart Singapore at 11.30am. The government said the route was secured in August 2024.
keyFacts: Daily service began on 23 November
A350-900 aircraft with 303 seats
Route was announced in August 2024

leftOut.title: China sets Wednesday launch for Shenzhou-24 crew including Pakistani astronaut
leftOut.summary:
The China Manned Space Agency said on Tuesday that Shenzhou-24 would launch at 8.18am local time on Wednesday from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre on a Long March-2F rocket, Reuters reported. It said the crew was in good condition and preparations were complete.

The crew includes Pakistani payload specialist Zeeshan Ali, who would be the first foreign astronaut to visit China's Tiangong space station, on a short-term stay, according to Reuters. Commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer Wu Yi complete the crew. Pakistan's participation was announced earlier this month, Al Jazeera reported.
keyFacts: Launch set for 8.18am Wednesday, Beijing time
Zeeshan Ali to be first foreigner on Tiangong
41st crewed flight of China's program

leftOut.title: Wong previews Senate speech warning US-China rivalry is eroding guardrails
leftOut.summary:
Foreign Minister Penny Wong previewed a major foreign policy address due in the Senate on Tuesday, saying the US and China were competing in every domain with less regard for guardrails, the ABC reported. She described the rivalry as the defining strategic dynamic of the period.

Wong said China was undertaking the largest military build-up by any country since the Second World War and called for reform of the UN Security Council. She said middle powers would not benefit from abandoning multilateral institutions because they were imperfect. The speech itself had not been delivered at the time of reporting, and its themes were outlined in an earlier report.
keyFacts: Speech due to be delivered in the Senate on Tuesday
Wong calls for UN Security Council reform
She cites China's military build-up

leftOut.title: ABC analysis says AI share bubble has deflated but not burst
leftOut.summary:
ABC chief business correspondent Ian Verrender wrote in an analysis piece that the share market bubble around artificial intelligence had deflated significantly but had not burst. He noted Nvidia had fallen about 40% from its October peak before rebounding after Jensen Huang's reinstatement.

The piece said the Nasdaq was more than 18% below its 6 October peak. It estimated about a fifth of Australia's roughly $4.8 trillion superannuation pool was invested on Wall Street. Verrender argued the sell-off may make further interest rate rises less likely while markets remain volatile. The article is labelled as analysis.
keyFacts: Piece is labelled analysis
Nasdaq more than 18% below its October peak
Discusses superannuation exposure to US shares

leftOut.title: Israeli broadcaster reports Eisenkot plans surprise coalition announcement
leftOut.summary:
Israeli public broadcaster Kan reported that Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot plans to announce a coalition at an unexpected time and seek a Knesset vote within a day or two, according to the Times of Israel. Kan did not cite sources for the report.

Eisenkot was chosen by Israel's president earlier this month to try to form the next government. There was no confirmation from Eisenkot's party of the reported plan, and no date has been set for any vote. Representatives of Yashar and Likud have also held unity talks, the Times of Israel reported.
keyFacts: Report attributed to broadcaster Kan without sources
No vote date has been set
Yashar and Likud have held unity talks

leftOut.title: Canadian Press report examines Canada's likely miss of its 2030 emissions target
leftOut.summary:
A Canadian Press explanatory report said Canada was not on track to meet its 2030 Paris Agreement target of cutting emissions by 40 to 45 per cent from 2005 levels, and that the government had not said so directly. It said the government's own projection from a year earlier showed a best-case cut of 28 per cent.

Environment Minister Julie Dabrusin said Canada remained committed to the Paris Agreement but did not say whether that included the 2030 target. Her office said Canada would report to the UN on the target next month. Environmental groups and a Conservative MP questioned the government's approach, the report said.
keyFacts: Government projection showed a 28% cut by 2030
Target is a 40–45% cut from 2005 levels
Canada due to report to the UN next month

leftOut.title: Lowy index rates Modi as Asia's second most effective leader after Xi
leftOut.summary:
The Lowy Institute's 2026 Asia Power Index rated Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi as the region's second most effective leader after China's Xi Jinping, the Press Trust of India reported. India remained the third most powerful country in Asia, with its score rising 0.5 points to 40.5.

The index said India's low profile during the Gulf conflict weighed on Modi's global leadership rating. It scored the US at 78.9 and China at 73.6, the narrowest gap since 2018. Indian media also reported political exchanges between the governing BJP and opposition leader Rahul Gandhi over the ranking. The index's main findings were reported earlier.
keyFacts: India ranked third most powerful country in Asia
US–China gap is the narrowest since 2018
Index covers 27 countries and territories

leftOut.title: Vox Balearic MP says she received voting card for husband who died 15 years ago
leftOut.summary:
Manuela Cañadas, spokesperson for the Vox party in the Balearic parliament, said on Monday she had received an electoral census card in the name of her husband, who died more than 15 years ago, ahead of Spain's 29 November general election, The Objective and El Debate reported. She showed the card at a press conference in Palma.

Cañadas said the central government was capable of altering the electoral roll and called on families who received cards for dead relatives to report it. El Debate cited Spain's statistics office, INE, which has said deaths are removed from rolls when notified and that delays can leave names listed. No government response was reported.
keyFacts: Spain's general election is on 29 November
Cañadas showed the card at a press conference
INE says removal delays can occur

leftOut.title: Former Countdown host Molly Meldrum dies aged 83
leftOut.summary:
Music presenter Ian "Molly" Meldrum, known for hosting the ABC television program Countdown, has died aged 83, his family announced on Monday, according to the ABC. The family said he died peacefully.

Victorian Premier Ben Carroll said the family had accepted the offer of a state funeral. Tributes came from Opposition Leader Angus Taylor and from musicians including the band Blondie, the ABC reported. Meldrum was born in Orbost, Victoria, in 1943 and helped introduce many bands to Australian audiences through Countdown in the 1970s and 1980s.
keyFacts: Meldrum died aged 83
Victoria offers a state funeral
Hosted Countdown in the 1970s and 1980s

leftOut.title: Two teenagers charged after fatal stabbing in Melbourne's CBD
leftOut.summary:
Victoria Police charged a 17-year-old and an 18-year-old with affray after a 21-year-old man from Narre Warren was stabbed and later died in hospital following an altercation on La Trobe Street on Saturday night, the ABC reported. Five males were arrested, and three were released pending further inquiries.

Police also reported two other stabbings on Saturday, one near Elizabeth and Bourke streets in the CBD and one outside a restaurant in Broadmeadows, with arrests made in both cases, according to the ABC.
keyFacts: 21-year-old man died after La Trobe Street altercation
Two teenagers charged with affray
Arrests made over two other Saturday stabbings

leftOut.title: More than 12,000 evacuated from Manchester concert after substance released
leftOut.summary:
Greater Manchester Police said more than 12,000 people were escorted out of a Don Toliver concert at the Co-op Live arena on Sunday night after reports that an unknown substance had been released, Reuters reported. Police were alerted shortly after 10pm local time.

The North West Ambulance Service said the substance was believed to be tear gas, while police said it had not yet been identified. One person was taken to hospital and paramedics assessed more than 50 people, some with eye and breathing symptoms, according to Reuters.
keyFacts: More than 12,000 people escorted from the arena
Ambulance service believes it was tear gas
One person taken to hospital

leftOut.title: ABC analysis says Victorian Labor is bracing for a heavy election loss
leftOut.summary:
