An ABC analysis by Patricia Karvelas says Victorian Labor insiders expect a result at Saturday's state election comparable to NSW Labor's 2011 defeat, when it lost 30 seats. It says polls point to a Liberal majority and that many insiders expect Labor to lose 30 to 35 seats.

The piece also says One Nation could win several seats and hold the balance of power in the upper house, and notes Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has kept away from the campaign. It is analysis and reports no new events.
keyFacts: Victorian election is on Saturday
Analysis cites insiders expecting heavy losses
Piece is analysis, not new reporting

leftOut.title: ABC analysis examines what COP31's collapse means for Australia and the Pacific
leftOut.summary:
An analysis by ABC global affairs editor Laura Tingle examines the consequences of the COP31 talks in Antalya ending without a deal after almost two days of overtime. It cites Climate Minister Chris Bowen saying red lines over fossil fuels and climate finance prevented an agreement.

The piece quotes Tuvalu's and Panama's ministers criticising the outcome and notes UN climate chief Simon Stiell plans to seek advice on reforming the process before next year's talks in Ethiopia. It is analysis and largely restates events already reported.
keyFacts: Piece is analysis by Laura Tingle
Bowen blamed red lines on fossil fuels and finance
Next talks are due in Ethiopia

leftOut.title: Negotiators say Saudi Arabia shaped outcome of failed COP31 talks
leftOut.summary:
Negotiators from Europe, small island states, Latin America, Asia and Africa told Reuters that Saudi officials had regular access and outsized influence at the COP31 talks, and led resistance to language on fossil fuels. Ireland's climate minister, speaking for the EU, said some oil states had hijacked the summit.

The Turkish presidency said no group received preferential treatment, Reuters reported. Saudi Arabia and Australia did not immediately comment. COP31 president Murat Kurum said there was no agreement and he would not put forward a new text.
keyFacts: Negotiators say Saudi officials had outsized influence
Turkish presidency denies preferential treatment
Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment

leftOut.title: Sahm rule creator says Australian recession is 'entirely possible'
leftOut.summary:
US economist Claudia Sahm, who devised a recession indicator based on rising unemployment, told the ABC it was possible Australia could cross the threshold within six to 12 months. Unemployment rose to 4.9 per cent in October, the highest since 2021.

The ABC reported a 2020 Reserve Bank research note set an Australian threshold of 0.75 percentage points, and the current reading is 0.6. Economist Saul Eslake said the rule could trigger in December if unemployment kept rising at its recent pace. The RBA says it is not forecasting a recession, and chief economist Sarah Hunter told a hearing in October indicators did not suggest one was near.
keyFacts: Unemployment rose to 4.9% in October
Current reading of 0.6 points is below the 0.75 threshold
RBA says it is not forecasting a recession

leftOut.title: Victorian Labor MPs question leadership change in final week of campaign
leftOut.summary:
Some Victorian Labor MPs are questioning whether replacing Jacinta Allan as premier was the right decision, as polling shows the party trailing before the 28 November state election, ABC analysis reported. A senior Labor figure described the campaign as a disaster, and a former minister said the same of the leadership change.

The ABC said Labor is losing votes to the Liberals, One Nation and the Greens after almost 12 years in government. It said the Coalition appears set to win with a primary vote under 40 per cent, and that Liberal leader Jess Wilson has not yet released costings, which she says are coming.
keyFacts: State election is on 28 November
Unnamed Labor figures criticise the campaign
Liberal costings not yet released

leftOut.title: Liberal preferences could decide Greens contests in inner Melbourne, ABC analysis says
leftOut.summary:
ABC elections analyst Casey Briggs wrote that Liberal how-to-vote cards could decide several inner-Melbourne contests between Labor and the Greens at Saturday's Victorian election. The Liberals have put Labor above the Greens in all Greens target seats except Brunswick and Footscray.

The Greens hold Brunswick, Melbourne and Richmond and hope to regain Prahran and win seats including Northcote, Pascoe Vale, Preston and Footscray. Briggs estimated the Liberal preference choice could move final margins by two to five points towards Labor. Most recent polls have the Greens at 14 to 15 per cent statewide.
keyFacts: Liberals preference Labor over Greens in most target seats
Greens hold Brunswick, Melbourne and Richmond
Estimated 2–5 point shift towards Labor

leftOut.title: Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar and UAE condemn Iran's attack on Bahrain
leftOut.summary:
Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Qatar condemned Iran's Saturday attack on Bahrain, ABC News (US) reported, with Qatar calling it a violation of sovereignty and Saudi Arabia holding Iran responsible. CBS News reported the United Arab Emirates also condemned the attack.

Accounts of casualties differed. ABC News (US) cited Bahrain as saying two people were injured and a fire broke out at a civilian industrial facility, while CBS said Bahrain had reported no injuries. Iran's Revolutionary Guards have said the strikes targeted US air defence sites in Bahrain.
keyFacts: Four Gulf states condemn the attack
Reports differ on whether anyone was injured
IRGC says it targeted US air defence sites

leftOut.title: Piastri finishes third behind Verstappen and Norris at Las Vegas Grand Prix
leftOut.summary:
Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix from pole, his 75th Formula One win, the ABC reported. Australian Oscar Piastri finished third behind McLaren teammate Lando Norris after starting 17th because of a 10-place grid penalty for a new engine component.

The ABC reported the race had 35 lead changes. New world champion Kimi Antonelli finished fourth after an energy deployment problem late in the race. Charles Leclerc dropped to 10th after a 10-second penalty for a collision with Lewis Hamilton, who finished seventh.
keyFacts: Verstappen wins from pole
Piastri third after starting 17th
Antonelli fourth after late technical problem

leftOut.title: HMAS Sydney 85th anniversary events scaled back in Carnarvon
leftOut.summary:
Commemorations in Carnarvon for the 85th anniversary of the loss of HMAS Sydney II were scaled back because the Shire of Carnarvon council has been dissolved, the Naval Association of Australia said, according to the ABC. The cruiser was sunk off the Western Australian coast in 1941 in a battle with the German raider Kormoran, with all 645 crew lost.

The association's state president, Ian Holthouse, proposed a military tourism trail linking Carnarvon and Geraldton. The shire's commissioner said the proposal had not been formally considered. About 100 people attended Carnarvon's evening service, where minister Hannah Beazley unveiled an upgraded memorial.
keyFacts: All 645 crew lost when HMAS Sydney II sank in 1941
Events reduced because the local council was dissolved
Upgraded memorial unveiled in Carnarvon

leftOut.title: Police officer shot and man found dead in linked incidents on Flinders Island
leftOut.summary:
A Tasmania Police officer was shot while on duty at Whitemark Police Station on Flinders Island at about 9.45pm on Saturday, police said, according to the ABC. Police said the officer was in a serious but stable condition, and Pulse Tasmania reported the officer was flown to Royal Hobart Hospital.

Police later found a man in his mid-20s dead in a nearby street with a gunshot wound and said they believe the incidents are linked, Pulse Tasmania reported. Police said the situation was contained. Premier Jeremy Rockliff said he had spoken with the police commissioner. A professional standards investigation is under way and police have asked for CCTV and dashcam footage.
keyFacts: Officer shot at Whitemark Police Station about 9.45pm Saturday
Man in his mid-20s found dead nearby
Police believe the two shootings are linked

leftOut.title: Man dies and two injured in three separate stabbings across Melbourne
leftOut.summary:
Victoria Police are investigating three separate stabbings in Melbourne on Saturday, the ABC reported. A 21-year-old man from Narre Warren died after an alleged stabbing on La Trobe Street in the CBD at about 8.40pm. Three people aged 17, 18 and 19 were arrested nearby and police are looking for a fourth man.

Earlier, a 24-year-old was seriously injured in what police allege was an unprovoked attack in Bourke Street Mall, and police named a man they are seeking. Police said the two CBD incidents are not believed to be linked. A 33-year-old man was allegedly stabbed in Broadmeadows; police said the people involved are believed to know each other.
keyFacts: 21-year-old man died after La Trobe Street stabbing
Three teenagers arrested over the fatal stabbing
Police say the CBD incidents are not believed to be linked

leftOut.title: Former NSW upper house MP Fred Nile dies aged 92
leftOut.summary:
Fred Nile, who served in the NSW Legislative Council for more than 40 years, has died aged 92, his family said in a statement on social media, according to the ABC. The family said he died on 21 November.

Nile led the Christian Democratic Party and lost his seat at the 2023 state election. He campaigned against abortion and same-sex marriage. Independent MP Alex Greenwich said the two disagreed often but worked together on some issues, the ABC reported. Former premiers Barry O'Farrell and Bob Carr also paid tribute.
keyFacts: Fred Nile died on 21 November aged 92
Served more than 40 years in the NSW Legislative Council
Tributes from Alex Greenwich, Barry O'Farrell and Bob Carr

leftOut.title: Wallabies beat Wales 29-26 to end four-match losing streak
leftOut.summary:
Australia beat Wales 29-26 in a Nations Championship rugby union Test in Cardiff on Saturday night local time, the ABC reported. The result ended a run of four consecutive Test losses for the Wallabies, according to the ABC's coverage of the match.

SBS News reported that centre Len Ikitau credited a renewed focus on defence for the team's performance in the second half. The Wallabies are scheduled to play Ireland next weekend, SBS News said. The win in Cardiff came on the Wallabies' end-of-year tour of Europe, with the Ireland match to follow.
keyFacts: Wallabies won 29-26 against Wales
Result ended a four-match losing streak
Australia plays Ireland next weekend

leftOut.title: Trump says he wants a 'permanent' deal stopping Iran from getting nuclear weapons
leftOut.summary:
US President Donald Trump told Fox News he intends to reach a permanent agreement that would prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons, Euronews reported. He said the aim was a deal that a future president could not undo.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has said diplomacy can still end the war, but that Iran's conditions include keeping its highly enriched uranium in the country, SBS News reported. Both positions have been stated in earlier reports, and no new talks were announced.
keyFacts: Trump said he wants a permanent deal on Iran's nuclear program
Araghchi says Iran still seeks diplomacy
No new negotiations announced

leftOut.title: Analysts forecast Coalition win as Victorian campaign enters final week
leftOut.summary:
Political analysts expect the Coalition to win majority government at Victoria's 28 November election, possibly on a scale similar to Jeff Kennett's 1992 victory, ABC News reported. Premier Ben Carroll and Opposition Leader Jess Wilson campaigned at early voting centres on Saturday.

A Redbridge poll for the Australian Financial Review projects a two-party preferred result of 57 per cent for the Coalition and 43 per cent for Labor, according to the ABC. Deakin University's Geoff Robinson said regional cities including Geelong, Ballarat and Bendigo were in play. Carroll declined to say whether he would hold his seat of Niddrie. These are forecasts, not results.
keyFacts: Election is on 28 November
Redbridge poll projects 57-43 to the Coalition
Analysts compare possible result with 1992

leftOut.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim to have shot down US drone over Strait of Hormuz
leftOut.summary:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said its aerospace forces shot down a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz, Middle East Eye reported, citing state broadcaster IRIB. The IRGC said it was the 58th MQ-9 destroyed by Iranian forces.

The claim has not been independently confirmed. Middle East Eye's report included no US response and no details of when the incident happened or of any wreckage. Iran and the US have been at war since 28 February, and Iran has made similar claims about US drones in recent days.
keyFacts: IRGC claims MQ-9 drone shot down over Hormuz
IRGC says it is the 58th such drone
No US confirmation or response reported

leftOut.title: Araghchi says Iran still seeks diplomacy as Trump calls Tehran's terms unacceptable
leftOut.summary:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran still hopes diplomacy can end its war with the United States and that messages are being exchanged through mediators, Ariana News reported, citing Reuters and Iranian media. He said Iran wants guarantees that Washington is serious and an agreement preventing further war.

Araghchi said keeping Iran's highly enriched uranium inside the country was a red line, though a fair solution was possible. At a White House news conference on Friday, US President Donald Trump said Iran wanted a deal but not one acceptable to him. Qatari and Iranian officials met earlier in the week.
keyFacts: Araghchi says messages passing through mediators
Uranium staying in Iran is a red line, he said
Trump says Iran's terms are unacceptable

leftOut.title: Trump says Jensen Huang should get a second chance at Nvidia
leftOut.summary:
US President Donald Trump said on Friday he would like to see former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang given a second chance, Al Jazeera reported. Huang resigned on 12 November over a scandal involving an alleged relationship with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.

Trump described Huang as a good man who had made bad decisions and said he wanted a big apology. Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones has said directors unanimously accepted the resignation and do not plan to reinstate Huang, according to Al Jazeera. Trump also said he had not lost confidence in Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.
keyFacts: Trump backs a return for Huang
Nvidia board says it will not reinstate him
Trump says he still has confidence in Lutnick

leftOut.title: Cricket Australia board backs Pat Cummins to stay as Test captain
leftOut.summary:
Cricket Australia's board unanimously supported Pat Cummins as captain for the three-Test series against New Zealand starting in Perth on 9 December, SBS News reported, citing AP. CA said it rejected any implication that his integrity had been compromised.

Cummins has denied knowing about the use of sandpaper on the 2018 tour of South Africa. Former teammates including Usman Khawaja and David Warner have given contradicting accounts, according to the report. Cummins said he supports an independent forum on the tour and would attend. CA chair David Boon and chief executive Todd Greenberg met him in Sydney on Friday.
keyFacts: Board support was unanimous, CA says
Series against New Zealand starts 9 December
Cummins denies prior knowledge of ball tampering

leftOut.title: Man in critical condition after stabbing in Melbourne CBD
leftOut.summary:
A 24-year-old man was taken to the Royal Melbourne Hospital in a critical condition after being stabbed on Bourke Street near Elizabeth Street at about 2.30pm on Saturday, ABC News reported, citing Victoria Police.

Police said the two men were not believed to know each other. The alleged offender fled along Elizabeth Street towards Little Bourke Street, according to police, who are making inquiries. No arrest had been reported. Police asked anyone with information or footage to contact Crime Stoppers.
keyFacts: 24-year-old in critical condition
Police say the men did not know each other
No arrest reported

leftOut.title: Boy, 11, dies after being hit by ute on South Western Highway in Kirup
leftOut.summary:
An 11-year-old boy died after being hit by a ute while crossing the South Western Highway in Kirup, about 220 kilometres south of Perth, at about 5.50pm on Friday, ABC News reported, citing WA Police. He was flown to Perth Children's Hospital and later died.

The 25-year-old driver was not injured and is assisting police. A local resident told the ABC that residents had asked Main Roads to lower the town's 60km/h speed limit to 40km/h. Main Roads had been contacted for comment, the ABC said.
keyFacts: Boy hit while crossing highway on Friday evening
Driver, 25, assisting police
Residents had sought a lower speed limit

leftOut.title: Former Brazilian president Bolsonaro hospitalised with intestinal obstruction
leftOut.summary:
Former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, 71, was admitted to hospital in Brasilia on Friday with abdominal pain and distension, according to a hospital statement reported by MercoPress. Reuters reported his doctor said tests showed a partial intestinal obstruction.

His son, Senator Carlos Bolsonaro, said on social media that his father was receiving pain relief and doctors were trying to treat the condition without surgery, Reuters reported. Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after his 2022 election loss and is under humanitarian house arrest. He has had several operations since being stabbed in 2018.
keyFacts: Admitted to a Brasilia hospital on Friday
Doctor reports partial intestinal obstruction
Bolsonaro is under humanitarian house arrest

leftOut.title: Trump says Canada feels emboldened but he wants a fair trade deal
leftOut.summary:
US President Donald Trump said at a White House news conference on Friday that Canada was feeling emboldened but that the US was working on a fair trade deal, The Canadian Press reported. He said he had spoken with Prime Minister Mark Carney at the Asia-Pacific summit in Shenzhen.

Trump repeated claims that Canada had taken advantage of the US, according to the report. US-Canada trade talks broke down in August, and 50 per cent tariffs apply to some Canadian goods. Carney said on Wednesday a very good arrangement was possible but Canada was pursuing other trade deals.
keyFacts: Trump says he wants a fair deal with Canada
Talks broke down in August
Carney says Canada is pursuing other deals

leftOut.title: Indian minister responds to Rahul Gandhi's 'compromised PM' post
leftOut.summary:
Indian Congress leader Rahul Gandhi posted a picture of the three-way meeting between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, writing that a "compromised PM" could never sit at that table, in remarks seen as aimed at Prime Minister Narendra Modi, The Hans India reported.

Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said Gandhi should not make statements against India, according to the report, and the Deccan Herald reported that he questioned Congress over the 1962 war with China. BJP media convenor Ashish Usha Agarwal said a US-China-Russia meeting does not define India's global standing, citing its role in BRICS, the Quad and the G20.
keyFacts: Gandhi posted about Trump-Xi-Putin meeting
Rijiju said Gandhi should not speak against India
BJP cites India's role in BRICS, Quad and G20

leftOut.title: First Nations youth plan Canada-wide day of action against major projects bill
leftOut.summary:
First Nations youth in Canada plan a national day of action on 8 December against federal legislation to fast-track major projects, The Canadian Press reported. The date coincides with an Assembly of First Nations meeting in Ottawa.

The 243-page bill would shorten reviews and create national interest zones for pre-approval, according to the report. Organisers from Attawapiskat First Nation said it would override Indigenous rights and fail to protect the environment, and the Chiefs of Ontario support the action. Prime Minister Mark Carney has said Indigenous participation is central to his agenda.
keyFacts: Day of action set for 8 December
Bill would shorten project reviews
Chiefs of Ontario back the protest

leftOut.title: Kim Jong Un inspects factories after Trump leaves Asia without meeting
leftOut.summary:
North Korean state media said Kim Jong Un inspected factories producing school equipment on Friday, AFP reported via Arab News. The visit came after US President Donald Trump left Asia without meeting Kim.

Trump said he had been too busy and that he and Kim would meet at some point, according to AFP. Pyongyang has not commented on Trump's remarks. Trump has said Kim would like to meet him, which North Korea has not confirmed. The two leaders met three times during Trump's first term.
keyFacts: KCNA says Kim inspected school equipment factories
Trump left Asia without meeting Kim
Pyongyang has not responded to Trump's comments

leftOut.title: Man charged with terrorism offences after raids in Sydney's south-west
leftOut.summary:
A 35-year-old man was charged with making a document connected with terrorism and using a carriage service to possess violent extremist material after raids in Sydney's south-west on Friday, ABC News reported. Police allege the material related to religiously motivated extremism, including Islamic State.

The man was arrested at an Ingleburn home and refused bail, according to the ABC. A 34-year-old man arrested in Campbelltown was expected to be charged with hindering police, and a 33-year-old arrested at Wolli Creek was expected to face firearms charges. Police searched several properties and seized items.

Police allege Islamic State-related material
Two other men arrested in the raids

leftOut.title: Trump says nuclear arms limits with China and Russia will be hard to achieve
leftOut.summary:
US President Donald Trump said after talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin that an agreement to limit nuclear weapons would be very hard to achieve but he would keep working on it, Reuters reported. He spoke to Reuters by phone on his flight back from the three-way meeting in China.

Trump said Xi agreed with the concept, according to Reuters, while China has been reluctant to join arms control talks. Reuters cited estimates of about 410 Chinese, 3,708 US and 5,420 Russian warheads. The leaders' joint statement said a nuclear war cannot be won and committed them to dialogue on reducing nuclear risks.
keyFacts: Trump spoke to Reuters after the Shenzhen meeting
He said Xi agrees with the concept
Joint statement commits to dialogue on nuclear risks

leftOut.title: China again urges Japan to correct its statements on Taiwan
leftOut.summary:
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun on Friday repeated Beijing's call for Japan to correct its words and actions on Taiwan, Anadolu Agency reported. He said Japan must honour four political documents between the two countries.

The day before, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said Japan's position was unchanged from the 1972 joint communique and called for stable ties with Beijing, according to Anadolu, citing Kyodo. She spoke before leaving the APEC summit in Shenzhen. Relations have been strained since Takaichi's November 2025 comments about a possible Japanese military response to a Chinese attack on Taiwan.
keyFacts: Beijing repeats demand on Japan's Taiwan stance
Takaichi says Japan's position is unchanged
Dispute dates from November 2025 remarks

leftOut.title: Arizona town issues business licence for planned immigration detention centre
leftOut.summary:
The town of Marana, Arizona, issued a business licence to Management & Training Corporation to run an immigration detention centre in a former state prison, AP reported, citing Arizona Luminaria. A town spokesman said there were no grounds under town code to refuse it.

Arizona Public Media said the town had twice asked the company why sexual abuse allegations were missing from a 2023 audit of the site. The company said one allegation was mistakenly omitted and the others were classed as unfounded. ICE awarded the company a $US335 million contract in September. Opponents said they would keep opposing the facility.
keyFacts: Licence dated 18 November, runs to November 2027
ICE contract worth $US335 million
Town says code gave no grounds to refuse

leftOut.title: ABC News staff reportedly placed on leave over Trump Jr business story
leftOut.summary:
ABC News reportedly placed two employees on paid leave after an internal review of an October story about Donald Trump Jr.'s business dealings, according to reports citing The Wall Street Journal and Status. An ABC spokesperson said no one's employment status had changed, Fox News and ComingSoon.net reported.

The story was removed a day after publication in October and restored with corrections, according to the reports. It had said venture firm 1789 Capital took a major stake in defence company Anduril. ABC later clarified that the firm invested $US50 million as part of a larger round. A 1789 spokesperson told Fox News the firm was considering legal action.

ABC says no employment status has changed
Story was corrected after publication in October

leftOut.title: Students protest across Europe over cost of living, war and education cuts
leftOut.summary:
Thousands of young people protested in cities across Europe and the UK on Friday, ABC News reported. The organising Youth Strike coalition said it planned demonstrations in about 400 cities in countries including Germany, France, Italy, Spain and the UK.

Issues raised included the cost of living, climate, education budgets, housing, defence spending and compulsory military service, according to the ABC. The Berlin rally was among the largest. In Rome a small group threw firecrackers, but events were mostly peaceful, and London police kept a rival group apart from students. Organisers said larger Paris protests were planned for the weekend.
keyFacts: Organisers planned protests in about 400 cities
Berlin rally among the largest
Mostly peaceful, according to the ABC

leftOut.title: Sydney Marathon winner Jepchirchir disqualified and banned for three years
leftOut.summary:
Kenya's Peres Jepchirchir has been disqualified from the Sydney Marathon and suspended for three years after testing positive for EPO in a sample taken before her August win, AAP reported. She has also been banned for life from the world's major marathons.

Irine Cheptai is set to be named champion, according to AAP. The Athletics Integrity Unit also announced bans for two other Kenyan runners. Race director Wayne Larden said the case showed the testing system worked. AIU head Brett Clothier said there was still a long way to go, and that Kenya's government had committed to strengthening its anti-doping agency.

Three-year suspension and life ban from majors
Irine Cheptai set to be elevated to winner

leftOut.title: Three 16-year-olds charged with murder over Loganholme pub shooting
leftOut.summary:
Queensland police have charged three 16-year-old boys with murder, attempted murder and arson over a drive-by shooting at a pub at Loganholme, south of Brisbane, on 24 October, AAP reported. Five people were taken into custody after search warrants were executed on Thursday.

Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau was shot during a boxing event and died five days later, according to AAP. Three men were also injured. Detective Inspector Ian Galpin said two people were in the car from which shots were fired, and gang involvement had not been ruled out. The three were due in Brisbane Children's Court on Friday.

Shooting occurred on 24 October
Police have not ruled out gang involvement

leftOut.title: Bukele expected to register for a third term as El Salvador's president
leftOut.summary:
El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele was expected to register as a candidate for a third term before Thursday's deadline, Al Jazeera reported, citing Reuters. The election is set for 28 February 2027. A 2025 constitutional change allowed a third term and extended terms from five to six years.

Rights groups say more than 1 per cent of the population has been detained under a state of emergency with limited due process, according to the report. The government says gangs have been largely dismantled. Rival candidates include Maytee Iraheta of ARENA and Rafael Aguirre of the FMLN. Registration had not been confirmed in the report.

2025 amendment allowed a third term
Registration not yet confirmed

leftOut.title: Rohingya community in Australia reacts to ICJ genocide ruling
leftOut.summary:
Members of Australia's Rohingya community welcomed the International Court of Justice ruling that Myanmar committed genocide, AAP reported. Asma Nayim Ullah, who arrived in Australia by boat as a child, told AAP that many people's first word on hearing the news was "finally".

AAP said about 5,000 Rohingya live in Australia. Her family stayed up on Thursday night to watch the ruling from The Hague, according to the report. AAP cited estimates that about 750,000 Rohingya have fled to Bangladesh since August 2017. The article did not include a response from the Australian government.

Community members watched the ruling overnight
No Australian government response reported

leftOut.title: Ministers say Treasury and RBA are not forecasting a recession
leftOut.summary:
Workplace Relations Minister Amanda Rishworth said on Friday the Reserve Bank and Treasury were not forecasting a recession and she had no reason to dispute that, the ABC reported. Health Minister Mark Butler said the coming mid-year budget update would aim to ease inflation pressure without a "slash and burn" approach.

Shadow Treasurer Tim Wilson accused the government of pursuing policies that add to inflation, and Deputy Liberal Leader Jane Hume called for action to restore business confidence, according to the ABC. The comments followed Thursday's figures showing unemployment rose to 4.9 per cent in October.

Butler rules out 'slash and burn' in MYEFO

leftOut.title: Gulf states seek partial deal as concerns grow of renewed US-Iran war
leftOut.summary:
Concerns are growing about a return to full-scale conflict between the US and Iran, AAP reported. At a White House news conference on Friday, President Donald Trump said Iran wanted a deal but not one acceptable to him, and repeated that Iran would never have a nuclear weapon.

An unnamed Middle Eastern diplomat said Gulf Arab states were seeking a partial arrangement that would ease shipping limits in the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for limited sanctions relief for Iran, AAP said. Iran has widened attacks on Gulf neighbours in the past week after a US strike on Qeshm Island. US forces continue a naval blockade of Iranian ports.

An unnamed diplomat said Gulf states seek a partial deal
A US naval blockade of Iranian ports continues

leftOut.title: Carroll says Victorian election is winnable as poll shows Labor behind
leftOut.summary:
Victorian Premier Ben Carroll said every election is winnable ahead of the 28 November state poll, AAP reported. Carroll took over five months ago after a leadership spill that led to Jacinta Allan's resignation.

A RedBridge Group and Accent Research survey published in the Australian Financial Review put the Coalition on 31 per cent, Labor on 23 per cent and One Nation on 22 per cent, AAP said. Carroll is defending his seat of Niddrie, which he held in 2022 on a 6.7 per cent margin. He acknowledged Labor faced a difficult contest but said he would keep campaigning across the state.

leftOut.title: Kensington Palace announces documentary on Princess of Wales's cancer treatment
leftOut.summary:
Kensington Palace has announced a documentary, Heal, about the Princess of Wales's experience of cancer, the ABC reported, citing AFP and Reuters. It will air on the BBC on 29 November and on Channel Nine in Australia on 1 December.

The palace said the film follows her on the Three Peaks Challenge, which she completed in June, and features others facing serious illness. Catherine announced in March 2024 that she was being treated for cancer and said in January 2025 that she was in remission. The palace said funds from distribution will go to the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity.

Proceeds go to the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity

leftOut.title: ABC analysis examines Albanese's diplomacy after APEC and Quad trip
leftOut.summary:
An ABC analysis by chief digital political correspondent Clare Armstrong reviews Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's 11-day trip, which included the Quad meeting in Manila and APEC in China. It notes that Albanese told Russian President Vladimir Putin at APEC to end the war in Ukraine, and that US President Donald Trump met Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.

Armstrong argues Albanese has grown more comfortable managing relations with Beijing and Washington but has limited influence over decisions made by the three leaders. The piece is analysis and does not report new events beyond those already covered.
